title: Rent Payment
bodyText: Tenant shall pay Landlord monthly rent of {{monthly_rent}} (Monthly Rent) in advance on the due date specified in this Lease, without demand, deduction, or setoff, except as permitted by applicable law. If the due date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, rent is due on the next business day.

State-driven, not uniform. CROSS-STATE FLAG raised from the CA pass 2026-09-19: this row says rent is payable 'without demand, DEDUCTION, OR SETOFF'. CA had to drop that language because Civ. Code s1942 gives tenants a statutory repair-and-deduct right a lease cannot waive (see rent-payment-ca). Most states have some repair-and-deduct or rent-withholding statute, so the same wording may purport to waive a non-waivable right in several of the other eight. NOT adjudicated here - each state's statute must be read before changing their text. Flagged for the cross-state review. CROSS-STATE FLAG RESOLVED BY DRAFTING 2026-09-19. The flag: 'without demand, deduction, or setoff' can purport to waive a statutory right. Adjudicated from the library's OWN verified per-state findings rather than new statute reading - ND (s47-16-13) and SD (s43-32-9) have statutory REPAIR-AND-DEDUCT; MN has court-administered RENT ESCROW under s504B.385 whose rights 'may not be waived or modified' (s504B.465); OH has escrow under s5321.07. CO, WY, KS and NE have neither repair-and-deduct nor escrow, so the language was already safe there. Fix applied: the words 'except as permitted by applicable law' added, which is protective in all eight states and required no state-specific rewrite - the same approach that let addendum-precedence absorb its CA override. This clause's 'in advance on the due date specified in this Lease' is the contract to the contrary that displaces it, so the clause is correct and no edit is proposed - but the choice is only made if the lease actually states a due date. If the builder ever lets the due date render blank for a South Dakota lease, the statutory default takes over and rent is payable at the END of the period. Flagged as a builder constraint, not a clause defect. No change to the shared text. | NM: Applies as written. 'Except as permitted by applicable law' preserves the tenant's statutory offsets, such as payments to a utility for service the landlord failed to pay for (N.Y. Real Prop. Rule 15: written section-open. | AZ: Applies as written. A.R.S. §33-1314(C): rent payable without demand or notice at the time and place agreed. No payment-timing statute conflicts. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | AZ (retro 2026-10-03, SOP 1.32 rule 79, basis): every A.R.S. section cited in this row's AZ note re-read section-open 2026-10-03 in Taylor's built-in browser from azleg.gov (official compilation; each section fetched twice, copies matched, heading number checked; saved to the AZ retro source folder with a SHA-256 match); each cited subdivision says what the note says, and each qualifier sits on the sentence the statute attaches it to. | WI: Applies as written. Act 247), the Wisconsin Administrative Code (current through Register September 2026, No. 849) and the Wisconsin Constitution, loaded in the built-in browser from docs.legis.wisconsin.gov, saved and hash-matched (WI log §1). Rent is payable without demand or notice at the agreed time and place (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-310(c)); 'except as permitted by applicable law' preserves the tenant's essential-services procure-and-deduct remedy (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-630(a)(1)); South Carolina has no repair-and-deduct right (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-630(c)). Basis (rule 79, SC retro 1.50): 27-40-310, 27-40-630 read section-open 2026-10-04 in the built-in browser from the official South Carolina Code of Laws on scstatehouse.gov (site current through the 2025 session; each section saved and SHA-256 matched to the browser, SC retro 1.50 sources); the cited subdivisions and every qualifier checked against the text. | WA: Applies as written. The cited sections apply where the URLTA is in effect; elsewhere the clause works as a contract term. Read section-open 2026-10-04/05 from the saved, hash-matched corpus of the whole Kentucky Revised Statutes (apps.legislature.ky.gov, each section's PDF with its Effective date and History line; the site states it includes enactments through the 2026 Regular Session, database updated 10/04/2026) and the Kentucky Constitution (KY log §1). Rule 15: written section-open. | WV: Tagged as written (tag-first screen, rules 26-28, WV log §2.1): No West Virginia statute sets when or where rent is paid or a weekend or holiday rule; a summary-relief petition may rest on the tenant being 'in arrears in the payment of rent' with no demand first (W. Va. Code § 55-3A-1(a)(3); `edu-no-nonpayment-notice-wv`), which 'without demand' matches. West Virginia gives no repair-and-deduct right, but unless the lease otherwise provides it reduces rent after a casualty the tenant did not cause (W. Va. Code § 37-6-28; this library's lease provides its own measure in `casualty-wv`), and a tenant facing a summary-relief petition for arrears may defend on the landlord's breach of a material covenant on which the duty to pay rent depends (W. Va. Code § 55-3A-3(b)); 'except as permitted by applicable law' keeps both (WV battery a-repair-deduct-r2 (tenant repair-and-deduct, rent withholding, rent escrow or abatement (rerun of repair-deduct)): 27 hits, control 0; known positives passed (2 real sections, 2 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205); grace periods: `edu-no-rent-grace-period-wv`. title: Late Fee
bodyText: If Tenant fails to pay Monthly Rent in full within {{late_fee_grace_days}} days after it is due, a late fee of {{late_fee_amount}} will be assessed. Acceptance of a late payment does not waive Landlord's right to require full payment of Rent on the date it is due or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease.
notes: CO added - verified this session (statute walk + full-library audit; content itself EDITED this session WY added 2026-08-21 (full-library cross-check pass): generic mechanics, no CO-specific statutory language or number, confirmed no conflict with WY findings from this project. | NE extended (session 6): the non-waiver sentence isn't prohibited in Nebraska the way the exculpation clauses were in Kansas — it's just insufficient on its own to satisfy §76-1433's after-the-breach requirement. No override needed; see edu-late-rent-reservation-fix-ne for the landlord-facing explanation of why lease text alone doesn't solve this and what actually does. | NE REMOVED 2026-08-31 (NE re-audit) — superseded by late-fee-ne. §76-1433 read verbatim from nebraskalegislature.gov. This clause's phrase 'or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease' is UNQUALIFIED and therefore purports to preserve termination for the very breach §76-1433 says is waived. §5a.1 JUDGMENT — STATE-DRIVEN, not uniform: the fix was deliberately NOT propagated to CO, WY, or MN. A non-waiver clause preserving termination after accepting late rent is genuinely valuable where contract can preserve it, and none of those three has been shown to carry Nebraska's express statutory timing rule. Narrowing all four states would surrender real protection in three of them to solve a problem only one has. Structurally consistent with Kansas, which also took its own late-fee-ks override. | ND ADDED 2026-09-06 (ND re-audit, exhaustive generic-clause audit prompted by the checklist-to-CSV reconciliation screen). LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK: North Dakota has NO enumerated prohibited-lease-provisions statute (confirmed this session -- § 47-16-02 is a maximum-term cap, and § 47-16-13.3 supplies only case-by-case unconscionability). The exculpation exposure that forced fixes to this clause family in KS and NE therefore does not arise for ND, same reasoning as the WY addendum. 5a.1 JUDGMENT: UNIFORM -- states field changed, clause TEXT unchanged, no re-review owed on existing tags. State-driven, not uniform. SD sets no statutory late-fee cap and no mandatory grace period, so the landlord-set fields create no conflict. The non-waiver sentence is also safe: SD has no waiver-by-acceptance rule of the NE S76-1433 / KS type. MATERIAL GAP CLOSED: SD previously had NO late-fee clause of any kind, and because SD law leaves late fees entirely to the lease, an SD lease generated without this clause could not charge a late fee at all. | FL: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). No late-fee cap or grace-period statute in Fla. Stat. ch. 83 Part II (full read, §§83.40-83.684); boundary: Part II only, other titles not searched. Local fee caps are preempted by Fla. Stat. §83.425 ('fees charged by the landlord'; s. 1, ch. 2023-314). The amount stays subject to §83.45 (unconscionability). The clause does not designate the fee as rent; under §83.43(12) only payments 'designated as rent in a written rental agreement' are rent. Library default (Taylor, NJ 2026-09-26): fees are not labeled rent. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | FL: FL research pass 2026-09-26 (advanced research, once; report in the conversation). Trial-level Florida decisions (secondary) treat a 3-day notice that demands a late charge not designated as rent as defective; the library's no-'additional rent' posture avoids that. No statewide late-fee cap found (not a full-text verified absence). | ND 2026-09-28: the LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK above is withdrawn as to any clause disclaiming liability for the landlord's own violation of law. North Dakota does have enumerated bans outside its landlord-tenant title: N.D.C.C. §§9-08-02 (exculpation), 9-08-03 (penalties), 9-08-04 (liquidated damages) and 9-08-05 (restricting enforcement). See edu-prohibited-lease-terms-nd. | ND (added 2026-09-28): the absence of a cap is confirmed statewide, not only in ch. 47-16 (edu-no-late-fee-cap-nd). title: Returned Checks / Dishonored Payments
bodyText: If any payment of Rent is returned for insufficient funds or otherwise fails, Landlord may require that the payment be replaced by a cashier's check, certified check, or money order, and may charge Tenant a fee associated with the failed payment, not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law. If more than two of Tenant's payments during any 12-month period are returned for insufficient funds, Landlord may require all future payments of Rent be made by cashier's check, certified check, or money order.

No conflict with this clause's generic mechanics; the actual NSF cap lives in Title 6 general banking law (§6-08-16), not landlord-tenant law, and isn't restated here. | KS CHECKED 2026-08-30 (v59 canvass): K.S.A. 60-2610(g) caps the service charge on a dishonored check at $30. title: Application of Payments
bodyText: Each payment Tenant makes will be applied first to the Monthly Rent due for the current or oldest unpaid rental period, and only then to any other fees, charges, or amounts due under this Lease, unless Tenant directs otherwise in writing for a particular payment or applicable law requires otherwise. Nothing in this provision limits any statutory right Tenant may have to cure nonpayment of Rent.

title: Late Fee Limit
bodyText: Any late fee charged under this Lease is agreed to by Landlord and Tenant in writing by this Lease, will be imposed only as stated in this Lease's late fee provision, and will not exceed 8% of the overdue Rent payment. If Landlord receives housing assistance payments for the property under a contract with a federal, state, or local government, any late fee will be calculated and assessed only on the portion of Rent payable by Tenant.
notes: MN verified (Minnesota session, statute walk): confirmed against Minn. Stat. § 504B.177(a) directly from revisor.mn.gov. Cap is 8% of the overdue rent payment; written agreement required specifying when the fee applies. Text as originally tagged was already accurate. | RETRO CHECKS (SOP 1.19), 2026-10-02 -- a scalpel, not a re-audit: MN added (retro checks, SOP 1.19, 2026-10-02 -- a scalpel, not a re-audit). Official Minnesota Revisor full-text search of the 2025 Minnesota Statutes (api.revisor.mn.gov search service, exact-phrase with word variants, nonsense control term run and returning 0), every landlord-relevant hit read section-open on revisor.mn.gov. *** RESTORED. ITEM 19 / RULE 78 FINDING, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE NEW JERSEY CASE THE RULE WAS WRITTEN FROM. *** The 2026-09-29 three-bucket scrub switched this row off and created NO education counterpart, so Minnesota was left with no statement of Minn. Stat. Sec. 504B.177 anywhere -- not in a clause, not in education. Every other capped state carries one (CO `edu-late-fee-limit-co`, UT `edu-late-fee-cap-ut`, NV, NJ, TN, VA, NC, TX, KS, NE, AZ all have a clause or an education row). The shared `late-fee` row supplies a free-text {{late_fee_amount}}, so after the scrub a Minnesota landlord could enter any figure with nothing in the lease or the library saying 8%. The scrub's own verdict table does not list this row at all, although it covers 'all 27 lease clauses written for this state alone' -- so the switch-off was never given a recorded verdict. WHY IT GOES BACK IN THE CLAUSE RATHER THAN EDUCATION (item 19's test): Sec. 504B.177, read section-open in full, has three limbs and two of them are conditions a number check cannot catch. (a) No late fee at all is permitted 'unless the tenant and landlord have agreed in writing that a late fee may be imposed', and 'the agreement must specify when the late fee will be imposed' -- the lease IS that writing, so the condition can only live in the lease; the {{late_fee_grace_days}} mechanic in `late-fee` supplies the 'when'. (c) A landlord under a housing assistance payments contract (42 U.S.C. 1437f or 1485, or any programme where the landlord takes rent from the tenant and a payment from government) must calculate and assess the fee ONLY on the tenant's portion of rent -- a change to the base, keyed to a tenant class, which no cap check would detect. This is the direct analogue of the N.J.S.A. 2A:42-6.1 senior and benefit-recipient grace period that New Jersey restored to `late-fee-nj`. The 8% ceiling itself is the limb a builder check could catch (backlog M.13) and is stated here anyway because the row already existed. ALSO IN THE STATUTE, NOT PUT IN THE CLAUSE: (b) where a federal statute, regulation or handbook permitting late fees for a federally subsidised tenancy conflicts with (a), the landlord may publish and implement a federally compliant fee schedule -- an override that operates outside the lease; and the definitional point that 'due date' excludes an earlier date by which paying earns the tenant a discount. Both recorded here, not drafted, because neither is a term the lease should state. A late fee is expressly 'not considered to be either interest or liquidated damages'. Currency: Sec. 504B.177 amended 2024 c 118 s 13; history line read. Rule 76: the decision to restore to the clause rather than education is a drafting judgment, made here and recorded. Sync 2026-10-02 (Claude Code): topic_key set to `late-fee-limit`, since this is a companion clause to the shared `late-fee`, not a replacement for it (one subject per row; a companion keeps its own key).

title: Late Fee (Tennessee URLTA Counties)
bodyText: If any Rent is not paid in full by the end of the grace period, Tenant will owe a late fee of {{late_fee_amount}}. The grace period is five days, beginning on and counting the day the Rent is due. If the last day of the grace period falls on a Sunday or on a legal holiday under Tenn. Code Ann. § 15-1-101 (which includes days set apart for county, state or national elections), no late fee will be charged if the Rent is paid on the next business day. Any charge or fee for the late payment of Rent, however described, will not exceed ten percent (10%) of the amount of Rent past due. Landlord's acceptance of a late payment does not change the due date of any later payment.

title: Late Fee
bodyText: If Tenant does not pay Monthly Rent in full within {{late_fee_grace_days}} days after it is due, Tenant will owe a late charge of {{late_fee_amount}}, but never more than the lesser of 10 percent of the periodic Rent or 10 percent of the remaining balance due and owed by Tenant. Landlord will not charge a late charge (a) after a foreclosure sale, until Tenant has received any written notice Virginia law requires of where to pay Rent, or (b) on rent covered by a payment plan that Virginia law requires Landlord to offer, while Tenant makes the plan payments on time. Landlord's acceptance of a late payment does not change the due date of any later payment.
notes: VA: VA-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. Read section-open 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser on the official Code of Virginia (law.lis.virginia.gov; Title 55.1 Chapter 12 read whole from the vacodefull page, which prints the 2026-session amendments and every delayed-effective version with its history line); 2024-2026 amending chapters read in enrolled text on lis.virginia.gov with their effective-date clauses (VA log §1). Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1204(E) (history ends 2026, cc. 722, 723; the late-charge subsection itself unchanged by the 2024-2026 acts, 2026 cc. 722/723/1066 read): a landlord may not charge for late payment 'unless such charge is provided for in the written rental agreement', and no late charge may exceed 'the lesser of 10 percent of the periodic rent or 10 percent of the remaining balance due and owed by the tenant'. Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1204(C)(4)-(5): where no written lease is offered, rent is late if not paid by the fifth. Late charges are recoverable from the deposit only as 'reasonable charges for late payment of rent specified in the rental agreement' (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1226(A)). No statutory grace period for a written lease; the grace days are contractual. The shared late-fee row was not tagged: it has no cap wording. The shared non-waiver sentence was replaced with the neutral due-date sentence because Virginia's partial-payment rule is a notice rule (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1250(A), acceptance with reservation by written notice, may be in the termination notice), not something a lease sentence can satisfy (edu-acceptance-of-rent-with-reservation-va). Separate caps: submetered/RUBS utility bills late charge up to $5, not less than 15 days after the bill (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1212(C)-(D)); from 2027-07-01 no additional late fees during a statutory payment plan (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1245(G) as amended by 2026 Acts ch. 1105). DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED (instruction 21, kickoff): the pre-project text ('Any late fee ... will not exceed the lesser of 10% of the periodic Rent or 10% of the remaining balance due under this Lease') had the cap right but said 'remaining balance due under this Lease' (the statute says 'due and owed by the tenant', which a court could read as the arrearage, not the rest of the term's rent), carried no fee amount or grace period, and omitted the written-lease precondition; UNVERIFIED and inactive, now verified and active, superseding the shared late-fee row. | VA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's fee (it must be in the written lease to be charged); the restated 10% cap is in edu-late-fee-rules-va. | VA: Retro check 2026-10-04 (SOP 1.55), fix 4 (rule 78 with rule 47). The 10-percent-of-periodic-Rent limb is a number the builder can check (backlog M.13), but the 'remaining balance due and owed' limb depends on what is unpaid when the charge is assessed, so no build-time check can catch it; the clause carries it again in the statute's words (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1204(E), both versions). ADDED (conditions the pre-scrub text never carried, rule 78): no late charge after a foreclosure until the successor owner gives written notice of where to pay, where the lease designates no managing agent (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1237); and, from 2027-07-01, no further late fees on the arrearage in a statutory payment plan while the tenant pays on time (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1245(G), version effective July 1, 2027, landlords with more than four units; 2026 Acts ch. 1105). Both turn on facts a number check cannot see. The sentences bind only where the law applies, so the clause stays lawful for every landlord. title: Late Fee
bodyText: If any payment of Monthly Rent is five or more calendar days late, counting from the day after it was due, Tenant will owe one late fee of {{late_fee_amount}} for that late payment. If Tenant's Rent is subsidized by a government housing program, the late fee will not exceed the greater of $15.00 or five percent (5%) of Tenant's share of the monthly Rent. Acceptance of a late payment does not waive Landlord's right to require full payment of Rent on the date it is due or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease.
notes: NC: Read section-open 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser from the official General Statutes on ncleg.gov (Chapter 42 read whole on the chapter page, which prints each section's history line; the latest amendments in those history lines are S.L. 2025-45, 2025-52 and 2025-54; all 61 session laws of 2026 (S.L. 2026-1 to 2026-61) screened for Chapter 42 amendments, none found). DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED (instruction 21; NC log §5). Prior text (UNVERIFIED, inactive, from an old nationwide pass): 'Any late fee assessed under this Lease will not exceed the greater of $15.00 or 5% of Monthly Rent, and no late fee will be assessed until at least 5 days after Rent is due, as required by North Carolina law.' Right: the $15/5% cap and the five-day threshold. Missing or wrong: the weekly-rent cap; 'calendar' days counted from the day after the due date (added by S.L. 2024-47, s. 8, effective 2024-09-09, stated as clarifying); once per late payment; no deduction from a later payment to create a default; no late fee for unpaid landlord-billed water or sewer; subsidized rent computed on the tenant's share. Now supersedes the shared `late-fee` for NC (not tagged: its free grace-days and amount fields could produce a void fee). topic_key normalised from `late-fee-limit-nc` to `late-fee`. Controlling text: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(a)(1)-(2), (b), (d), (h)(4) ('Any provision of a residential rental agreement contrary to the provisions of this section is against the public policy of this State and therefore void and unenforceable') and (h)(5) (subsidized rent) (history ends 2025-54, s. 12.4(a)). The last sentence is the shared late-fee non-waiver sentence; partial-payment non-waiver is a separate opt-in (partial-payment-nonwaiver-nc). | NC: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's fee and its five-day trigger; the restated cap, subsidy, once-only and utility rules are in edu-late-and-eviction-fees-nc. | NC: RETRO 2026-10-02 (SOP 1.21, fix 22; rules 78 and 47): the 2026-09-29 scrub trim was screened for statutory conditions a number check cannot catch. RESTORED two: (1) 'one late fee ... for that late payment' (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(b): 'may be imposed only one time for each late rental payment'), so a landlord cannot fill the amount field with a daily or repeating charge; (2) the subsidized-tenant cap (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(h)(5): any fee 'shall be calculated on the tenant's share of the contract rent only'), because the builder's cap check (backlog M.13) compares the figure with the full Monthly Rent and cannot see a subsidy. NOT RESTORED, with reasons: the $15-or-5% cap for unsubsidized rent is a number check (M.13); the weekly-rent cap (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(a)(2)) cannot arise because the clause applies only to Monthly Rent; the no-deduction rule (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(b)) is already secured by `application-of-payments`, which applies every payment to the oldest unpaid Rent before any fee; the water and sewer rule (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(d)) cannot arise because the clause charges a late fee only on Monthly Rent, and `utility-billing-nc` repeats it. Why it matters: a fee a void term provides for is not just unenforceable (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(h)(4)); collecting a charge the collector is not 'legally entitled to' is a debt-collection violation carrying a $500 to $4,000 civil penalty per violation if the landlord is a 'debt collector' (N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 75-50(3), 75-55(2), 75-56(b); case law on landlords not read). Required-content search (rule 78): no North Carolina statute requires late-fee text in the lease beyond the parties' agreement (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-46(a): 'the parties may agree to a late fee'), and no other text the scrub removed is required in the lease itself (rule 46 and rule 48 batteries, battery log). title: Late Fee Limit
bodyText: Any late fee assessed under this Lease will not exceed 4% of one month's Rent, and no late fee will be assessed until at least 15 days after Rent is due. Landlord will provide Tenant written notice of this late fee policy at signing, as required by Maine law.

title: Late Fee
bodyText: If any portion of the Rent for a rental period remains unpaid two full days after the date it was originally due, and also remains unpaid {{late_fee_grace_days}} days after that date, Tenant will pay a late fee consisting of an initial fee of {{late_fee_amount}}[, plus a daily fee of {{late_fee_daily_amount}} for each additional day any portion of that Rent remains unpaid]. The initial fee and any daily fees for a rental period are a single late fee, and their total for that rental period will not exceed 12% of the Rent for that rental period if the property is in a structure containing four or fewer dwelling units, or 10% if the structure contains more than four. Landlord and Tenant agree the late fee is a reasonable estimate of uncertain damages to Landlord related to the late payment of rent. Acceptance of a late payment does not waive Landlord's right to require full payment of Rent on the date it is due or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease.
notes: TX: DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED 2026-09-25 (instruction 21). Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92 read in full, section-open, 2026-09-25 (Justia '2025 Texas Statutes' host copy supplied by Taylor; per-section history lines checked - latest amendments 89th Leg., R.S. (2025); CONFIRMED 2026-09-25 against the official statutes.capitol.texas.gov ch. 92 page supplied by Taylor: no 1st or 2nd called-session amendment; text matches section for section - TX log s14). Controlling text: Tex. Prop. Code s92.019 (Amended by Acts 2019, 86th Leg., R.S., Ch. 629 (S.B. 1414), eff. Sept. 1, 2019) and s92.0191 (added same Act). Defects in the pre-rigor text: (1) 'No late fee will be assessed until at least 2 days after Rent is due' - statute requires that any portion of rent has remained unpaid TWO FULL DAYS after the date originally due (s92.019(a)(3)); '2 days after' reads as allowing a fee on day 2. (2) Omitted s92.019(b): initial plus daily fees are ONE late fee for the percentage test - a daily fee stacked on a capped initial fee could breach the cap. (3) Presented 12%/10% as an absolute cap; they are the reasonableness SAFE HARBOR (s92.019(a-1)(1)). A higher fee is lawful under (a-1)(2) if not more than the landlord's uncertain damages (collection costs, overhead) - this clause deliberately stays inside the safe harbor, which forfeits any higher lawful amount (K.3 ceiling-only warning; judgment call surfaced for Taylor, TX log s4). (4) Omitted s92.0191 statement-on-request. Builder: the 'later of' formulation means no {{late_fee_grace_days}} value can shorten the statutory two full days. Unit-count threshold is per STRUCTURE, not per property. Penalty for violation: $100 + 3x the fee collected + attorney's fees (s92.019(c)); waiver void (s92.019(d)). Supersedes late-fee (base not tagged TX). | Prior (pre-rigor) body: Any late fee assessed under this Lease is intended to be a reasonable estimate of Landlord's damages from a late payment of Rent, consistent with Texas law, and will not exceed 12% of one rental period's Rent for a property with 4 or fewer units, or 10% of one rental period's Rent for a property with more than 4 units. No late fee will be assessed until at least 2 days after Rent is due. | TX: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's fee and the agreed-damages sentence; the two-day floor is now a bracket prompt, and the 12%/10% cap and written-statement duty are in edu-late-fee-rules-tx. | TX: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): follow-up fix: removed the limit bracket placed next to {{late_fee_grace_days}}, which would have printed in the lease; the two-day floor stays in edu-late-fee-rules-tx and the builder check (Addendum M.13). | TX retro 2026-10-03 (SOP 1.29, fix 21 and rule 78): two conditions RESTORED to the lease text. The 2026-09-29 scrub left '{{late_fee_grace_days}} days after the date it was originally due'; a lawful-looking entry of 2 then allows a fee on the third day, but Tex. Prop. Code §92.019(a)(3) bars any fee until rent 'has remained unpaid two full days after the date the rent was originally due', and a number check that accepts 2 cannot see the difference. The clause again requires both the two-full-day floor and the landlord's grace period (the later controls). Second, §92.019(b) makes initial and daily fees 'a single late fee'; lawful-looking separate figures (for example 5% initial plus a daily fee) can pass the §92.019(a-1)(1) 12%/10% safe harbor within days, and no per-figure check catches the running total, so the clause again caps the combined fee by structure size. Staying inside the safe harbor means the clause never needs the §92.019(a-1)(2) uncertain-damages route for a higher fee (the agreed-estimate sentence remains as support for reasonableness), the same deliberate choice recorded 2026-09-25 (TX log §4). Required-content search: §92.019(a)(1) 'notice of the fee is included in a written lease' - this clause is that notice and still is; no other required-content provision reaches it (battery in the TX retro log). Penalty unchanged: $100 + 3x the fee + fees (§92.019(c)). Read section-open 2026-10-03 from the official Texas statutes (chapter HTML served by tcss.legis.texas.gov behind statutes.capitol.texas.gov; site current through the 89th Legislature, 2nd Called Session, 2025); the whole Property, Business & Commerce, Civil Practice & Remedies and Finance Codes and the Constitution were loaded, proved complete against the site's chapter lists, saved and hash-matched (TX log, 'Retro checks (SOP 1.29)').

title: Late Charge
bodyText: Monthly Rent is due on the first day of each rental period. If Landlord has not received the full Monthly Rent by the end of the fourth day of the rental period (counting the day Rent is due as the first day), Tenant will owe a late charge of {{late_fee_amount}}, a flat amount charged once for that rental period, which becomes due on the fifth day of the rental period. Landlord will not charge a late charge if Landlord refused a payment Tenant offered by check or another commercially reasonable method, and will not deduct a late charge from a Rent payment.
notes: OR: Dormant row rewritten and activated (rule 25; OR log §5): the old text described Oregon's three late-charge structures but read them as caps on a lease figure and left out the written-agreement contents. Overrides `late-fee` and `late-fee-ne`, which are not tagged: their grace period is whatever the builder fills in, and a landlord may impose a late charge 'only if' 'The rent payment is not received by the fourth day of the weekly or monthly rental period for which rent is payable' (ORS 90.260(1)(a)) and a written rental agreement specifies the tenant's obligation, 'The type and amount of the late charge' and 'The date on which rent payments are due and the date or day on which late charges become due' (ORS 90.260(1)(b)(A)-(C)); this clause states all three, so it is the written agreement the statute requires for any late charge (REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE). It fixes the fourth-day rule in its own words, so {{late_fee_grace_days}} is not used (OR log §10). It uses the flat-amount structure only: 'A reasonable flat amount, charged once per rental period' (ORS 90.260(2)(a)), and 'Reasonable amount' means the customary amount for the rental market, a limit the landlord's {{late_fee_amount}} must meet (Claude's drafting choice; the per-day and five percent structures in ORS 90.260(2)(b)-(c) are explained in `edu-late-fee-or`). Refused payments: 'A landlord may not charge a late fee or terminate a tenancy based on nonpayment of rent or other charge if a landlord refuses to allow a payment offered by the tenant under subsection (1) of this section' (Or. Laws 2026, ch. 23, § 3(3)) (effective June 5, 2026, § 8; applies to rental agreements entered into before, on or after that date, § 7(1)). No deduction: ORS 90.260(4). The shared clause's blanket non-waiver sentence is left out on purpose: Oregon's acceptance-waiver rule (ORS 90.412) turns on warning notices and agreements made after the violation, which a lease sentence can't supply (`edu-waiver-by-acceptance-or`). Rent due date: rent 'may not be considered to be due prior to the first day of each rental period' (ORS 90.220(7)(a)). (OR battery 200 (late charges and late fees (caps)): 24 hits, control 0; known positives passed (1 real section, 1 synthetic); scope CONST 383, OAR 40864, ORS 39614, SL2026 142) Read section-open 2026-10-04 from the saved, hash-matched corpus of the whole Oregon Revised Statutes (oregonlegislature.gov, 2025 edition, every chapter page with history lines and Notes), the Oregon Constitution, the 2026 session laws as enrolled and the Oregon Administrative Rules (secure.sos.state.or.us). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Late Fee Guidance
bodyText: Landlord and Tenant agree that if Tenant fails to pay rent when due, the actual damage to Landlord from that late payment would, from the nature of the case, be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix. Landlord and Tenant therefore agree that {{late_fee_amount}} shall be presumed to be the amount of damage sustained by Landlord from a late payment of rent. This amount is a presumed measure of Landlord's actual damages and is not a penalty.
notes: CA: REWRITTEN 2026-09-19 against Civ. Code s1671 (primary text supplied by Taylor). CONFIRMED STANDARD INVERSION - the prior dormant row recited the s1671(b) test ('a reasonable estimate of Landlord's actual damages'), which is the wrong test for a residential lease. s1671(c)(2) routes a lease of real property for use as a dwelling to subdivision (d), NOT (b). Under s1671(d) a liquidated-damages provision is VOID, except that the parties may agree on an amount presumed to be the damage 'when, from the nature of the case, it would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix the actual damage.' Two consequences the old text got backwards: (1) the default is voidness, not validity; (2) the burden flips - under (b) the party attacking the clause must prove it unreasonable, while under (d) the landlord must bring the clause within the exception. The new body text is drafted to track (d)'s exception language rather than the (b) standard. s1671(a) yields to any other statute expressly prescribing a liquidated-damages rule for the contract - none found for residential late fees in the sections read, but note s1950.5 expressly governs security, so deposit-forfeiture provisions route there and not through s1671. NOT CONFIRMED: the old row's assertion that 'California does not set a statutory cap on late fees' is consistent with everything read this pass but is NOT a full-chapter proof-of-absence - no dedicated late-fee cap search was run. Do not upgrade that limb to CITED without one. Also unread: Orozco v. Casimiro and Del Monte Properties v. Dolan are the cases usually cited for applying s1671(d) to residential late fees; both are pointers only, neither has been read. EXTEND SCREEN 2026-09-19: now supersedes the base row `late-fee`, which is blocked for CA. s1951.5 RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (primary text supplied): it reads in its entirety 'Section 1671, relating to liquidated damages, applies to a lease of real property.' CONFIRMATORY, NOT CORRECTIVE, as predicted - s1671(c)(2) already reached a lease of real property for use as a dwelling on its own terms, and s1951.5 removes any argument that s1671 is confined to contracts for goods and services. No change to this row's analysis; the earlier flag is cleared. MILITARY TENANTS, added 2026-09-19: Mil. & Vet. Code s403(b) - no fine or penalty accrues during a court stay of an action to enforce the lease, and a court may relieve a service member from a late fee incurred while in service if military service materially impaired their ability to pay. Applies during service and within 120 days after. See edu-military-default-judgment-ca. || OPEN ITEM CLOSED 2026-09-28, gap-discovery source 4 (outside-title search). This row's notes said the 'California does not set a statutory cap on late fees' limb was NOT a proof of absence and must not be upgraded without a dedicated late-fee cap search. That search has now been run on the official leginfo code full-text search: 'late fee' in the Civil Code returns 13 sections and 'late charge' 23. Reviewed by section and title, the hits are common interest development assessments (ss5650, 5655, 5658, 5665, 5685, 5720, 6808, 6812), mortgage and deed-of-trust late charges (ss2954.4, 2954.5), retail installment and consumer credit (ss1812.402, 1812.626, 1812.643, 1799.91), debt collection (s1788.102), s3273.23, and the WATER SUBMETER sections. NO general cap on residential rent late fees exists, so the s1671(d) analysis in this row is the whole of the law on the amount. ONE REAL EXCEPTION, and it is new to the library: Civ. Code s1954.213 caps late fees on SUBMETERED WATER bills at $7 on the first bill and $10 on each subsequent bill, with all late fees in any 12-month period limited to 10 percent of the unpaid amount, and bars any late fee until 25 days after the bill is sent. Water charges are not rent (s1954.213(d)), so that cap does not touch a rent late fee - but a landlord who submeters has two different late-fee regimes running at once. See edu-water-submeter-billing-ca. SCOPE of the search: statutes only, exact phrases and the two word forms run; regulations, local ordinances and case law were not searched, and Orozco v. Casimiro and Del Monte Properties v. Dolan remain unread. | CA: 2026-09-29 (Addendum M.14): {{late_fee}} renamed {{late_fee_amount}}, the name clauseVariables.js resolves; the placeholder had always printed raw.

title: NSF Fee Limit
bodyText: If Tenant pays Rent or any other amount due under this Lease by check, draft or order for payment and it is not honored for lack of funds, because Tenant has no account with the drawee, or because Tenant stops payment, Tenant shall be liable to Landlord for the amount of the payment and a service charge of {{nsf_fee}}. No service charge is owed if Tenant stopped payment in order to resolve a good faith dispute with Landlord, if Tenant gives Landlord written confirmation from Tenant's financial institution that the instrument was returned because of that institution's error, or if Tenant gives Landlord written confirmation that the account had insufficient funds because of a delay in the regularly scheduled transfer or posting of a direct deposit of a social security or government benefit assistance payment.
notes: CA: REWRITTEN 2026-09-19 against Civ. Code s1719(a) (primary text supplied by Taylor). Figures CONFIRMED - $25 first, $35 each subsequent 'to that payee' - but the prior dormant row carried three defects. (1) FRAMING: it said the cap applies 'as required by California law'. s1719(a)(1) is a statutory ENTITLEMENT capped at those amounts, not a requirement to charge. Third CA row found reciting a landlord option as a legal mandate, after month-to-month-notice-ca and the CO entry-notice precedent. (2) INSTRUMENT SCOPE - the substantive defect. The old row capped the fee for any 'dishonored or returned payment'. s1719(a)(6) defines the trigger as making, uttering, drawing or delivering a CHECK, DRAFT OR ORDER for the payment of money upon a bank or depository that refuses to honor it. A returned ACH debit or a declined card is not obviously an instrument drawn by the tenant, so s1719 may not reach electronic payment methods at all. That cuts both ways: the old row asserted a statutory safe harbour over payment types the statute may not cover, and for those types a returned-payment fee in a residential lease is an ordinary liquidated-damages provision governed by s1671(d) - VOID unless actual damages were impracticable or extremely difficult to fix. See late-fee-safe-harbor-ca; the two rows are now linked by that analysis. Clause scoped to checks, drafts and orders accordingly. (3) OMITTED EXCEPTIONS: s1719(a)(3) good-faith-dispute stop payment, where the payee recovers only on CLEAR AND CONVINCING evidence that no good faith dispute existed; (a)(4) written confirmation of financial institution error; (a)(5) written confirmation that the shortfall came from a delayed direct deposit of SOCIAL SECURITY OR GOVERNMENT BENEFIT ASSISTANCE. A flat fee clause misstates the law against benefit recipients in particular. All three now in body text. Note s1719(a)(6)(C): a STOP PAYMENT counts as passing a check on insufficient funds, subject to the good-faith-dispute carve-out. CROSS-CHAPTER: s1719 sits in Part 3, Obligations Imposed by Law - outside the landlord-tenant title. Instruction 7 pattern, fourth confirmation in CA. EXTEND SCREEN 2026-09-19: now supersedes the base row `returned-payments`, which is blocked for CA. s1719 NOW READ IN FULL 2026-09-19 - three additions. (1) TREBLE DAMAGES, s1719(a)(2): after a written demand by CERTIFIED MAIL stating the section's provisions, the check amount and the service charge, the drawer has 30 DAYS to pay; failing that, liability becomes the unpaid check amount PLUS TREBLE that amount, not less than $100 nor more than $1,500, in place of the service charge. (2) EXCEPTIONS to the service charge: a STOP PAYMENT in a good-faith dispute (payee must prove no good-faith dispute by clear and convincing evidence, s1719(a)(3), (b)); written confirmation of BANK ERROR (a)(4); and a delayed SOCIAL SECURITY or government benefit deposit (a)(5). For a stop payment, the demand must be in the prescribed s1719(c) form, sent certified with a receipt in evidence (d), and the payee must show a reasonable effort to reconcile before suing (e). s1719(j)(2): liability arises only ONCE per check. (3) NO POSTDATED-CHECK EXCLUSION anywhere in s1719 - candidate 427.4's North Dakota trap does not exist here. The ACH/card scope caveat stands: every limb is framed around a 'check, draft, or order'. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's fee; the restated $25/$35 cap and the tenant's statutory defenses moved to edu-nsf-treble-damages-ca. | CA: RESTORED 2026-10-03, SOP 1.31 retro check 25 (rule 78 with rule 47). The 2026-09-29 scrub moved the whole of s1719's tenant-side content to edu-nsf-treble-damages-ca, including the THREE STATUTORY EXCEPTIONS, leaving a bare 'service charge of {{nsf_fee}}' that a builder number check cannot save: the $25/$35 cap is a number check (backlog M.13), but the exceptions are CONDITIONS, and with them gone the clause tells a tenant a charge is owed in three cases where s1719 says it is not. Civ. Code s1719(a)(3), (a)(4) and (a)(5) re-read section-open on leginfo 2026-10-03 and restored to body text in the statute's own terms: (a)(3) stop payment to resolve a GOOD FAITH DISPUTE, where the payee recovers only on clear and convincing evidence that no good faith dispute existed; (a)(4) written confirmation of FINANCIAL-INSTITUTION ERROR; (a)(5) written confirmation that the shortfall came from a delay in a direct deposit of SOCIAL SECURITY OR GOVERNMENT BENEFIT ASSISTANCE. The third is the New Jersey shape exactly (NJ restored the 2A:42-6.1 senior and benefit-recipient grace period to late-fee-nj): a flat fee clause misstates the law against benefit recipients in particular. The treble-damages route, the certified-mail demand and the prescribed s1719(c) notice stay in edu-nsf-treble-damages-ca - they are remedy machinery, not conditions on the clause. Nothing else in the clause changed.

title: Returned Payments
bodyText: If any payment Tenant makes under this Lease by check, draft, order of payment, debit card order, or electronic funds transfer is refused by the drawee because of lack of funds, lack of credit, or lack of an account, or if Tenant stops payment on it with intent to defraud, Tenant will pay Landlord the bank fees Landlord actually incurred in tendering the payment, plus a service charge of $25 if the face value does not exceed $50, $30 if the face value exceeds $50 but does not exceed $300, or $40 if the face value exceeds $300, or 5 percent of the face value, whichever is greater. Landlord may require that the payment be replaced by a cashier's check, certified check, or money order. If more than two of Tenant's payments during the Term are returned, Landlord may require all future payments of Rent to be made by cashier's check, certified check, or money order. This Section does not limit any other remedy Florida law gives Landlord for a dishonored payment.
notes: FL: DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED 2026-09-26 (instruction 21). Primary text pasted by Taylor 2026-09-26 from flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026 (official 2026 Florida Statutes), read section-open with history lines. Supersedes returned-payments (base not tagged FL: the rewritten row states the measure the base's 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' points to, and both cannot display). Controlling text: Fla. Stat. §68.065(2) (s. 1, ch. 2013-113 latest): 'In lieu of a service charge authorized under subsection (3), s. 832.062(4)(a), or s. 832.07, the payee ... may lawfully collect bank fees actually incurred ... plus a service charge of $25 ... $30 ... $40 ...; or 5 percent of the face value ..., whichever is greater.' What the pre-rigor row got right: the $25/$30/$40 tiers and the $50/$300 break points. What it got wrong: (1) the 5% alternative applies at EVERY tier, not only above $300; (2) actual bank fees are recoverable IN ADDITION; (3) the statute covers drafts, orders of payment, debit card orders and electronic funds transfers, not only checks (§68.065(1)); (4) it reaches stop-payments only with intent to defraud. The tiers also appear in §832.08(5), the state attorney's diversion-fee schedule, which is not a landlord cap. Additional remedy: after a 30-day written demand in the §68.065(4) form, treble damages (minimum $50) plus costs and fees in a civil action (§68.065(3)); hardship waiver (7) (edu-dishonored-payment-remedies-fl). The charge is not designated rent (library default), so it cannot be demanded in a §83.56(3) 3-day notice as rent. Replacement-method sentences carried from the base; no Florida payment-method statute in Part II (acceptable-payment-methods tagged FL).

title: Dishonored Check Fee
bodyText: If a check Tenant gives Landlord is dishonored because of a lack of funds or credit, because Tenant has no account with the bank, or because Tenant stopped payment without good cause, Tenant will owe Landlord a dishonored check fee of [amount, not more than $35] plus any amount a bank charged Landlord for processing the dishonored check. Landlord will not charge a fee for any other failed or returned payment.
notes: OR: Dormant row rewritten and activated (rule 25; OR log §5): the old text was close but said 'any actual bank charges' and reached any 'dishonored or returned payment'. Overrides `returned-payments`, which is not tagged: it lets Landlord demand certified funds after a failed payment and states the fee only as a ceiling (rule 53), and Oregon now requires a landlord to 'allow a tenant to make payments by check or other commercially reasonable methods' (Or. Laws 2026, ch. 23, § 3(1); effective June 5, 2026, § 8; applies to rental agreements entered into before, on or after that date, § 7(1)). Fee: a landlord may charge a fee for 'A dishonored check, pursuant to ORS 30.701 (5). The amount of the fee may not exceed the amount described in ORS 30.701 (5) plus any amount that a bank has charged the landlord for processing the dishonored check' (ORS 90.302(2)(b)); 'If a check is dishonored, the payee may collect from the maker a fee not to exceed $35' (ORS 30.701(5)). The three reasons in the clause are the only ones ORS 30.701(6) reaches, and 'Check' means 'a check, draft or order for the payment of money' (ORS 30.701(7)(a)); a fee for a failed card or electronic payment is not on the ORS 90.302 list, and a fee not allowed by ORS 90.302 costs 'twice the actual damages of the tenant or $300, whichever is greater' (ORS 90.302(8)). A fee must be described in a written rental agreement (ORS 90.302(1)); this clause is that description. title: Bounced Checks and Returned Payments
bodyText: Pennsylvania has no civil statute capping the fee a landlord may charge for a returned rent payment; a fee in the lease should be reasonable. Writing a check knowing it will not be paid is a crime. On conviction, the court orders repayment of the check, interest and a service charge of up to $50 (or the payee's actual bank fees if higher), but only if a written notice of the service charge was conspicuously displayed at the payee's premises when the check was given. After a conviction and a written demand at least 10 days before suit, the payee may sue for the greater of $100 or three times the check, limited to $500 more than the check's value.
notes: PA: Read section-open 2026-09-29 in the built-in browser on the General Assembly's official site (palegis.us) and, for court rules and regulations, the official Pennsylvania Code site (pacodeandbulletin.gov): The Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951 (1951 P.L. 69, No. 20) read whole from the official unconsolidated-statute text with every amendment note (newest: Act 88 of 2024, 2024 P.L. 944); the Pennsylvania Constitution and all 74 titles of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes (75 files) loaded from the official title files (29.28 million characters; revision stamps 2022-03-07 to 2026-09-16) and searched whole; all 262 acts of 2024, 2025 and 2026 screened in full text for landlord-tenant terms; no special-session act in 2024-2026 (PA log §1). P.S. numbers are Purdon's, which the official site does not print; each 1951-Act cite gives the Act section in parentheses (kickoff rule). DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED (instruction 21). Former text (pre-project, UNVERIFIED, inactive): 'Any fee charged for a dishonored or returned payment under this Lease will not exceed $50.00, or the actual fee Landlord's bank charges if higher, as required by Pennsylvania law.' WHAT IT TURNED OUT TO BE: the $50-or-bank-fee figure is real but is CRIMINAL RESTITUTION on conviction under 18 Pa.C.S. § 4105(e)(3) (last amended Act 70 of 2007), conditioned on a written notice of the service charge 'conspicuously displayed on the payee's premises when the check was issued'; it is not a cap on lease fees and 'as required by Pennsylvania law' was wrong. The kickoff's candidate '13 Pa.C.S. § 3506' does not exist (Title 13 Chapter 35 ends at 13 Pa.C.S. § 3505; official Title 13 text, revised 2025-12-01). Civil damages after conviction: 42 Pa.C.S. § 8304 (greater of $100 or triple; not more than $500 over the check; 10-day written demand; partial restitution limit). ABSENCE: no civil returned-check fee cap located - Pa.C.S. regex '(returned|dishonou?red|bad|worthless) (check|instrument|payment)' near fee/charge: 18 Pa.C.S. § 4105, 7 Pa.C.S. § 6122 (mortgage licensees), 75 Pa.C.S. § 1374 only (PA log §17 search 80); unconsolidated "dishonored check" 18 results (banking, vehicle and 2008 Act 117 sections, none landlord). Converted from a lease clause to education because no statute constrains a lease fee; `returned-payments` (tagged PA, 'not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law') carries the lease term. Id kept so the dormant row is resolved in place.

title: Returned Payments
bodyText: If any payment of Rent or other amount due under this Lease is dishonored and returned unpaid, Tenant will pay Landlord a processing fee of {{nsf_fee}}, unless a reimbursement fee for the same payment has been collected under Article 102.007(e) of the Texas Code of Criminal Procedure; if one is collected after Tenant pays the processing fee, Landlord will refund the processing fee. Landlord may require that the payment be replaced by a cashier's check, certified check, or money order. If more than two of Tenant's payments during the Term are returned unpaid, Landlord may require all future payments of Rent to be made by cashier's check, certified check, or money order.
notes: TX: DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED 2026-09-25 (instruction 21). Primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-25 from the official Texas Constitution and Statutes site (statutes.capitol.texas.gov), with per-section history lines; read section-open. Controlling text: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code s3.506 (Added 2001; last Amended by Acts 2019, 86th Leg., R.S., Ch. 1352 (S.B. 346), eff. Jan. 1, 2020). Not in Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92. Pre-rigor row: the $30 figure was right. Its claim that the fee applies 'in addition to any fee the bank itself assesses' is NOT supported by s3.506(b), which sets a 'maximum processing fee of $30'. s3.506(e) says the section does not affect rights under a written contract - whether that lets a lease add the landlord's own bank charges on top is an AMBIGUITY (research-mode candidate, TX log s11.4); the clause stays inside $30 total. 'Payment device' includes paper or electronic payments (s3.506(a)), so ACH returns are covered. No fee if a reimbursement fee was collected through the district-attorney check process (s3.506(c), Code Crim. Proc. art. 102.007(e) - unread). Supersedes returned-payments (base not tagged TX: its 'maximum permitted by law' referent is now known, but a hard number is safer than a self-limit). Requiring certified funds after dishonor is a written-lease payment requirement consistent with s92.011(a). | Prior (pre-rigor) body: Any processing fee charged for a dishonored or returned payment under this Lease will not exceed $30.00, in addition to any fee the bank itself assesses, as required by Texas law. | Earlier 2026-09-25 hold note: TX 2026-09-25: STILL DORMANT - research question pending Tex. Bus. & Com. Code s3.506 and neighbours (requested). Not in Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92 (full read: no returned-payment provision). The row's claim that a bank's own fee may be added on top of the $30 figure has no support yet. base returned-payments held for TX on the same dependency. | TX: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's fee and payment-method rights; the $30 cap moved to edu-returned-payment-fee-tx. | TX retro 2026-10-03 (SOP 1.29, fix 21 and rule 78): condition RESTORED. After the scrub moved the $30 cap to `edu-returned-payment-fee-tx`, a lawful-looking fee of $30 or less still breaks Tex. Bus. & Com. Code §3.506(c) if a reimbursement fee was collected through the district-attorney process ('A person may not charge a processing fee ... if a reimbursement fee has been collected under Article 102.007(e), Code of Criminal Procedure', and a fee already collected must be refunded 'immediately'). A number check cannot see that, so the clause now carries it. The $30 ceiling is a number a builder check can catch, so it stays in education. Code Crim. Proc. art. 102.007(e) itself not read; the condition is stated from §3.506(c). Required-content search: no statute requires lease text for a returned-payment fee. Read section-open 2026-10-03 from the official Texas statutes (chapter HTML served by tcss.legis.texas.gov behind statutes.capitol.texas.gov; site current through the 89th Legislature, 2nd Called Session, 2025); the whole Property, Business & Commerce, Civil Practice & Remedies and Finance Codes and the Constitution were loaded, proved complete against the site's chapter lists, saved and hash-matched (TX log, 'Retro checks (SOP 1.29)').

title: Use of Security Deposit
bodyText: Tenant shall pay Landlord a security deposit of {{security_deposit}} (Security Deposit) prior to occupancy. Landlord may apply the Security Deposit to remedy a Tenant default under this Lease, including past due Rent, and to repair damage to the property caused by Tenant or Tenant's guests beyond ordinary wear and tear. Landlord will not apply the Security Deposit to normal wear and tear or to any damage or defective condition that preexisted the tenancy. Landlord may apply the Security Deposit to cleaning costs only if the property is substantially less clean at the end of the Term than it was at the start of the Term. The Security Deposit will not relieve Tenant of any obligation to pay Rent due under this Lease prior to its termination.
notes: CO added - verified this session (statute walk + full-library audit; content itself EDITED this session | NE extended (session 6, closing the last open NE item): Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1416(2) permits applying the deposit 'to the payment of rent and the amount of damages which the landlord has suffered by reason of the tenant's noncompliance with the rental agreement or section 76-1421' — substantively the same rent-plus-damages-beyond-wear-and-tear framing this clause already uses. No last-month's-rent restriction like Kansas's, so no override needed. Not extended to WY in this pass — WY currently has no clause of this type at all (security-deposit-use-wy doesn't exist), a separate, pre-existing gap noticed while resolving this, not fixed here since it's outside this session's Nebraska-specific scope. | MN extended (Minnesota session, whole-library audit): matches Minn. Stat. § 504B.178, subd. 3(b) — landlord may withhold only for rent defaults and to restore the property, ordinary wear and tear excepted. No conflict. | ND extended (North Dakota session 1, statute walk): N.D.C.C. § 47-16-07.1(3) permits application to pet/negligence damage, unpaid rent, and cleaning/repair costs necessary to restore the property, reasonable wear and tear excepted — compatible with this clause's existing self-limiting language. No ND-specific override needed. | SD extended (South Dakota session 1, whole-library generic-clause audit): SDCL 43-32-6.1's deposit-application concept (deposit secures performance of the rental agreement) is compatible with the generic's existing self-limiting language (default/damage beyond wear-and-tear, not preexisting conditions); no SD-specific override needed for the use/application language itself. Return mechanics are SD-specific and handled separately by security-deposit-return-sd (switched off 2026-09-29). | WY ADDED 2026-08-28 (deposit split, Taylor's decision): WY previously folded application language into security-deposit-return-wy. Split to the CO pattern. Compatible with Wyo. Stat. 1-21-1208(a). TWO DELIBERATE GIVEAWAYS accepted: (1) cleaning deductions only if 'substantially less clean', vs 1208(a)'s 'clean to the condition at start'; (2) 1208(a)'s catch-all 'any other costs this Lease provides for' not carried over. Both more tenant-favorable than WY requires. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written; narrower than 118A.242(4), which allows reasonable cleaning costs (clause limits cleaning deductions further - lawful, tenant-favourable). Return mechanics in security-deposit-return-nv. | TX: Read in full 2026-09-25 against Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92 (full chapter, section-open; Justia 2025 host copy with per-section history lines). Applies as written. Consistent with s92.104(a)-(b) (deductions for damages/charges the tenant is legally liable for; none for normal wear and tear as defined s92.001(4)). The cleaning limit is stricter than Texas requires - a voluntary landlord limit, lawful. | GA: Applies as written. O.C.G.A. § 44-7-34(a) allows retention for unpaid rent and late fees, abandonment, unpaid utilities, repair or cleaning contracted by the tenant with third parties, unpaid pet fees and actual damages from breach (with mitigation), and bars retention for ordinary wear and tear; this clause is narrower on cleaning, which is lawful. 'Prior to occupancy' works with O.C.G.A. § 44-7-33(a) only if the move-in damage list is presented BEFORE the deposit is tendered (`move-in-damage-list-ga`). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | TN: Tagged 2026-09-28 (section text read 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser (Justia host copy of the 2025 Tennessee Code with history lines; 2025-2026 public chapters screened; TN log §1)). Consistent with the Act-county definition of a security deposit (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-104(14): damage beyond ordinary wear and tear and monetary damage from breach) and § 66-28-301(e) (application to unpaid rent); the cleaning limit is more protective than the statute. No deposit statute outside Act counties. TN-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. | UT: Utah Code Ann. § 57-17-3(1) allows applying a deposit to rent, damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, other costs and fees provided for in the contract, and cleaning; this clause is narrower (cleaning only if substantially less clean), which the landlord may choose. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IL: Tagged. Withholding for damage beyond normal wear and tear requires the itemized statement (765 ILCS 710/1(a)); security-deposit-return-il and deposit-cost-schedule-il supply the Illinois mechanics. Read section-open 2026-09-30 (IL log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ID: Idaho Code § 6-321(1): a deposit is refunded 'except amounts necessary to cover the contingencies specified in the deposit arrangement', and may not be kept for normal wear and tear. This clause is the specification of contingencies; it names default, past-due Rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear and cleaning. Lawful as written. Read section-open 2026-09-30 from legislature.idaho.gov (ID log s1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | OK: Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 115(B): the deposit may be applied to accrued rent and damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the act and the rental agreement; the clause's 'remedy a Tenant default' and wear-and-tear limits fit. Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 115(F): unless the rental agreement provides otherwise the tenant may not apply the deposit to the last month's rent; the clause's last sentence keeps that default. Return, demand and the six-month reversion: security-deposit-return-ok; escrow: edu-security-deposit-rules-ok. Read section-open 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 from oklegislature.gov (OK log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NM: Applies as written. NMSA 1978, § 47-8-18(A): a 'reasonable deposit to be applied by the owner to recover damages, if any, caused to the premises by the resident'; NMSA 1978, § 47-8-18(C): on termination, deposits may be applied 'to the payment of rent and the amount of damages which the owner has suffered by reason of the resident's noncompliance with the rental agreement or Section 47-8-22', never to normal wear and tear, and nothing prevents retaining portions 'for nonpayment of rent or utilities, repair work or other legitimate damages'. Uncleanliness is not normal wear and tear (NMSA 1978, § 47-8-3(K)); the clause's narrower cleaning standard is lawful. Applying the deposit during the tenancy is not addressed by NMSA 1978, § 47-8-18(C), which speaks of application 'upon termination of the residency'; it is not prohibited, and the act allows terms it does not prohibit (NMSA 1978, § 47-8-14) (Claude's reading). Limits on {{security_deposit}} (one month's rent for an agreement shorter than a year; interest above one month's rent under an annual agreement) are in `edu-deposit-cap-nm` and the builder (NM log §10). Read section-open 2026-10-02 in the built-in browser from nmonesource.com (NMSA 1978 annotated chapter PDFs, 2026 compilation; the whole NMSA 1978 and the Constitution loaded, saved and hash-matched, NM log §1); 2025 N.M. Laws ch. 122 read as enrolled (NM log §1.2). Rule 15: written section-open. | FL: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). Fla. Stat. §83.49 does not bar applying the deposit during the tenancy (contrast NJ 46:8-21.1); §83.43(14) defines security deposits as money held 'as security for the performance of the rental agreement'. Return mechanics sit in security-deposit-return-fl (instruction 24 family). A pet deposit is 'deposit money' (§83.43(4)). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | FL: FL retro 2026-10-03 (SOP 1.30) - rule 79 (group 1): basis recorded. Fla. Stat. ch. 83 Part II was read whole in the FL pass (2026-09-26); the sections this note cites were re-read section-open on the official Online Sunshine text 2026-10-03 and the note holds. | AL: Tagged. At termination the deposit may be applied only to accrued rent and to damages from the tenant's noncompliance with Ala. Code § 35-9A-301, itemized in writing (Ala. Code § 35-9A-201(b)); 'rent' includes all payments due under the lease (Ala. Code § 35-9A-141(12)). The clause's wear-and-tear, pre-existing-condition and cleaning limits are narrower than the statute, not broader. Return mechanics: `security-deposit-return-al`; cap: `security-deposit-cap-al`. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. AL basis (SOP 1.32 rule 79, 2026-10-03): every Alabama section cited in this segment read section-open on ALISON (official Code of Alabama, current versions after the 2026-10-01 effective date; text saved and SHA-256 matched, AL retro sources); cited subdivisions and qualifiers checked against the text. | AZ: Applies as written. A.R.S. §33-1321(D) lets the landlord apply prepaid rent and security to all rent and, subject to the duty to mitigate, to all charges specified in the signed lease or the Act, including damages from the tenant's noncompliance with §33-1341. This clause is narrower (no wear and tear, cleaning only if substantially less clean), which is a landlord choice, not a conflict. §33-1310(15): a reasonable charge for redecorating or cleaning is not "security". Return mechanics: security-deposit-return-az. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | AZ (retro 2026-10-03, SOP 1.32 rule 79, basis): every A.R.S. section cited in this row's AZ note re-read section-open 2026-10-03 in Taylor's built-in browser from azleg.gov (official compilation; each section fetched twice, copies matched, heading number checked; saved to the AZ retro source folder with a SHA-256 match); each cited subdivision says what the note says, and each qualifier sits on the sentence the statute attaches it to. | PA: Tagged. Consistent with 68 P.S. § 250.512(a) (Act § 512: damages caused by the tenant; withholding for nonpayment of rent or breach of any other lease condition); narrower on wear and tear and cleaning, so lawful. Return: `security-deposit-return-pa`. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. PA basis (SOP 1.49 rule 79, 2026-10-03): section-open, official text on palegis.us (68 P.S. § 250.512(a) (Act § 512(a)); 1951 Act text hash-matched to the live page, 72 of 72 sections); cited subdivision and qualifiers confirmed. | SC: Tagged. Withholding is limited to accrued rent and damages from the tenant's noncompliance with S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-510, which includes complying with the lease (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-510(8)), so 'remedy a Tenant default' and the cleaning sentence fit (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-410(a)). Deposit is held in trust (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-210(18)). title: Return of Security Deposit
bodyText: The Security Deposit, less any lawful deductions, will be returned to Tenant within the time period required by applicable law after Tenant vacates the property upon expiration or earlier termination of this Lease. Any deductions will be described in an itemized statement provided with the returned portion of the deposit. Tenant will provide Landlord a forwarding address to which the Security Deposit and itemized statement should be sent.
notes: CO added - verified this session (statute walk + full-library audit; content itself unchanged | Display-collision bug fixed (session 7, full-library supersedes audit): CO removed — already covered by a state-specific override that supersedes this row; both versions were displaying simultaneously before this fix.

title: Security Deposit Limit
bodyText: The total of all refundable deposits Landlord demands or receives under this Lease, including the Security Deposit and any damage deposit, pet deposit or advance rent deposit, will not exceed two months' Monthly Rent. Nonrefundable fees, and money that is to be applied toward the payment of Rent or to reimburse services or utilities provided to Tenant, are not deposits for this purpose. However, any amount Tenant pays in advance toward Rent for the last month of the Term is an advance rent deposit: it counts toward this limit and is held, applied and returned as part of the Security Deposit, unless this Lease states that the amount is Rent for a specific calendar month.
notes: GA: Read section-open 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser from Justia's '2025 Code of Georgia', a host copy of the official O.C.G.A. that already prints the 2026 session (history lines cite Ga. L. 2026, pp. 278, 988 and 1069), with each section's history line and editor's notes. DORMANT ROW RESOLVED (instruction 21): rewritten and activated. Controlling text: O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30.1 ('No landlord shall demand or receive a security deposit in an amount that exceeds the equivalent of two months' rent'; Ga. L. 2024, p. 91, § 4/HB 404, the Safe at Home Act, Act 392, signed 2024-04-22, effective 2024-07-01; HB 404 § 6 applies it to residential lease agreements entered into or renewed on or after 2024-07-01); O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30(3) ('security deposit' includes damage deposits, advance rent deposits and pet deposits; excludes nonrefundable fees and money not to be returned or to be applied toward rent or to reimburse services or utilities); O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30(1) (nonrefundable fee). The O.C.G.A. § 44-7-36 small-landlord exemption does NOT reach O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30.1. WHAT THE PRE-RIGOR ROW GOT RIGHT: the two-month cap, and that pet and other refundable deposits count. WHAT IT GOT WRONG OR LEFT OUT: (1) its second sentence ('returned within 30 days after Tenant vacates') misstated the trigger, which is 30 days after the landlord obtains possession under O.C.G.A. § 44-7-33(b) (termination and vacation, or surrender and acceptance, whichever first); that sentence is dropped and the return rule lives in `security-deposit-return-ga`; (2) it said nothing about nonrefundable fees or rent-applied money, which the definition excludes; (3) 'as required by Georgia law' was UNVERIFIED and the cap dates only from 2024-07-01. Pattern holds: one real fact, the operative rule partly missed. BUILDER: validate {{security_deposit}} + refundable pet deposit + any advance rent deposit (including any last-month amount entered in `due-at-signing`) <= 2 x {{monthly_rent}}. No statutory remedy for over-collection is stated in O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30.1; O.C.G.A. § 44-7-35 penalties concern withholding. LAST-MONTH RENT (Taylor decision 2026-09-28, GA log §6.1): the statute does not say where an 'advance rent deposit' (inside) ends and money 'to be applied toward the payment of rent' (outside) begins, so the library takes the conservative reading in the body's last sentence: money paid in advance toward the last month is a deposit, inside the cap and held, applied and returned under `security-deposit-escrow-ga` (unless the O.C.G.A. § 44-7-36 exemption applies) and `security-deposit-return-ga`, unless the lease expressly makes it Rent for a named calendar month. BUILDER: do NOT insert the named-month designation automatically, which would switch the rule off for every lease; a landlord who adds it by hand relies on the statute's unexplained line. PRIOR TEXT (dormant, UNVERIFIED, CONSTRAINED): "The Security Deposit under this Lease, including any pet deposit or other refundable deposit, will not exceed two months' Monthly Rent, as required by Georgia law. The Security Deposit will be returned to Tenant within 30 days after Tenant vacates the property." Prior notes: 'UNCHANGED - pre-existing tag from before this project, not touched this session'. | GA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-security-deposit-rules-ga). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Security Deposit Cap
bodyText: The Security Deposit under this Lease will not exceed two months' Monthly Rent, or one month's Monthly Rent if Tenant is 62 years of age or older, as Connecticut law requires.
notes: CT: DORMANT ROW REVERIFIED AND LEFT SWITCHED OFF (rule 25; CT log §5). The law it states is correct: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(b)(1) ('In the case of a tenant under sixty-two years of age, a landlord shall not demand a security deposit in an amount that exceeds two months' rent'); § 47a-21(b)(2) ('In the case of a tenant sixty-two years of age or older, a landlord shall not demand a security deposit in an amount that exceeds one month's rent'), with a refund of the excess on request when a tenant turns 62. title: Return of Security Deposit
bodyText: By the earlier of 60 days after the tenancy ends or 45 days after a new tenant moves into the property, Landlord will deliver to Tenant the Security Deposit, less any deductions this Lease and West Virginia law allow, together with a written itemization of the damages or other charges deducted. If damage to the property exceeds the Security Deposit and requires the services of a third-party contractor, Landlord will tell Tenant so in writing within that same period and will then provide the itemization of the damage and the cost of repair within 15 more days. Landlord will deliver the Security Deposit and any notice in person or by mail to Tenant's last known address or the forwarding address Tenant provides, and Tenant is responsible for giving Landlord an accurate address. If personal delivery is not reasonably possible and a mailed deposit or notice is returned as undeliverable, Landlord will hold it for six months and will deliver it to Tenant, or to Tenant's authorized agent or attorney, at Landlord's place of business during normal business hours within 72 hours after Landlord receives Tenant's written request.
notes: WV: Rule 25: this was the dormant UNVERIFIED row from the early nationwide pass (topic key 'security-deposit-return-wv'). Verified and rewritten: its 60 and 45 days are West Virginia's, but it counted from when 'Tenant vacates', while the statute counts 60 days from 'the termination of the tenancy' or 45 days from 'the occupation of the premise by a subsequent tenant', 'whichever time period is shorter' (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-1(7)); it omitted the contractor extension (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-2(c)) and the delivery and six-month hold rules (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-2(g)). Topic key corrected to `security-deposit-return` (rule 58). Delivery with 'a written itemization of any such damages or other charges' (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-2(a)); the tenant's address duty: 'It shall be the responsibility of the tenant to provide an accurate address to the landlord' (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-2(g)). Replaces the blank-states parent `security-deposit-return`, which says 'within the time period required by applicable law'. RECOMMENDED, not REQUIRED: no statute requires return terms in the lease (rule 56). Penalty `edu-security-deposit-penalty-wv`; records `edu-security-deposit-holding-wv`. Rule 37: the clock runs from termination of the tenancy for every tenancy type. title: Interest on the Security Deposit
bodyText: [Omit this Section if the property is in a building owned or controlled by an educational institution and used to house its students and their families.] Landlord will pay interest on the Security Deposit at a rate not less than the deposit index the Banking Commissioner sets for each calendar year. On each anniversary date of the tenancy, Landlord will [choose one: pay the interest to Tenant / credit the interest toward the next Rent payment due]. If the tenancy ends before an anniversary date, or Landlord returns all or part of the Security Deposit before the tenancy ends, Landlord will pay the accrued interest within 21 days. No interest is owed for any month in which Tenant was more than ten days late paying that month's Rent, unless Landlord charged a late charge for that late payment. Landlord will not increase the Rent because Landlord must pay this interest.
notes: CT: DORMANT ROW REVERIFIED AND REWRITTEN (rule 25; log §5). The old text's "administrative fee of up to 1%" has no basis in Connecticut law: § 47a-21(h)(2)(D) lets the escrow agent 'retain interest credited to the account in excess of the amount of interest payable to the tenant', which is not a fee charged against the tenant's interest; and a waiver of deposit interest is void (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(4)). Controlling text: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(i) (landlords 'other than a landlord of a residential unit in any building owned or controlled by any educational institution and used by such institution for the purpose of housing students of such institution and their families' pay interest; 'On and after January 1, 2012, the rate for each calendar year shall be not less than the deposit index, as defined in section 36a-26, for that year'; 'On the anniversary date of the tenancy and annually thereafter, such interest shall be paid to the tenant or resident or credited toward the next rental payment due from the tenant or resident, as the landlord or owner shall determine'; accrued interest due 'not later than twenty-one days after such termination or return'; 'Interest shall not be paid to a tenant for any month in which the tenant has been delinquent for more than ten days in the payment of any monthly rent, unless the landlord imposes a late charge for such delinquency'; 'No landlord shall increase the rent due from a tenant because of the requirement that the landlord pay on interest the security deposit'). The Banking Commissioner set the 2026 deposit index at 0.49% (Department of Banking page, saved and hashed 2026-10-09; log §1.1); the clause names no figure because it changes each year. SERVES_LANDLORD: the landlord's statutory choice to pay or credit, and the delinquency rule, are recorded in the Lease. topic_key changed from `security-deposit-interest-ct` to the shared key `security-deposit-interest` (rule 58). Read section-open in the 2026 Supplement. Rule 15: written section-open.
