GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Rent & Fees' -> 'Rent & Payment' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states). | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-rent-increase-notice-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Tenant Care of Premises
bodyText: Tenant shall keep the part of the premises Tenant occupies and uses clean and sanitary as the condition of the premises permits; dispose of all rubbish, garbage and other waste from the dwelling unit in a clean and sanitary manner; properly use and operate all electrical, gas and plumbing fixtures and keep them as clean and sanitary as their condition permits; neither do, nor permit any person on the premises with Tenant's permission to do, anything that willfully or wantonly destroys, defaces, damages, impairs or removes any part of the structure or dwelling unit or its facilities, equipment or appurtenances; and use the premises as Tenant's abode, using portions of it for living, sleeping, cooking or dining only as those portions were designed or intended to be used. Tenant shall repair deteriorations or injuries to the premises caused by Tenant's want of ordinary care.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1941.2 and 1929, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. These are the two provisions cross-referenced by s1942(c) as disqualifying a tenant from repair-and-deduct, so they are the other half of edu-repair-and-deduct-ca. s1941.2(a) is NOT a free-standing tenant duty clause - it is a CONDITION ON THE LANDLORD'S DUTY: the landlord's s1941/s1942 repair obligation does not arise where the tenant is in SUBSTANTIAL violation AND the violation CONTRIBUTES SUBSTANTIALLY to the dilapidation or substantially interferes with the landlord's ability to repair. Both qualifiers matter; a clause that recites the five duties without them overstates the landlord's position. rule_type RECOMMENDED rather than REQUIRED for that reason - the statute does not require these terms in a lease, it defines when the landlord is excused. TRAP AT s1941.2(b): paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) - cleanliness and waste disposal - DO NOT APPLY where the landlord has EXPRESSLY AGREED IN WRITING to perform them. So a lease in which the landlord undertakes cleaning or waste removal silently disables those two limbs as an excuse. Screen any CA lease that bundles janitorial or trash service. s1929 is the general hiring rule (want of ordinary care) and sits in Chapter 1, not Chapter 2. SUPERSEDES tenant-maintenance for CA as of 2026-09-19: the overlap check found both rows stating the same tenant care duties, which would have put them in a CA lease twice. This row tracks s1941.2 and governs. | CA: SOP 1.31 retro check 24 (rule 78), 2026-10-03: pointer repointed to edu-repair-and-deduct-ca. Found by the full sweep, not by the prompt's list. Also noted at this retro: Civ. Code ss1928 and 1929, read section-open 2026-10-03, are the statutory basis for the tenant's care and repair duties this clause states - see edu-no-landlord-self-cure-ca and edu-tenant-caused-damage-ca.

title: Application screening fees
bodyText: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only to cover the actual cost of screening, capped at a statutory amount that is adjusted annually for inflation, and may not charge one at all when the landlord knows or should know that no unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must also operate one of two processes: either consider completed applications in the order received against written screening criteria given to the applicant with the application form and approve the first applicant who meets them, or return the entire fee to every applicant not selected within seven days of selecting a tenant or thirty days of the application, whichever comes first. The landlord must give the applicant an itemized receipt, refund any part of the fee not actually used, and give the applicant a copy of any consumer credit report obtained within seven days of receiving it.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1950.6, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. AMENDED BY AB 1170, Stats. 2025 ch. 67, EFFECTIVE 2026-01-01 - one of the most recently changed provisions in the CA set, and squarely in the legal-watch zone. DO NOT HARDCODE $30. s1950.6(b) caps the fee at the lesser of actual out-of-pocket cost plus the reasonable value of time spent, or $30 per applicant, BUT the $30 'may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998'. The operative figure today is therefore a CPI-indexed number well above $30, computed from a 1998 base, and it is landlord-computed rather than published. Body text deliberately says 'a statutory amount adjusted annually for inflation' rather than stating a number. The app should not assert a figure it cannot derive. s1950.6(c)(2) is the structural obligation and it is new to this project: the landlord must OFFER one of two defined processes - (A) first-come-first-considered against written criteria supplied WITH THE APPLICATION FORM, first qualifying applicant approved, no fee until the application is actually considered, with a 7-day refund for inadvertent duplicate collection (or, at the applicant's option, transfer to another unit); or (B) full refund to every non-selected applicant within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever is first. This is product workflow, not lease text. s1950.6(c)(1): no fee where the landlord knows or should know no unit is or will soon be available. s1950.6(d) itemized receipt; (e) refund of the unused portion where no reference check or credit report was obtained; (f) copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant within 7 days of receipt. s1950.6(k): the fee is NOT 'security' under s1950.5 and not an 'advance fee' - so it sits outside the AB 12 deposit cap entirely. s1950.6(j) includes GUARANTORS AND COSIGNERS in 'applicant'. s1950.1 READ 2026-09-19 - see edu-reusable-screening-report-ca. The interaction matters: s1950.1(d) applies 'notwithstanding Section 1950.6', so a landlord who elects to accept reusable reports may charge an applicant who supplies one NEITHER an access fee NOR an application screening fee at all.

title: Three-day notice content and service
bodyText: California's three-day notices are governed by statute rather than by the lease. The three days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and judicial holidays. A notice demanding rent must state the amount due and the name, telephone number and address of the person to whom rent is to be paid, with the usual days and hours that person is available if payment may be made personally; alternatively it may give a financial institution account number with the institution's name and street address, provided the institution is within five miles of the rental property, or refer to an electronic funds transfer procedure already established. It must be served on the tenant and on any subtenant in actual occupation, and may be served at any time within one year after the rent becomes due. A notice to perform other covenants gives the tenant, a subtenant, a mortgagee or another interested person three days to perform and save the lease from forfeiture, and no such notice is required where the violated covenant can no longer be performed. Assigning or subletting contrary to the lease, committing waste, maintaining a nuisance or using the premises for an unlawful purpose terminates the lease and supports a three-day notice to quit with no opportunity to cure. Notices may be served by personal delivery; by leaving a copy with a person of suitable age and discretion at the tenant's residence or usual place of business and mailing a copy to the residence; or, where neither can be ascertained and no suitable person is found, by posting conspicuously on the property, delivering to a person residing there if one can be found, and mailing to the property. A landlord may not charge any fee for serving, posting or delivering these notices. You also may not charge the tenant any fee for serving, posting or otherwise delivering any notice about the tenancy, including a notice ending a periodic tenancy or a three-day notice (Civ. Code 1946.1(i); CCP 1161(6)). One more rule governs how these notices travel: California's electronic transactions law says outright that an electronic record may not be substituted for any notice required to be served under Code of Civil Procedure section 1162, which is the section that governs service of these notices. So a three-day notice, or a notice terminating a tenancy, cannot be emailed or texted in place of the statutory service methods, whatever the lease says about electronic delivery.
notes: CA: CCP ss1161 and 1162, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. s1161 amended by SB 611 (Stats. 2024 ch. 287), OPERATIVE 2025-02-01. Routed to LANDLORD_EDUCATION per the standing decision to send notice-and-cure mechanics to the legal tracker rather than into lease text. The s1161(2) content list MIRRORS Civ. Code s1962 almost exactly, INCLUDING THE FIVE-MILE FINANCIAL-INSTITUTION LIMIT and the conclusive-presumption-on-mailing proviso. The two must stay consistent: the lease disclosure under owner-identity-disclosure-ca supplies the same facts the pay-or-quit notice must recite, and s1962(c) separately bars a non-compliant SUCCESSOR owner from serving a s1161(2) notice for rent accrued during noncompliance. Getting the lease disclosure wrong therefore breaks the eviction notice too. The three days EXCLUDE Saturdays, Sundays and judicial holidays, in both s1161(2) and the s1161(3) cure window. A one-year outer limit applies to serving a rent notice. s1161(3): the cure right runs to the tenant, a subtenant in actual occupation, a MORTGAGEE OF THE TERM, or another person interested in its continuance - broader than the tenant alone. No notice is required where the violated covenant cannot afterward be performed. s1161(4): assignment or subletting contrary to the lease, waste, nuisance or unlawful purpose TERMINATES the lease by operation of the statute and supports a three-day notice to quit with NO cure right. Cross-references Civ. Code ss3482.8, 3485(c) and 3486(c), ALL READ 2026-09-19 - see edu-nuisance-eviction-assignment-ca. Only s3482.8 (dogfighting/cockfighting) is statewide. s3486 applies ONLY in the City of Los Angeles. s3485 APPEARS TO BE REPEALED as of 2024-01-01 by its own s3485(j), which means s1161(4) carries a cross-reference to a section that no longer exists - and s1161 was itself amended by SB 611 in 2024 and made operative 2025-02-01 without fixing it. Do not treat the s1161(4) deemed-nuisance list as three live statewide grounds; as read, it is one statewide ground, one city-specific ground, and one dead pointer. s1161(7): 'tenant' excludes occupancies described in Civ. Code s1940(b), READ 2026-09-19 - see edu-tenancy-scope-ca. Two exclusions: transient occupancy subject to transient occupancy tax under R&T s7280, and hotel/motel occupancy where the innkeeper retains a right of access AND all five listed services are offered. Anyone outside those exclusions is a 'tenant' for s1161 purposes. s1162(a) gives the three residential service methods; s1162(b)-(c) are commercial and out of scope. Note s1946.1(f) permits certified or registered mail as an ALTERNATIVE to s1162 service for a periodic-tenancy termination, whereas s1162 does not list mail alone as a method - the two regimes differ and must not be merged in the tracker. INTERACTION NOT RESOLVED: s1946.2(c) requires a cure opportunity 'pursuant to paragraph (3) of Section 1161' before a just-cause termination for a curable breach; how that sequences against a s1161(4) no-cure ground has not been worked through. | CA: Content from notice-service-fee-ban-ca (switched off) added by the three-bucket scrub (2026-09-29); unchanged: Civ. Code §1946.1(i); CCP §1161(6); CCP §1161; Civ. Code §1946(b). | CA: ADDED 2026-10-03, SOP 1.31 retro check 9 (rule 45). Civ. Code s1633.3 read SECTION-OPEN on leginfo 2026-10-03 - the electronic-transactions act itself, not merely the landlord-tenant section that refers to it, which is what rule 45 requires. s1633.3(c) ends with a free-standing sentence: 'An electronic record may not be substituted for any notice that is required to be sent pursuant to Section 1162 of the Code of Civil Procedure.' That is an exclusion for exactly the notices rule 45 names (eviction, default, cure). Two further landlord-tenant exclusions in the same subdivision, recorded here because no other CA row carries them: Civ. Code s1950.6 (application screening fees - though s1950.6(d) and (f) supply their own email routes by agreement, see edu-screening-fee-ca) and Civ. Code s1983 (the abandoned-property notice, see edu-abandoned-property-ca). s1633.3(b)(4) also takes the act off any law requiring specifically identifiable text to be separately signed or initialled. CLAUSE SCREEN, run the same day: NO CA-tagged clause relies on electronic delivery of a s1162 notice. The shared `notices` row defers twice over - 'Where applicable law requires a particular method, form, timing, or content for a notice, that requirement will control over this Section, and nothing in this Lease designates an alternative method of delivery for any notice governed by law' - and `electronic-signatures` consents only to electronic execution of the Lease itself, which the act permits. NOT READ: ss1633.5 (variation by agreement) and 1633.8, and the Judicial Council's electronic-service rules.

title: Who counts as a tenant, and which occupancies fall outside the chapter
bodyText: California's residential landlord-tenant chapter applies to everyone who hires a dwelling unit in the state, including tenants, lessees, boarders and lodgers, however they are described in the agreement. A dwelling unit means a structure or part of a structure used as a home, residence or sleeping place by one person maintaining a household or by two or more people maintaining a common household. Two occupancies are outside the chapter: transient occupancy in a hotel, motel, residence club or similar facility where the stay is subject to transient occupancy tax, and occupancy at a hotel or motel where the innkeeper keeps a right of access to and control of the unit and the establishment offers all of five services to every resident - personal property safekeeping, central telephone service under filed tariffs, maid, mail and room services, occupancy for periods of less than seven days, and food service from an establishment on or next to the premises connected to the innkeeper. Unless a particular provision says otherwise by its own terms, the chapter's provisions apply to a tenancy in a dwelling unit.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1940, read section-open 2026-09-19, together with s1961 for the separate Chapter 4 disclosure scope. Matters for a property-management product because it decides whether the whole CA clause set applies at all. s1940(a) reaches 'boarders, lodgers, and others, HOWEVER DENOMINATED', so calling an agreement a licence, a room-share or a lodging arrangement does not move it out of the chapter. s1940(b)(2): the hotel/motel exclusion is CONJUNCTIVE - the innkeeper must retain a right of access AND ALL FIVE services must be offered to all residents. A short-stay operator missing any one of the five is inside the chapter and owes the full CA clause set. This is the provision a short-term-rental operator is most likely to assume protects them. s1940(d) is a construction rule worth keeping: nothing limits the application of any Chapter 2 provision to a tenancy in a dwelling unit UNLESS the provision is so limited by its specific terms - i.e. read the chapter broadly by default. READING FLAGGED, NOT ASSERTED: s1940(b)(1) contains a double negative - the transient exclusion does not apply to 'a person to whom this paragraph pertains if the person has not made valid payment for all room and other related charges owing as of the last day on which his or her occupancy is or would be subject to tax'. On its face that keeps a non-paying transient OUTSIDE the chapter, but the sentence is genuinely awkward and the practical question - when a hotel guest who overstays becomes a tenant entitled to unlawful-detainer process - is the kind of thing that turns on case law. NOT researched. Do not build occupancy-type logic on this subdivision without confirming it. s1940(c)'s 'dwelling unit' definition is also the hinge for CCP s1162(c)'s commercial-tenant carve-out, so the two travel together. R&T s7280 READ 2026-09-19 and it supplies the operative line: s7280(a) authorises the tax on occupancy of a hotel, inn, tourist home, motel or other lodging 'UNLESS THE OCCUPANCY IS FOR A PERIOD OF MORE THAN 30 DAYS'. Because s1940(b)(1) excludes occupancy that IS OR WOULD BE subject to that tax, the 30-day line governs even in a jurisdiction that never levied one. So a stay of MORE THAN 30 DAYS is outside the transient exclusion and inside Chapter 2, subject still to the separate s1940(b)(2) five-service hotel exclusion. That is the concrete boundary a short-stay operator needs. s7280(c) also sweeps campground and RV-park spaces into 'other lodging', while excluding local-government facilities, time-share owner occupancy and s7282 campsites. The s1940(b)(1) non-payment double negative flagged above is a SEPARATE question and is still unresolved. EXCEPTION ADDED 2026-09-19: Civ. Code s1940.1 bars requiring a residential hotel occupant to move or check out and re-register before 30 days for the purpose of preserving transient status, with a rebuttable presumption of that purpose from any required check-out ($500 civil penalty). And Civ. Code s1954.071 moves the line from 30 days to 270 for DISASTER-DISPLACED guests until 2031-01-01 - see edu-disaster-displaced-guests-ca.

title: Reusable tenant screening reports
bodyText: California lets a rental applicant supply a reusable tenant screening report - a consumer report prepared within the previous 30 days at the applicant's own request and expense, made available to the landlord at no cost either directly or through a third-party service. Such a report must include the applicant's name and contact information, verification of employment, last known address, and the results of an eviction history check, and must state prominently the date through which its information is current. A landlord is not required to accept these reports. A landlord who does accept them may ask the applicant to confirm that nothing in the report has materially changed, but may not charge that applicant any fee to access the report and may not charge an application screening fee at all. Where a local ordinance conflicts with these rules, whichever gives applicants greater protection applies.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1950.1, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (added by AB 2559, Stats. 2022 ch. 288, eff. 2023-01-01). Closes the s1950.6(g) dependency. THE DECISION POINT IS BINARY AND HAS A PRICE: s1950.1(h) says a landlord need not accept reusable reports, but s1950.1(d) provides that IF the landlord accepts them and an applicant supplies one, the landlord may charge NEITHER an access fee NOR an application screening fee - 'notwithstanding Section 1950.6'. So electing to accept them forfeits screening-fee revenue from every applicant who brings one. The app should surface this as a landlord-level setting, not a per-application choice. s1950.1(e)(6): the report must have been prepared WITHIN THE PREVIOUS 30 DAYS, at the applicant's request AND EXPENSE, and be available to the landlord AT NO COST - a report the landlord must pay to access is not a reusable screening report and does not trigger the fee ban. s1950.1(g) is a one-way local-preemption rule: where a local policy conflicts, whichever gives APPLICANTS GREATER PROTECTION applies. Third CA provision found deferring to the municipal layer, after s1946.2(i) and s1947.12(d)(3), and it reinforces edu-municipal-layer-ca. UNREAD AREA SURFACED BY s1950.1(f): criminal-history consideration in housing is governed by 2 CCR Art. 24, s12264 et seq. (Civil Rights Council again) plus local ordinances. That is an entire tenant-screening regulatory area this pass has NOT touched and it is not in the canvass. Flagging it as a gap-discovery find, not resolving it.

title: Nuisance-based eviction and the city-prosecutor assignment
bodyText: California deems certain conduct a nuisance for the purpose of a three-day notice to quit, but the provisions are narrower than they appear. Using a building or property for dogfighting or cockfighting is a public nuisance statewide. A separate controlled-substance eviction procedure lets a city prosecutor or city attorney bring an unlawful detainer action, but it operates only in the City of Los Angeles. Under that procedure the prosecutor must first give the owner 30 calendar days' written notice requiring the owner to act, and the owner must within 30 days either supply all relevant information or give a written safety-related explanation together with an assignment of the right to bring the action. Accepting the assignment can cost the owner up to $600 in investigation, discovery and attorney's fees. If the owner does not act, or does not prosecute the action diligently and in good faith, the prosecutor may file and join the owner as a defendant, and on a finding of unlawful detainer the prosecutor's costs may be assessed against the owner and recorded as a lien on the property. The court may order a partial eviction removing only the person involved and barring their return, rather than ending the whole tenancy.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss3482.8, 3485 and 3486, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. These are the three sections CCP s1161(4) incorporates as deemed nuisances. Reading them changes what that limb is worth. s3482.8 (added SB 426, eff. 2012-01-01): dogfighting under Pen. Code s597.5 or cockfighting under s597b(b) - STATEWIDE, and the only one of the three that is. s3486: controlled-substance purpose, defined at s3486(c) by a long list of H&S Code offences. s3486(g): 'This section applies ONLY IN THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES to a court having jurisdiction over unlawful detainer cases involving real property situated in the CITY OF LOS ANGELES.' s3486(h) further conditioned its 2014 operativity on the City of LA's reporting compliance. s3485 (unlawful weapons or ammunition): APPEARS REPEALED. s3485(j) reads 'This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2024, and as of that date is repealed', and the codifier's annotation says 'Repealed as of January 1, 2024, by its own provisions.' Corroborating but not conclusive: the text supplied is served as the 2022 California Code while ss3482.8 and 3486 came as 2025, which is what a publisher does when a section has left the current code. Same evidentiary posture as s2924.85 - strong, one notch below CITED. CONFIRM against the current Civil Code index at sync. SECOND INSTANCE OF CROSS-REFERENCE ROT IN CA, and worse than the 2 CCR s12178(f) case: there the target existed but had been re-lettered; here the target is GONE, and CCP s1161(4) was amended by SB 611 in 2024 and made operative 2025-02-01 while still citing it. LANDLORD EXPOSURE is the reason this is an education row rather than a footnote: s3486(a)(1)(E) puts up to $600 of the prosecutor's costs on the owner upon acceptance of an assignment, and s3486(a)(3) assesses the prosecutor's costs against the DEFENDANT OWNER with an abstract of judgment becoming A LIEN ON THE PROPERTY. An owner who ignores a 30-day notice can be joined as a defendant in an action against their own tenant. s3486(b) partial eviction: the court may remove and permanently bar an individual, including a household member, without terminating the tenancy, and may condition the remaining tenancy on the others not inviting that person back. s3486(f)(2)(B) gives the tenant an extreme-hardship stay on clear and convincing evidence, expressly NOT available on economic hardship alone. s3486(a)(5) preserves CCP s1179 relief from forfeiture - NOT READ. TYPE SIZE AND TRANSLATION AGAIN: s3486(a)(1)(C) requires the tenant notice in at least 14-POINT BOLD TYPE and in English plus all the s1632 languages. Fifth type-size floor found in CA and a third s1632 linkage - though this notice is the prosecutor's to serve, not the landlord's, so it is not lease content. s3485 EVIDENCE UPGRADED 2026-09-19, WITH A CAVEAT THE s2924.85 REPEAL DOES NOT CARRY: AB 2930 (Stats. 2018 ch. 880) as enacted on leginfo sunsets s3485 on 2024-01-01; the federal OJP National Gang Center legislation index, citing LexisNexis, lists it 'Repealed effective January 1, 2024'; Justia's latest version is 2022. BUT s3485 HAS BEEN REPEALED AND REVIVED BEFORE - AB 1013 (2007), AB 530 (2009), AB 2310 (2014, re-adding it after a lapse) and AB 2930 (2018). The 2014 revival came AFTER a lapse, so a post-2024 revival is plausible on the section's own history. Two targeted searches found every prior revival and NONE after 2018; per the two-attempt rule the search stopped there. Treat as repealed, but this is the one row in the CA set where a legal-watch hit is genuinely likely: watch for any bill adding s3485 to the Civil Code. FULL s3485 TEXT READ 2026-09-19 (2022 version, the last published): s3485(j) confirms the 2024-01-01 sunset from the section's own words, not just the enacting bill. SCOPE WHILE IN FORCE, s3485(f): only courts with unlawful detainer jurisdiction over property in the CITIES OF LOS ANGELES, LONG BEACH, SACRAMENTO AND OAKLAND - four cities, against s3486's one. So the named-locality pattern is stronger than recorded: both sibling sections were city-confined, to different city lists. While operative it also required a tenant notice in at least 14-POINT BOLD type, translated into every s1632(b) language, and conditioned the prosecutor's standing on annual reporting to the California Research Bureau (s3485(g)-(i)). This text does NOT resolve the revival caveat: a 2022 version shows what was repealed, not whether anything was re-added after 2024. The legal-watch item stands. REVIVAL CAVEAT NARROWED 2026-09-19: Justia's code pages are published by code year, and the s3485 page Taylor supplied is headed '2022 California Code' while every current section in this pass is headed '2025 California Code'. A section re-added by any 2023-2025 enactment would carry a later-year page. So no revival through the 2025 code year; only the CURRENT (2026) legislative session remains unchecked. Treated as repealed.

title: Permitted Payment Methods
bodyText: Tenant may pay Rent and the Security Deposit by the following methods: [list the accepted methods, including at least one that is neither cash nor electronic funds transfer]. If Tenant attempts to pay with a check drawn on insufficient funds or instructs the drawee to stop payment, Landlord may require cash as the only form of payment for up to three months, after giving Tenant written notice that the instrument was dishonored, stating the length of the cash-only period, and attaching a copy of the dishonored instrument.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1947.3, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended by SB 611, Stats. 2024 ch. 287, eff. 2025-01-01). Blocks two base rows - see the CA extend manifest. s1947.3(a)(1): at least one form of payment that is NEITHER CASH NOR ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFER must be allowed, so an electronic-only or cash-only rent policy is unlawful from the outset. s1947.3(d) defines EFT broadly enough to catch ACH, card, telephone and recurring transfers, and even 'transfers initiated electronically that deliver a paper instrument'. s1947.3(a)(2): cash-exclusive is permitted ONLY after a dishonored check or a stop-payment instruction, ONLY for up to THREE MONTHS, and only with a written notice that states the dishonour, states the period, and ATTACHES A COPY of the instrument - and it must comply with s827 if it changes the lease terms. s1947.3(a)(3): third-party rent payment must be allowed, subject to a signed acknowledgment; the statute supplies a substantially-prescribed form, and failure to supply it voids the landlord's obligation to accept. s1947.3(a)(3)(E) preserves the landlord's freedom not to enter a Section 8 contract. s1947.3(b): NO FEE for payment by check, for rent or security deposit. Distinct from the s1719 returned-instrument service charge - do not conflate. s1947.3(f): waiver void. SUPERSEDES acceptable-payment-methods (link set 2026-09-19; the manifest recorded the replacement but the field was never populated - the only broken link of the 19 base-to-CA replacements). | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's accepted methods and cash-only right; the statutory method rule is now a bracket prompt, and the third-party payment and no-check-fee duties moved to edu-payment-methods-ca.

title: Political Signs
bodyText: Tenant may post or display political signs relating to an election or legislative vote, the initiative, referendum or recall process, or issues before a public commission, board or elected local body. In a multifamily dwelling such signs may be posted in the window or on the door of the premises; in a single-family dwelling they may also be posted from the yard, window, door, balcony or outside wall. Landlord may prohibit a political sign only if it is more than six square feet in size, if posting it would violate a local, state or federal law, or if it would violate a lawful provision of a common interest development governing document. Tenant will post and remove political signs within the time limits set by any local ordinance, or otherwise within the period Landlord reasonably establishes, which will begin at least 90 days before the election or vote and end at least 15 days after it.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1940.4, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (added SB 337, eff. 2012-01-01). CONFIRMS the suspicion raised on the extend screen's eyeball pass: the base row common-area-use bars 'any sign, banner, or advertisement visible from outside the property without Landlord's consent', which s1940.4(a) makes unlawful as applied to political signs. common-area-use is BLOCKED for CA. The permitted display locations differ by dwelling type - window or door only in multifamily, but also yard, balcony and outside wall for a single-family dwelling - so the builder needs the property type to render this correctly. Only three grounds for prohibition, and size is a hard number: SIX SQUARE FEET. s1940.4(d) makes the TENANT solely responsible for any local-ordinance violation. s1940.4(e): a change of terms made to implement this section, noticed under s827, is NOT a diminution in housing services - which matters under a local just-cause ordinance. s1353.6, cross-referenced at s1940.4(c)(3), NOT READ. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-tenant-display-and-use-rights-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Waterbeds and Liquid-Filled Bedding
bodyText: If the structure received its valid certificate of occupancy after January 1, 1973, Landlord will not refuse to rent to Tenant, or refuse to continue renting to Tenant, solely because Tenant has a waterbed or other liquid-filled bedding, provided Tenant meets the requirements of Civil Code section 1940.5. Those include furnishing Landlord, before installation, a waterbed insurance policy for property damage of at least $100,000 written by a carrier licensed in California and maintained until the bedding is removed; conforming to the floor load capacity and distributing the weight on a pedestal or frame substantially the dimensions of the mattress; installing, maintaining and removing the bedding per manufacturer, retailer or state standards, whichever is safest; and giving Landlord 24 hours' written notice before installing, removing or moving it. Landlord may inspect the installation on notice under Civil Code section 1954, may increase the security deposit by one-half of one month's rent, and may charge a reasonable administration fee.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1940.5, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. CONFIRMS the second suspicion from the extend screen's eyeball pass: common-area-use bans waterbeds outright, which s1940.5 forbids for any structure whose valid certificate of occupancy issued AFTER 1973-01-01. common-area-use is BLOCKED for CA on this ground as well as the political-sign ground. s1940.5(g) is a DEPOSIT-CAP EXCEPTION and is cross-noted at edu-security-deposit-cap-ca: 'notwithstanding Section 1950.5' the owner may increase the deposit by one-half of one month's rent, plus a reasonable administration fee. A third exception to the AB 12 cap. s1940.5(f): the inspection right is expressly SUBJECT TO s1954 NOTICE, and non-conforming installation gets a three-day notice to conform or remove unless there is immediate danger to the structure. The insurance limb cross-references s1962 and s1962.5 for application content; s1962.5 NOT READ. Pre-1973 structures are outside the section entirely, so a ban there is unaffected - the builder needs the certificate-of-occupancy date, which the app does not currently capture. | CA: SOP 1.31 retro check 24 (rule 78), 2026-10-03: pointer repointed. Found by the full sweep, not by the prompt's list.

title: Holdover
bodyText: If Tenant does not vacate the property by the end of the Term, Landlord may pursue any remedy allowed by law to recover possession and may recover the actual damages caused by Tenant's continued possession, including the reasonable rental value of the property for the period Tenant remains. Alternatively, Landlord may accept Tenant's continued payment of Rent, in which case this Lease will continue on a month-to-month basis on the same terms, terminable only as provided by law.
notes: CA: written 2026-09-19 to replace the base holdover row for California. CCP s1174 read section-open. CALIFORNIA SUPPLIES NO HOLDOVER MULTIPLIER, so the base row's 'holdover damages in the maximum amount permitted by applicable law for each day' resolves to NOTHING in CA - the same empty-referent defect that forced holdover-oh and holdover-sd. s1174(b) awards ACTUAL damages including rent found due, plus STATUTORY DAMAGES OF UP TO $600 only where MALICE IS SHOWN. That $600 is a court-awarded figure on a malice finding, NOT a per-day amount a lease can stipulate, and it must not be drafted as one. A stipulated per-day holdover charge would itself be liquidated damages under s1671(d) and void absent the impracticability showing, so California is doubly constrained here: no statute to point at, and a stated figure faces s1671(d). Body text therefore claims actual damages and reasonable rental value only. The month-to-month limb is deliberately 'terminable only as provided by law' rather than 'on written notice', because s1946.1 and s1946.2 both govern once the tenancy converts. s1951.5 RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (primary text supplied): it reads in its entirety 'Section 1671, relating to liquidated damages, applies to a lease of real property.' CONFIRMATORY, NOT CORRECTIVE, as predicted - s1671(c)(2) already reached a lease of real property for use as a dwelling on its own terms, and s1951.5 removes any argument that s1671 is confined to contracts for goods and services. No change to this row's analysis; the earlier flag is cleared. MALICIOUS HOLDOVER, added 2026-09-19: CCP s1174(b) - where the defendant is found guilty of unlawful detainer and MALICE is shown, the landlord may be awarded STATUTORY DAMAGES UP TO $600 in addition to actual damages including rent found due. The trier of fact decides which. A landlord remedy, not lease text. | TX: Read in full 2026-09-25 against Tex. Prop. Code chs. 24, 54, 91, 92 and 301 (official statutes.capitol.texas.gov text for chs. 24/54/91/301). Applies as written. No Texas holdover multiplier in chs. 24, 91 or 92 (full read), so the base 'holdover' row's 'maximum amount permitted by law' has no referent (K.3) - not tagged. This row's actual-damages / reasonable-rental-value measure and month-to-month conversion fit Texas; month-to-month termination is s91.001 (one month's notice, or as the parties agree in a signed instrument). | GA: Tagged instead of the base `holdover` (K.3). Georgia has no statutory holdover multiplier: confirmed absent statute-wide (official full-text search 2026-09-28: holdover, 'holding over', 'at sufferance' near rent, damages, double or mesne profits), so the base's 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' has no referent. A tenancy continued without a set term is a tenancy at will: 60 days' notice from the landlord, 30 from the tenant (O.C.G.A. §§ 44-7-6, 44-7-7), which 'terminable only as provided by law' picks up. A stipulated daily holdover rate (as in the Georgia REALTORS lease) would be liquidated damages under O.C.G.A. § 13-6-7; offered as the opt-in `holdover-rate-ga` (Taylor decision 2026-09-28, GA log §6.2). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NC: Tagged instead of the base `holdover` (K.3). North Carolina has no statutory holdover multiplier (confirmed absent, full-text search 2026-09-28; edu-no-holdover-multiplier-nc): a holdover is removed by summary ejectment (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-26(a)(1)) and the landlord may claim 'damages for the occupation of the premises since the cessation of the estate' (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-28); occupation by permission without agreed rent yields 'reasonable compensation' (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-4). The base's 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' therefore has no referent. A month-to-month tenancy ends on 7 days' notice (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-14), which 'terminable only as provided by law' picks up; the opt-in periodic-tenancy-notice-nc lets the parties agree a longer period. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | TN: Tagged 2026-09-28 (section text read 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser (Justia host copy of the 2025 Tennessee Code with history lines; 2025-2026 public chapters screened; TN log §1)). Tagged in place of the base holdover (K.3: the base's 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' has no Tennessee figure). Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-512(c) (Act counties): possession, back rent, fees and other lease damages; actual damages if willful. Pairs with holdover-rate-tn. TN-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. | VA: Tagged 2026-09-28. VA-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. Read against the official Code of Virginia section-open (law.lis.virginia.gov; VA log §1). Basis: Tagged in place of the base holdover (K.3: the base's 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' has no Virginia figure unless the lease adopts the § 55.1-1253(C) liquidated amount). Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1253(C)-(D): possession plus actual damages, fees and costs; holdover with consent continues on the lease terms with rent change on 30 days' written notice. Opt-in liquidated damages: holdover-rate-va. | ID: Used instead of the base holdover row: the base's 'holdover damages in the maximum amount permitted by applicable law' would point at Idaho Code § 6-317, under which a court may enter judgment for three times the actual damages in an unlawful-detainer action (rule 53). This variant claims actual damages and reasonable rental value only. The month-to-month limb is 'terminable only as provided by law' (Idaho Code § 55-208, one month's written notice). Read section-open 2026-09-30 from legislature.idaho.gov (ID log s1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IN: Applies as written. No Indiana holdover statute or double-rent measure (IN battery 34: 19 sections, none a residential holdover rule); a general tenancy by the landlord's consent is month to month (Ind. Code § 32-31-1-2). Optional companion: holdover-rate-in. Read section-open 2026-09-30 from iga.in.gov (IN log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | OK: Used instead of the base: the base claims holdover damages 'in the maximum amount permitted by applicable law for each day', but Oklahoma's statutory extra measure applies only to a willful holdover not in good faith (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(D): not more than twice the average monthly rental, prorated daily), so the base states an amount and trigger the statute does not give (rule 53). holdover-ca claims actual damages including rental value, matching Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(D) ('an action for possession and damages'); its month-to-month sentence is the parties' agreement that Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(D) allows ('unless the parties otherwise agree') and displaces the older presumption of renewal for up to a year on acceptance of rent (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 35). edu-holdover-ok. Read section-open 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 from oklegislature.gov (OK log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MI: Applies as written in place of the base. Michigan sets no statutory holdover multiplier (MI battery 63); a landlord who wins possession may recover damages from the notice to quit or demand for possession (Mich. Comp. Laws § 600.5750). Its month-to-month sentence is the parties' agreement; a month-to-month tenancy ends on the notice Mich. Comp. Laws § 554.134(1) sets. edu-holdover-mi. Read section-open 2026-10-01 from legislature.mi.gov (MI log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written: tracks NRS 118A.470 (actual damages; landlord-consented holdover is month to month on the same terms). Chosen over base holdover, whose "maximum amount permitted by law" figure has no located NV referent - the empty-referent defect this row was written to cure in CA. PROVISIONAL pending NRS Ch. 40 (any holdover multiplier there would add to, not contradict, this text). | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): PROVISIONAL CLEARED. NRS 40.250: a fixed term ends without notice. NRS 40.360(2): in an unlawful-detainer judgment the court awards rent plus THREE TIMES the damages assessed. As in CA, that is a court-awarded measure, not a per-day figure a lease can stipulate; the clause's "any remedy allowed by law" preserves it. | NV (retro SOP 1.27, 2026-10-02): Rule 37: NRS 118A.470(2) makes a consented holdover week to week where rent is payable weekly and month to month otherwise, on the same terms 'unless specifically agreed otherwise'. The clause's 'month-to-month' is the statute's answer for monthly rent, which is every Steinoak lease; a weekly-rent lease type would need its own wording. Choice made on purpose (rule 50). Read section-open 2026-10-02 in Taylor's built-in browser from leg.state.nv.us (Nevada Revised Statutes 2025/2026 R1; the relied-on chapter pages print Rev. 4/15/2026 and the 36th Special Session (2025) amended none of the sections relied on; whole NRS loaded, 835 chapter pages, 49,746 sections, parser checked complete against every chapter's table of contents); each relied-on section saved with a SHA-256 match to the browser text (NV retro sources). | AL: Tagged instead of `holdover` (K.3). Alabama's statutory holdover recovery is lump-sum, not per-day: possession, and if the holdover is willful and not in good faith the greater of three months' periodic rent or actual damages, plus reasonable attorney's fees (Ala. Code § 35-9A-441(c)); if the landlord consents, the tenancy becomes periodic (Ala. Code § 35-9A-161(d)). Older double-rent sections (Ala. Code § 6-6-314; Ala. Code § 35-9-100(3)) and their interplay with the Act (Ala. Code § 35-9A-121) are case-law questions, not relied on: `edu-holdover-remedies-al`. Opt-in daily charge: `holdover-rate-al` (Taylor decision 2). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. AL basis (SOP 1.32 rule 79, 2026-10-03): every Alabama section cited in this segment read section-open on ALISON (official Code of Alabama, current versions after the 2026-10-01 effective date; text saved and SHA-256 matched, AL retro sources); cited subdivisions and qualifiers checked against the text. | IL: Tagged. holdover not tagged: its 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' states only a ceiling (rule 53). Illinois sets its own measures (double yearly value after written demand for a willful holdover, 735 ILCS 5/9-202; double rent after the tenant's own notice, 735 ILCS 5/9-203); this clause does not waive them (edu-holdover-damages-il). Both measures are conditional (willful holdover after written demand; holdover after the tenant's own notice), so the optional holdover-rate-il, placed after this clause, sets a daily charge for the other holdovers (IL retro 2026-10-03, SOP 1.39 fix 3). Month-to-month notice: periodic-tenancy-notice-il. Read section-open 2026-09-30 (IL log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MO: Tagged instead of the base holdover, whose 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' would point at Missouri's double measures (double the yearly value after demand and written notice, Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.080; double rent after the tenant's own notice to quit, Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.100; double damages and double monthly rents in an unlawful detainer judgment, Mo. Rev. Stat. § 534.330), each with its own trigger, which the base clause's 'after the end of the Term' wording does not match (rule 53). The statutory measures remain available by statute (edu-holdover-damages-mo). Optional companion for the cases those conditional measures leave out (good-faith holdover, days before a written demand, holdover ended without judgment): holdover-rate-mo (MO retro, SOP 1.42). Accepting Rent creates a month-to-month tenancy ended only on Missouri's notice (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.060(4)(1)). Read section-open 2026-09-30 (MO log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | PA: Tagged. K.3: Pennsylvania has no holdover multiplier; judgment is for 'damages, if any, for the unjust detention' plus rent (68 P.S. § 250.503(a)(2)-(3), Act § 503), matching actual damages / reasonable rental value. Opt-in `holdover-rate-pa`. 'Terminable only as provided by law': Pennsylvania sets only the landlord's notice to quit (68 P.S. § 250.501(b), Act § 501(b): fifteen days for a term of one year or less or an indeterminate term); the tenant's notice comes from `periodic-tenancy-notice-pa` (lease term). The base `holdover` was not tagged because its 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' has no Pennsylvania measure. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. PA basis (SOP 1.49 rule 79, 2026-10-03): section-open, official text on palegis.us (68 P.S. § 250.503(a)(2)-(3) (Act § 503); 68 P.S. § 250.501(b) (Act § 501(b)); 1951 Act text hash-matched to the live page, 72 of 72 sections); cited subdivision and qualifiers confirmed. | SC: Tagged instead of the base `holdover` (K.3): South Carolina's holdover recovery is statutory, not a per-day figure: attorney's fees if the holdover is not in good faith; if wilful, up to the greater of three months' periodic rent or twice actual damages (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-770(c)); see `edu-holdover-remedies-sc`. Month-to-month continuation ends on 30 days' written notice (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-770(b)). Opt-in daily rate `holdover-rate-sc` (decision 1). Basis (rule 79, SC retro 1.50): 27-40-770 read section-open 2026-10-04 in the built-in browser from the official South Carolina Code of Laws on scstatehouse.gov (site current through the 2025 session; each section saved and SHA-256 matched to the browser, SC retro 1.50 sources); the cited subdivisions and every qualifier checked against the text. | UT: A fixed term ends without notice (Utah Code Ann. § 78B-6-802(1)(a)); 'terminable only as provided by law' reads with periodic-tenancy-notice-ut. The base holdover is not tagged: 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' would point at the Utah Code Ann. § 78B-6-811(3) treble-damages judgment (K.3). Pairs with holdover-rate-ut (optional daily charge for holdover days outside an eviction case, never claimed in one; retro 2026-10-04, UT log 'Retro checks (SOP 1.53)') and edu-holdover-damages-ut. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | WV: Tagged as written (tag-first screen, rules 26-28, WV log §2.1): A tenant who stays after the right has expired is in unlawful detainer, with damages including mesne profits (W. Va. Code §§ 55-3-1, 55-3-2; `edu-holdover-wv`), which 'actual damages ... including the reasonable rental value' matches; no statutory multiple (WV battery b-holdover-rate (double rent or a multiple of rent for holding over): 3 hits, control 0; known positives passed (0 real sections, 1 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205). The month-to-month tenancy is 'terminable only as provided by law': W. Va. Code § 37-6-5, or the special agreement in `termination-notice-wv` where used. Not tagged: `holdover` (ceiling-only 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' with no West Virginia measure, rule 53). Read section-open 2026-10-05 from the saved, hash-matched corpus of the whole West Virginia Code and the West Virginia Constitution (WV log §1). Rule 15: written section-open. | MA: Tagged as written (tag-first screen, rules 26-28, MA log §2.1). Actual damages and reasonable rental value match Massachusetts: under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 3 tenants at sufferance 'shall be liable to pay rent therefor for such time as they may occupy or detain the same'; under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 1 possession is recovered through summary process after a lease ends 'by its own limitation'. Accepting rent after the Term creates a tenancy at will, terminable by the notice in § 12; the clause's "terminable only as provided by law" defers to it. Rule 15: written section-open. | CT: Tagged as written (tag-first screen, rules 26-28, CT log §2.1). Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-3d (holding over not evidence of a new lease) and § 47a-26b (court-ordered use and occupancy payments during a summary process action, at the last agreed rent or fair rental value) fit the clause's actual-damages measure; the month-to-month option on accepted rent is the landlord's election. See `edu-holdover-ct`. Rule 15: written section-open. | RI: Tagged as written (tag-first screen, rules 26-28, RI log §2.1). Fits § 34-18-43 (after termination the landlord has a claim 'for a sum for reasonable use and occupation') and § 34-18-38(c) (willful bad-faith holdover: up to three months' periodic rent or treble damages; with consent and no term, week-to-week if rent is paid weekly, otherwise month-to-month). The clause's month-to-month continuation assumes monthly rent, which the builder uses. No stipulated holdover rate is offered (`edu-holdover-rate-ri`). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Forfeiture election and the five-day redemption window
bodyText: In California a judgment in an unlawful detainer action declares the lease forfeited only if the three-day notice stated the landlord's election to declare a forfeiture. If the notice did not say so, the lease is not forfeited. Separately, where the action is for nonpayment of rent, the lease has not expired by its own terms and the notice did not elect forfeiture, the court may delay the writ for five days after judgment so that the tenant, a subtenant, a mortgagee or another interested party can pay the rent, damages and costs and be restored to the tenancy. That five-day delay is mandatory rather than discretionary where the lease is in writing, is for a term of more than one year, and contains no forfeiture clause.
notes: CA: CCP s1174(a) and (c), read section-open 2026-09-19. Routed to education because it governs notice drafting and post-judgment procedure rather than lease text. s1174(a) is a NOTICE-DRAFTING TRAP: omit the election to declare forfeiture from the s1161 notice and the lease survives the judgment. Belongs in the legal tracker's notice generator. s1174(c) IS A FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE OPT-IN PATTERN, and this time the opt-in runs the landlord's way: the five-day mandatory redemption window applies only where the written lease of more than one year 'DOES NOT CONTAIN A FORFEITURE CLAUSE'. Including a forfeiture clause removes the mandatory stay and leaves it discretionary. That is a real drafting decision the library currently does not surface, and it should be weighed against s1174(a)'s requirement that the notice elect forfeiture. NOT drafted as a clause here - flagged for Taylor's decision. s1174(e)-(m) carry an entire abandoned-personal-property regime cross-referencing Civ. Code ss1980-1991, with landlord non-liability safe harbours at (j)-(l). NONE OF THOSE SECTIONS READ - this is an unexplored area and the library has no CA abandoned-property row.

title: Rent Payment
bodyText: Tenant shall pay Landlord monthly rent of {{monthly_rent}} (Monthly Rent) in advance on the due date specified in this Lease, without demand. If the due date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, rent is due on the next business day. Nothing in this Lease limits Tenant's rights under Civil Code sections 1941 and 1942, including Tenant's right to repair and deduct the cost from rent.
notes: CA: overrides the base rent-payment row. The base text requires rent 'without demand, DEDUCTION, OR SETOFF'. Civ. Code s1942.1 makes any agreement waiving or modifying s1941 or s1942 rights VOID as contrary to public policy with respect to any condition rendering the premises untenantable, and s1942 is the repair-and-deduct remedy - so the deduction waiver is void as written. Removed rather than narrowed, and replaced with an express preservation, because a clause that is void in its most important application should not be shipped to tenants as though it bound them. 'Without demand' is retained and is unaffected. Note also that CCP s1161(2) requires a rent notice to state the amount due, which a disputed setoff complicates - see edu-three-day-notice-ca. ALSO relevant, read 2026-09-19: Civ. Code s1942.4 bars a landlord from demanding or collecting rent at all, or issuing a rent increase or a three-day pay-or-quit notice, while the four conditions in s1942.4(a) coexist. See edu-rent-demand-bar-ca.

title: Existing Condition
bodyText: Tenant has examined the property and, by signing this Lease, acknowledges its condition as of the Start Date (Existing Condition), except as otherwise noted in this Lease or in any move-in inspection record. This acknowledgment does not waive or modify Landlord's obligations under Civil Code sections 1941 and 1941.1, does not apply to any condition rendering the premises untenantable, and does not affect Tenant's rights regarding any condition that existed before the tenancy began. Landlord will deliver possession of the property to Tenant on the Start Date in the same or better condition as the Existing Condition, except for ordinary wear and tear.
notes: CA: overrides the base existing-condition row. The base text has the tenant acknowledge the property is 'in good order and repair and satisfactory condition'. Under Civ. Code s1942.1 that is void as a modification of s1941 rights to the extent it reaches any condition rendering the premises untenantable. It also works against the tenant on deposits: s1950.5(e)(2)(B) bars deducting for preexisting conditions, and a blanket good-condition recital is exactly the evidence a landlord would use to defeat that bar. Rewritten to acknowledge CONDITION rather than GOOD condition, with express carve-outs. Pairs with the s1950.5(g) move-in photograph duty at edu-deposit-photo-duty-ca, which for tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01 gives both parties a better record than a recital. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Condition' -> 'Tenant Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Services and Utilities Provided
bodyText: Landlord will provide only the services and utilities expressly specified in this Lease, and as otherwise required by applicable law. Except as to any condition that renders the premises untenantable, Landlord is not liable for an interruption or insufficiency of a service or utility resulting from causes beyond Landlord's reasonable control. Nothing in this Lease waives or modifies Landlord's obligations under Civil Code sections 1941 and 1941.1 or Tenant's rights under Civil Code section 1942.
notes: CA: overrides the base services-utilities-provided row. This is the row where I first read CA as diverging from Ohio and was wrong. The base disclaimer is limited to causes beyond the landlord's reasonable control, which Civ. Code s1953(a)(5) may not reach - but s1942.1 does: an agreement modifying s1941 or s1942 rights is void with respect to any condition rendering the premises untenantable, and water, heat and electrical service are s1941.1(a)(3)-(5) tenantability items. Ohio blocked the same row outright under s5321.13(D). CA permits the NARROWER fix rather than removal, because outside tenantability the disclaimer waives no statutory right - so the clause survives with an express tenantability carve-out. This is a genuine drafting difference between the two states on identical base text. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Utilities & Services' -> 'Landlord Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Property and Common Area Use
bodyText: Tenant will not, without Landlord's written consent, drill holes, use nails, hooks, or screws on the property, or fasten anything to its fixtures, appliances, or interior or exterior surfaces. Tenant will comply with any weight restrictions on balconies or porches and will not use them to store personal belongings without Landlord's consent. Tenant will not keep any item (such as a piano or safe) whose weight Landlord has not agreed is reasonable for the floor without Landlord's prior written consent. Tenant will not burn wax candles at the property. Except for political signs Tenant may display under Civil Code section 1940.4, Tenant will not post or display any sign, banner, or advertisement visible from outside the property without Landlord's consent.
notes: CA: overrides the base common-area-use row, which carried two CA-unlawful limbs. (1) Its blanket ban on any sign visible from outside is unlawful as applied to political signs - Civ. Code s1940.4(a); carved out and cross-referenced to edu-tenant-display-and-use-rights-ca. (2) Its flat waterbed ban is barred by s1940.5 for any structure whose valid certificate of occupancy issued after 1973-01-01; the waterbed sentence is REMOVED entirely and handled by waterbed-ca, which carries the statutory conditions. The general floor-load sentence is retained because s1940.5(b) and (d) themselves make weight and placement a condition of the waterbed right. Both limbs were caught on the extend screen's eyeball pass, not by the pattern screen. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Rules & Regulations' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states). | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): reference to the political-signs clause (now education) repointed to the statute. | CA: SOP 1.31 retro check 24 (rule 78), 2026-10-03: the notes pointer still named political-signs-ca, which the 2026-09-29 scrub switched off; the bodyText reference had already been repointed to the statute. Found by the full sweep, not by the prompt's list.

title: Pet Policy
bodyText: Tenant may keep only pets identified in writing to and approved by Landlord. Tenant will pay Landlord a pet deposit, if applicable, and pet rent of {{pet_rent_amount}} per month. Tenant is responsible for all damage, waste removal, odor, and disturbance caused by a pet. Landlord may revoke approval of a pet that becomes a nuisance or safety concern. This Section does not apply to an assistance animal, meaning a service animal or a support animal that Tenant or an occupant needs as a reasonable accommodation for a disability: no pet deposit, pet rent, additional security deposit, liability insurance or other additional fee may be charged in connection with an assistance animal, and no breed, size or weight limitation applies to one. Tenant remains responsible for the cost of repairing damage an assistance animal causes, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
notes: CA: overrides the base pet-policy row, which failed for CA on four grounds. (1) 2 CCR s12185(d)(2) bars any pet deposit, pet rent, additional security deposit, liability insurance or other fee for an assistance animal, and s12185(d)(5) bars breed, size and weight limits - carve-out added, mirroring the Ohio OAC 4112-5-07(C) fix. (2) Its indemnity limb waived future claims against the landlord contrary to Civ. Code s1953(a)(2) - REMOVED. (3) Its 'without liability to Tenant' limb was exculpatory under s1953(a)(5) - REMOVED. (4) Its right to 'enter the property and remove a pet' is not among the permitted entry purposes in Civ. Code s1954(a) - REMOVED; any entry must fit s1954 and landlord-entry-ca. Pet deposits remain subject to the s1950.5(c) cap, since a pet deposit is security however denominated. ADDITIONAL CA CONSTRAINT, read 2026-09-19: Civ. Code s1942.7 makes it unlawful to advertise in a manner designed to discourage applicants whose animal is not declawed or devocalized, to refuse or deny occupancy because of a refusal to declaw or devocalize, or to REQUIRE a tenant to declaw or devocalize any animal. 'Animal' covers any mammal, bird, reptile or amphibian - not just cats. Civil penalty up to $1,000 per advertisement or per animal, enforced by a city attorney, district attorney or other prosecutor. Screen any CA pet clause or listing for a declaw requirement.

title: Amounts Due at Signing
bodyText: Tenant will pay Landlord the following amounts, at the time specified for each: first month's Monthly Rent ({{monthly_rent}}) due at signing, and the Security Deposit ({{security_deposit}}) due at signing. These amounts are due in addition to, and are not credited against, Rent due for any other month of the Term.
notes: CA: overrides the base due-at-signing row, whose worked example collected a PET DEPOSIT and LAST MONTH'S RENT alongside the security deposit. Civ. Code s1950.5(b) defines security as any payment to secure performance 'however denominated', so both count toward the one-month cap in s1950.5(c)(1) - the base example invites an unlawful overcollection at the moment of signing, which is also the moment s1950.5(c)(6) fixes as the operative date. Prepaid last month's rent removed from the example entirely; landlords wanting advance rent should use the s1950.5(c)(2) route (six or more months' rent on a lease of at least six months), which is a different mechanism with a different test. Exceptions to the cap that the builder must still handle: s1950.5(c)(5) two-month small-landlord exception (disapplied for service members), and s1940.5(g) half-month waterbed increase. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): removed the restated deposit-cap sentence (edu-security-deposit-cap-ca).

title: Early Termination
bodyText: This Section applies to a tenancy for a fixed Term. If the tenancy is month-to-month or another periodic tenancy, the Month-to-Month Termination Notice Section governs ending it instead, and the damages described below do not apply because there is no balance of a Term. Tenant may terminate this Lease before the end of the Term by giving Landlord at least 30 days' written notice. Tenant remains responsible for Rent and other obligations up to the termination date. If this Lease terminates because Tenant breaches it and abandons the property, or because Landlord terminates Tenant's right to possession for breach, Landlord may recover the damages provided by Civil Code section 1951.2. Those damages include the worth at the time of award of the amount by which the unpaid rent for the balance of the Term after the time of award exceeds the amount of the rental loss that Tenant proves could be reasonably avoided. Unpaid rent earned before termination, and rent that would have been earned between termination and the award, shall bear interest at {{judgment_interest_rate}} or, if no rate is stated, at the legal rate. Landlord may terminate this Lease early only as permitted by law, including, where this property is subject to Civil Code section 1946.2, only for a just cause stated in the notice of termination, and only after giving Tenant an opportunity to cure where the law requires one. Nothing in this Section limits any right either party has under applicable law, including Tenant's right to terminate without penalty due to active military service, or due to the property becoming uninhabitable through no fault of Tenant.
notes: CA: overrides the base early-termination row, which failed for CA on two grounds. (1) Its early termination fee - 'one month's Rent or 30% of the remaining Rent, WHICHEVER IS GREATER' - is a liquidated damages provision in a residential lease. Civ. Code s1671(c)(2) routes it to s1671(d), where it is VOID unless actual damage would have been impracticable or extremely difficult to fix, and a whichever-is-greater formula is a penalty on its face. Replaced with an actual-damages-less-mitigation measure. (2) Its landlord limb let Landlord terminate on 30 days' notice for a material breach cured within 10 days, which ignores s1946.2 just cause, the s1946.2(c) cure requirement keyed to CCP s1161(3), and the s1946.1 notice periods. Rewritten to defer to law rather than state its own timetable. The death-of-tenant clause in the base row was dropped as unverified for CA rather than carried over. Civ. Code s1951.2 (landlord's damages on abandonment and the duty to mitigate) has NOT been read and is the section that would confirm the actual-damages measure - flag before this row is relied on. UPDATED 2026-09-19 after reading Civ. Code s1951.2, which the earlier flag said was needed - and the flag was right. s1951.2(c)(1) makes the (a)(3) measure - future rent for the BALANCE OF THE TERM AFTER AWARD, less avoidable loss - available ONLY IF THE LEASE SO PROVIDES, or (c)(2) only if the lessor relet before award and proves good-faith mitigation. My first draft said 'actual damages reduced by reasonable efforts to re-rent', which tracks (a)(2) but SILENTLY FORFEITED (a)(3). The statutory recital is now in the body text. FIFTH INSTANCE of the opt-in landlord right pattern in CA, after s1946.2(b)(2)(A)(ii) owner move-in, CCP s1174(c) forfeiture clause, s827(a) seven-day terms-change notice and s1942.1's arbitration limb. s1951.2(b) adds a second drafting opportunity: interest on the (a)(1) and (a)(2) amounts runs at the rate SPECIFIED IN THE LEASE if lawful, else the legal rate - so a silent lease takes the legal rate by default. The (a)(3) amount is discounted at the FRB San Francisco discount rate plus 1 percent and is not lease-adjustable. Burden note: under (a)(2) and (a)(3) it is the LESSEE who must prove the loss could reasonably have been avoided. s1951.5 RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (primary text supplied): it reads in its entirety 'Section 1671, relating to liquidated damages, applies to a lease of real property.' CONFIRMATORY, NOT CORRECTIVE, as predicted - s1671(c)(2) already reached a lease of real property for use as a dwelling on its own terms, and s1951.5 removes any argument that s1671 is confined to contracts for goods and services. No change to this row's analysis; the earlier flag is cleared. STATE MILITARY RIGHT, added 2026-09-19: California has its own non-waivable military termination right, Mil. & Vet. Code s409 - no early-termination charge, prorated rent, advance rent refunded within 30 days. See military-lease-termination-ca. This row's preservation language already accommodates it. | CA: TWO FIXES 2026-10-03. (1) SOP 1.31 retro check 24 (rule 78): the dangling pointer 'See military-lease-termination-ca' repointed to edu-military-tenant-protections-ca, which carries that content after the 2026-09-29 scrub switched the clause off. (2) SOP 1.31 retro check 1 (rule 37): the clause measured the tenant's exposure on 'the balance of the Term' and recited the Civ. Code s1951.2 measure, both of which only make sense in a FIXED TERM - exactly the shape rule 37 names ('an early-termination fee measured on the remaining Rent due under the Term'). For a California month-to-month tenancy there is no balance of a term, and s1946.1(b) gives the tenant a one-tenancy-period notice right that this clause's 30 days would have overstated for a week-to-week tenancy. An opening sentence now scopes the Section to a fixed Term and routes a periodic tenancy to month-to-month-notice-ca. The s1951.2 opt-in measure, the just-cause sentence and the military and uninhabitability savings are unchanged.

title: No general right of periodic inspection
bodyText: California limits landlord entry to the purposes listed in Civil Code section 1954. A general right to conduct periodic inspections of an occupied dwelling is not among them. The only inspection the statute provides for is the initial inspection a tenant may request before the end of the tenancy under Civil Code section 1950.5(f). Entry to make necessary or agreed repairs, to supply agreed services, or to show the unit is permitted, but a lease term reserving periodic inspections has no statutory basis and any waiver of section 1954 rights is void under Civil Code section 1953(a)(1).
notes: CA: CONFIRMED ABSENT 2026-09-19 from Civ. Code s1954(a) read section-open. Exists because the base row inspection-rights grants exactly this and is BLOCKED for CA with no replacement - per the proof-of-absence standard an absence recorded only in a prose manifest is invisible to future canvasses. Caught on the extend screen's eyeball pass, not by the pattern screen. Note the practical consequence: a CA landlord wanting a mid-tenancy condition check must fit it to a s1954(a) purpose, and s1953(a)(1) means the tenant cannot agree otherwise.

title: Damages when a tenant breaches and abandons
bodyText: When a tenant breaches the lease and abandons, or the landlord ends the tenant's right to possession for breach, California lets the landlord recover unpaid rent earned before termination, the rent that would have been earned between termination and the award less whatever loss the tenant proves could reasonably have been avoided, and any other detriment proximately caused by the breach. Recovering rent for the balance of the term after the award is different: it is available only if the lease expressly provides for it, or if the landlord re-rented the property before the award and proves the re-rental was reasonable and in good faith. Interest on the pre-award amounts runs at the rate stated in the lease if lawful, otherwise at the legal rate. Making efforts to re-rent does not waive the landlord's right to damages.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1951.2, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. Routed to education alongside the lease clause because the mechanics are litigation measures rather than lease terms. s1951.2(c)(1) is the OPT-IN: without the recital the landlord loses the post-award balance-of-term measure entirely unless it relet before award under (c)(2) - and (c)(2) recovery is itself 'subject to any limitations specified in the lease', so a badly drafted cap can bind the landlord on that route too. s1951.2(b): interest on (a)(1) and (a)(2) at the lease rate if lawful, else the legal rate; the (a)(3) amount is discounted at the FRB San Francisco discount rate PLUS 1 PERCENT and is not lease-adjustable. s1951.2(a)(2)-(3): the burden of proving avoidable loss is on the LESSEE, which is more landlord-favourable than a general duty-to-mitigate framing suggests. s1951.2(d): mitigation efforts do not waive damages. s1951.2(e) preserves the lessor's right to INDEMNIFICATION for pre-termination personal injury or property damage liability 'where the lease provides for such indemnification' - a sixth opt-in, but it sits in tension with s1953(a)(2) (waiver of future causes of action void) depending on whether the indemnity runs to third-party liability or to the tenant's own claims. NOT RESOLVED; flag before drafting an indemnity. s1951.4, cross-referenced at s1951.2(a) as the alternative remedy that keeps the lease in effect, has NOT BEEN READ - it is reported to depend on the lease permitting assignment and subletting subject to reasonable limitations, which would be a seventh opt-in. Read it before relying on either remedy.

title: Continuation of Lease After Abandonment
bodyText: The lessor has the remedy described in California Civil Code Section 1951.4 (lessor may continue lease in effect after lessee's breach and abandonment and recover rent as it becomes due, if lessee has right to sublet or assign, subject only to reasonable limitations).
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1951.4, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. VERBATIM SAFE-HARBOUR TEXT - s1951.4(a) states the remedy 'is available ONLY IF THE LEASE PROVIDES FOR THIS REMEDY' and then supplies this exact wording as a form that 'satisfies this subdivision'. Other wording is permitted, but there is no reason to invent any. SEVENTH CONFIRMED OPT-IN LANDLORD RIGHT IN CALIFORNIA. THIS ROW ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, and that is the trap: s1951.4(b) makes the remedy operate only if the lease ALSO satisfies one of three sublet/assignment conditions - (1) it permits, or does not prohibit or restrict, subletting or assignment; (2) it permits them subject to express standards reasonable at execution (express standards are PRESUMED reasonable, a presumption affecting the burden of proof), with the landlord not enforcing a standard that has since become unreasonable; or (3) it permits them with landlord consent AND provides that consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, or a standard to that effect is implied by law. A lease reciting s1951.4(a) while forbidding assignment in the landlord's SOLE DISCRETION satisfies none of the three and gets nothing. See no-sublet-assign-ca. s1951.4(c): acts of maintenance or preservation, efforts to relet, appointment of a receiver at the lessor's initiative, and lawfully withholding or terminating consent to a sublet do NOT constitute terminating the lessee's right to possession - so none of them forfeits the remedy.

title: Subletting and Assignment (Reasonable Consent)
bodyText: Tenant will not sublease or assign all or any portion of the property or this Lease without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord will not unreasonably withhold. Tenant will not rent the property, or any portion of it, on any short-term rental or home-sharing platform.
notes: CA: overrides the base no-sublet-assign row, and this one is a JUDGMENT CALL FOR TAYLOR RATHER THAN A DEFECT FIX - the base clause is not unlawful in California, it is self-defeating. I marked no-sublet-assign 'provisionally clear' on the extend screen because a sole-discretion consent requirement is permissible in a CA residential lease. That was right as far as it went and WRONG in consequence. Civ. Code s1951.4(b) makes the continue-the-lease-and-collect-rent remedy available only if the lease (1) permits or does not restrict sublet/assignment, (2) permits it subject to express standards reasonable at execution, or (3) permits it with consent NOT UNREASONABLY WITHHELD. 'Sole discretion' satisfies none of the three, so a landlord using the base clause forfeits the s1951.4 remedy entirely - even if the lease also carries continue-lease-remedy-ca. THE TRADE-OFF, stated plainly for Taylor's decision: keep SOLE DISCRETION and retain maximum control over who occupies the property, but lose the s1951.4 remedy and be left with s1951.2 damages after termination; or adopt NOT UNREASONABLY WITHHELD, as drafted here, and keep both remedies at the cost of having to justify a refusal. Most landlords want the remedy. I have drafted the reasonableness version because s1951.4(b)(3) is the cheapest of the three routes and because s1951.4(c)(3) confirms that lawfully withholding consent does not itself forfeit the remedy - but this is reversible on request. s1951.4(b)(2) is the alternative worth considering if control matters more: express standards are PRESUMED reasonable, with the burden on the tenant. The short-term-rental sentence is carried over unchanged and is unaffected by s1951.4. CHOICE GROUP 'ca-sublet-consent' (2026-09-19): this row and no-sublet-assign-discretion-ca are ALTERNATIVES - a CA lease must contain EXACTLY ONE. This is the DEFAULT. The builder has no choice-group field yet; see the log. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Tenant Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Termination by a Victim of Abuse or Violence
bodyText: Tenant may terminate this Lease if Tenant, a household member, or an immediate family member was the victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, abuse of an elder or dependent adult, a crime that caused bodily injury or death, a crime involving a firearm or other deadly weapon, or a crime involving the use or threat of force. Tenant must give Landlord written notice with one of the following attached: a copy of a qualifying restraining or protective order; a copy of a written report by a peace officer stating that a report has been filed; documentation from a qualified third party in the form set out in Civil Code section 1946.7; or any other documentation that reasonably verifies the act or crime occurred. Notice must be given within 180 days of the order, the report, or the act or crime. Tenant is responsible for rent for no more than 14 calendar days after giving notice, prorated if the property is re-rented sooner, and is released without penalty from any further obligation. Tenant will not forfeit any security deposit or advance rent because of the termination, and the termination is not a breach of this Lease. Any other tenant remains bound by this Lease.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1946.7, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (SB 1017, Stats. 2022 ch. 558, eff. 2023-01-01). MUCH BROADER THAN 'DOMESTIC VIOLENCE' - s1946.7(a)(6)-(8) reach ANY crime causing bodily injury or death, any crime involving a firearm or other deadly weapon, and any crime involving force or the threat of force. A lease or a canvass row labelled 'domestic violence' understates it. s1946.7(b)(4) is a CATCH-ALL: 'any other form of documentation that reasonably verifies' the act occurred. But s1946.7(k)(2)(B) removes STATUTORY damages against the landlord where the tenant relied on (b)(4) alone - so the catch-all is easier for the tenant to use and weaker to enforce. s1946.7(f): the landlord may NOT require forfeiture of the deposit or advance rent, and the termination is not a breach for any purpose. s1946.7(g): co-tenants stay bound. s1946.7(i): the landlord MAY NOT DISCLOSE the tenant's information to third parties except on written consent or court order - a confidentiality duty. s1946.7(j): may not refuse to rent to someone who previously exercised this right. s1946.7(k): actual damages plus STATUTORY DAMAGES of $100-$5,000. s1946.7(c) is an easily-missed limb: where the victim is an immediate family member who did NOT live with the tenant and no part of the crime occurred in or within 1,000 FEET of the unit, the tenant must attach a further written statement of intent to relocate and why.
