CROSS-REFERENCE ERROR IN THE STATUTE'S OWN FORM, found 2026-09-19: the verbatim Qualified Third Party Statement in s1946.7(b)(3)(B) says a victim of violent crime advocate is defined 'in Section 1947.6 of the Civil Code'. s1947.6 is the ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING section. The definition is actually at s1946.7(h)(5). The parallel forms in CCP s1161.3(a)(2)(C) and Civ. Code s1941.5(d)(3) both cite s1946.7 correctly, which confirms s1947.6 is a drafting slip rather than an intended cross-reference. If the app ever reproduces the s1946.7 form, reproduce it VERBATIM, error included - the statute says 'substantially the same form', and a silently 'corrected' form is no longer the statutory text - but add a builder-facing note. A third instance of cross-reference rot in CA, after 2 CCR s12185(c)(2) and CCP s1161(4). | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-abuse-violence-protections-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Right to Summon Emergency Assistance
bodyText: Nothing in this Lease prohibits or limits Tenant, any resident, or any other person from summoning law enforcement assistance or emergency assistance on behalf of a victim of abuse, a victim of crime, or an individual in an emergency. Landlord will not impose or threaten any fee, fine, penalty, termination, non-renewal, or inferior terms of tenancy because such assistance was summoned.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1946.8, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (AB 1171, eff. 2022-01-01). s1946.8(b): ANY lease provision prohibiting or limiting - or THREATENING to prohibit or limit - the right to summon assistance is VOID as contrary to public policy. s1946.8(e): waiver void. This row states the rule affirmatively rather than relying on silence, because a 'nuisance' or 'excessive police calls' clause elsewhere in a lease is the usual way the prohibition creeps in - SCREEN any CA lease for one. s1946.8(d): NO DOCUMENTATION is required to establish the person's belief that assistance was necessary. s1946.8(f)(2): REBUTTABLE PRESUMPTION that the affirmative defence is established if the landlord files an unlawful detainer WITHIN 30 DAYS of assistance being summoned and the notice alleges the summoning was a lease violation or nuisance. The landlord rebuts by showing another substantial motivating factor. 'Penalties' is defined broadly at s1946.8(a)(3) to include inferior terms and conditions of tenancy, not just fees and eviction. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-emergency-assistance-right-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Abuse and violence: eviction bar, lock changes, confidentiality
bodyText: A landlord may not terminate or refuse to renew a tenancy based on an act of abuse or violence against the tenant, the tenant's immediate family member, or a household member once the landlord has received qualifying documentation. There are two exceptions: where the perpetrator is a tenant in residence of the same unit, and where the perpetrator's words or actions have threatened the physical safety of other tenants, guests or invitees and the tenant continues to permit the perpetrator on the premises after a three-day notice requiring them not to. Where a person restrained by court order is a tenant of the same unit, the landlord must change the locks at the landlord's own expense within 24 hours of a written request accompanied by the order, and give the protected tenant a key; if the landlord does not, the tenant may change the locks and the landlord must reimburse the cost within 21 days. Information a tenant provides under these protections may not be disclosed to third parties without written consent or a court order. A landlord is not liable to other tenants for complying. Ending the lease (Civ. Code 1946.7): a tenant may terminate if the tenant, a household member or an immediate family member was the victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, elder or dependent-adult abuse, a crime that caused bodily injury or death, a crime involving a firearm or other deadly weapon, or a crime involving force or its threat. The tenant gives you written notice, within 180 days of the order, report or act, attaching a qualifying restraining or protective order, a peace officer's written report that a report was filed, qualified third-party documentation in the statutory form, or other documentation reasonably verifying the act. The tenant owes rent for no more than 14 days after the notice (prorated if you re-rent sooner), is released without penalty, forfeits no deposit or advance rent, and isn't in breach; any other tenant stays bound. Keep the tenant's information confidential. Where the person who committed or allegedly committed the abuse or violence is not a tenant of the same unit, change the locks at your own expense within 24 hours of the tenant's written request with any documentation listed in Civ. Code 1941.5(d), and give the tenant a key. If you don't, the tenant may change the locks without your permission and you must reimburse them within 21 days, provided they use locks of similar or better quality, tell you within 24 hours and give you a key.
notes: CA: CCP s1161.3 (amended AB 1756, eff. 2024-01-01) and Civ. Code s1941.6 (amended SB 1051, eff. 2025-01-01), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. s1161.3(b)(2)(B) is the operative landlord route and it is procedural: the three-day notice requires the TENANT not to voluntarily permit or consent to the perpetrator's presence - it is not a notice to the perpetrator, and it only works if the perpetrator's conduct threatened others' physical safety. s1161.3(c) protects the landlord from other tenants' claims arising from compliance. s1161.3(d)(2) routes same-unit-perpetrator cases to CCP s1174.27, NOT READ. s1941.6 applies ONLY where the restrained person is a TENANT OF THE SAME UNIT - a different and narrower trigger than s1161.3. The 24-hour clock runs from the written request plus the order. s1941.6(c)(3) limits the self-help lock change to leases executed on or after 2011-01-01. s1941.6(e): the excluded person remains liable for rent under the lease. s1941.6(d) disapplies s789.3 liability - s789.3 READ 2026-09-19, see edu-self-help-eviction-ban-ca. The carve-out is necessary because excluding the restrained co-tenant by a lock change would otherwise be a willful lockout within s789.3(b)(1). Confidentiality duties sit in both s1161.3(e) and Civ. Code s1946.7(i). CCP s1174.27 READ 2026-09-19 (the same-unit-perpetrator procedure s1161.3(d)(2) routes to): where the court finds documentation of abuse or violence, the defendant raising the defence and other occupants not otherwise at fault are NOT guilty and owe NOTHING - no holdover damages, costs, termination fees or attorney's fees. Where another defendant is shown to be the perpetrator and guilty, the court MUST order a PARTIAL EVICTION of that person only, WITHOUT terminating the tenancy, and MUST order the landlord to change the locks; it may bar the perpetrator permanently, taking custody and visitation arrangements into account. A s1174.27 finding is inadmissible in any other proceeding. | CA: Content from dv-lease-termination-ca (switched off) added by the three-bucket scrub (2026-09-29); unchanged: Civ. Code §1946.7; CCP §1161.3(a)(2)(C); Civ. Code §1941.5(d)(3); 2 CCR §12185(c)(2); CCP §1161(4). | CA: Content from lock-change-non-cotenant-ca (switched off) added by the three-bucket scrub (2026-09-29); unchanged: Civ. Code §1941.5; CCP §1161.3(a)(1).

title: Protected classes and source-of-income rules
bodyText: California prohibits housing discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information, including a perception that a person has any of those characteristics or is associated with someone who does. Source of income includes federal, state and local public assistance and housing subsidies, expressly including Section 8 vouchers and HUD-VASH vouchers, so refusing to rent because an applicant holds a voucher is unlawful. Where there is a government rent subsidy, any financial or income standard must be based only on the portion of rent the tenant actually pays, and an applicant must be offered the option of supplying alternative evidence of ability to pay instead of a credit history. A landlord must also count the aggregate income of people residing together on the same basis as it would for married people.
notes: CA: Gov. Code ss12955 (amended SB 267, eff. 2024-01-01) and 12927 (SB 222, eff. 2020-01-01), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. Answers two canvass rows at once. THREE OPERATIONAL RULES most likely to be breached by a screening workflow rather than by lease text: s12955(n) aggregate-income rule; s12955(o)(1)(A) subsidy income standard keyed only to the TENANT'S PORTION - a 3x-the-rent rule applied to full contract rent is unlawful for a voucher holder; and s12955(o)(1)(B) the credit-history alternative, which requires giving reasonable time AND reasonably considering the alternative evidence. These bind the app's screening logic, not the lease. s12955(b) bars INQUIRY into most protected characteristics - note source of income is deliberately absent from the (b) list and s12955(p)(2) confirms asking about level or source of income is not itself discrimination. s12927(c)(2)(A): narrow exception for renting a portion of an OWNER-OCCUPIED single-family house to ONE roomer or boarder, and even then the s12955(c) advertising ban still applies. s12927(d): 'housing accommodation' expressly includes units offered through a HOSTING PLATFORM. s12927(c)(1) is the statutory basis for the reasonable accommodation and modification duties implemented by 2 CCR ss12176-12181. ENFORCEMENT, Gov. Code ss12980-12989.3 read 2026-09-19: administrative complaint within ONE YEAR (s12980(b)); a private civil action within TWO YEARS, tolled while the complaint is pending, and available whether or not a complaint was filed (s12989.1); actual AND PUNITIVE damages, injunctions and discretionary prevailing-party fees (s12989.2); Attorney General pattern-or-practice suits with civil penalties up to $50,000 for a first violation and $100,000 for each subsequent one (s12989.3). NEW from 2026-01-01 (SB 477): s12981(a)(2) requires ALL PARTIES to take part in the department's MANDATORY DISPUTE RESOLUTION, free of charge, before the department sues. Candidate 572.7: NO RESPONDENT ELECTION RIGHT - because CA housing cases are not heard administratively at all. The department prosecutes by CIVIL ACTION in superior court (s12981(a)(1)), so there is no administrative forum for a landlord to elect out of, unlike Ohio's s4112.055(A)(2).

title: Tenant harassment and immigration-status disclosure
bodyText: California makes it unlawful for a landlord, for the purpose of influencing a tenant to vacate, to engage in conduct amounting to theft or extortion, to use or threaten force or menacing conduct interfering with the tenant's quiet enjoyment, to commit a significant and intentional violation of the entry statute, or to threaten to disclose information about the immigration or citizenship status of a tenant, occupant or anyone associated with them. A tenant who prevails may recover a civil penalty of up to $2,000 for each violation. Separately, it is unlawful to disclose such immigration or citizenship information to any immigration authority, law enforcement agency or government agency for the purpose of harassing or retaliating against a tenant, influencing them to vacate, or recovering possession. A court that finds such a disclosure must order statutory damages of between 6 and 12 times the monthly rent for each person whose status was disclosed, issue injunctive relief, and notify the district attorney. Separately, you may not ask about the immigration or citizenship status of a tenant, prospective tenant, occupant or prospective occupant, or require them to disclose or certify it (Civ. Code 1940.3(b)). You may still request information or documentation needed to verify financial qualifications or identity, and comply with federal law, a subpoena, warrant or court order.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1940.2 and 1940.35 (both AB 291, eff. 2018-01-01), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. s1940.2(a)(4) is the one that connects to the rest of this state's work: a SIGNIFICANT AND INTENTIONAL VIOLATION OF s1954 is statutory harassment, so misuse of the entry right is not merely a s1954 problem - it carries the s1940.2(b) $2,000-per-violation penalty. Cross-reference landlord-entry-ca and edu-no-periodic-inspection-ca. s1940.35 damages are MANDATORY and formula-based - 6 to 12 times monthly rent PER PERSON - plus attorney's fees to the prevailing party (s1940.35(e)) and waiver void (s1940.35(g)). s1940.35(h) lets a 501(c)(3) bring the injunctive action as a party. Among the most severe landlord penalties found in any state in this project. s1940.2(c) safe harbour: a good-faith oral or written warning about conduct that violates the lease, and ordinary explanation of the lease in the normal course of business, are not violations. Also relevant to retaliation: Civ. Code s1942.5(c)/(e) separately make threatening immigration reporting retaliatory conduct - three overlapping provisions on the same subject. | CA: Content from immigration-status-inquiry-ca (switched off) added by the three-bucket scrub (2026-09-29); unchanged: Civ. Code §1940.3(b).

title: Disposing of personal property left after a tenancy
bodyText: California provides an optional procedure for personal property a tenant leaves behind after the tenancy ends and the premises are vacated. The landlord gives written notice to the former tenant and anyone else reasonably believed to own the property, describing it well enough to be identified, stating where it may be claimed, that reasonable storage costs may be charged, and a claim deadline at least 15 days after personal delivery or 18 days after mailing. The statute supplies notice forms that satisfy the requirement. Property must be left on the premises or stored safely with reasonable care. If it is not claimed, it must be sold at public sale after published notice, unless the landlord reasonably believes the total resale value is under $700, in which case the landlord may keep or dispose of it. Sale proceeds left over go to the county within 30 days and may be claimed by the former tenant for a year. A landlord who follows the procedure is protected from liability. No storage cost may be charged if the tenant reclaims property within two days of vacating.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1980-1991 (Chapter 5, Disposition of Personal Property Remaining on Premises), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. CLOSES A GAP THE PROJECT HAD NO ROW FOR IN ANY STATE. s1981(a): the procedure is OPTIONAL, but s1981(e) is the sting - if its requirements are not satisfied, the chapter does not protect the landlord at all and ordinary liability rules apply. The s1989 non-liability shield is the whole point of using it. PRESCRIBED FORMS at s1984 (former tenant) and s1985 (other owner), each 'in substantially the following form'; s1984(b) requires ONE OF TWO alternative closing statements depending on whether the property will be publicly sold or is believed worth under $700. Getting the wrong one in loses the shield. s1982: property the landlord reasonably believes to be LOST goes to police or sheriff first under ss2080 et seq., not through this chapter - and only if they refuse does this chapter apply. s1988(a) $700 threshold; s1988(c) surplus to the county within 30 days, claimable for one year. s1990(c): if stored on the premises, the storage cost is the FAIR RENTAL VALUE of the space; no cost at all if reclaimed within two days. s1983(a): records are presumed to be the TENANT'S. s1981(c) excludes manufactured homes, mobilehomes and commercial coaches; s1981(d) excludes animals; s1980.5 excludes commercial property but NOT self-storage units. s1991 permits combining this notice with a s1951.3 notice of belief of abandonment - s1951.3 since READ (2026-09-19), see edu-abandonment-belief-notice-ca. Note the two notices run on the SAME 15-day personal / 18-day mailed clock, which is what makes combining them practical. CCP s1174(e)-(m) is the post-writ route into this chapter. SERVICE MEMBERS, added 2026-09-19: Mil. & Vet. Code s409.1(b) bars foreclosing or enforcing ANY lien on a service member's property or personal effects - EXPRESSLY INCLUDING LIENS FOR STORAGE - during service and 120 days after, except on a prior court order. So recovering storage costs against a service member's left-behind property needs a court order first. Misdemeanor plus damages and fees.

title: Death on the premises: the three-year rule
bodyText: California law occupies the field on disclosing deaths that occurred on a property. An owner or agent is not required to disclose the occurrence of an occupant's death, or the manner of death, where the death occurred more than three years before the prospective tenant offers to rent, and is never required to disclose that an occupant was living with HIV or died of AIDS-related complications. The implication is that a death within the previous three years is treated as a material fact. An owner or agent is also not immunized for an intentional misrepresentation made in response to a direct question about deaths on the property.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1710.2, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. NOTE it sits in Part 3, Obligations Imposed by Law - outside the landlord-tenant title. Sixth cross-chapter confirmation in CA. The section is drafted as a NON-disclosure safe harbour, not as a disclosure duty, so it states no affirmative requirement and the three-year duty is an inference from s1710.2(a)(1)(A)'s carve-out plus the general materiality standard. FLAGGED AS AN INFERENCE, NOT A HOLDING - the row is written as education and no lease clause is shipped. Confirm against case law before the app prompts for it. s1710.2(b): express field preemption over death and HIV-status disclosure. s1710.2(d): no immunity for an intentional misrepresentation in response to a DIRECT INQUIRY - so 'has anyone died here?' must be answered honestly even outside the three years. s1710.2(c) preserves all other physical-condition disclosure duties. 'Transferee' expressly includes a lessee or renter.

title: Eviction court records are masked for 60 days
bodyText: An unlawful detainer court file in California is not publicly accessible for the first 60 days after the complaint is filed. During that period the clerk may release records only to a party or their attorney, to someone who supplies the names of a plaintiff and a defendant plus the address including any unit number, to a resident of the premises who identifies a party or the case number and proves residency, or by court order on a showing of good cause. After 60 days the file opens if judgment has been entered for the plaintiff, and in a residential case based on a post-foreclosure claim only if judgment was entered for the plaintiff after a trial. The parties may also stipulate to bar access entirely. The clerk mails every named defendant a notice within 24 to 48 hours of filing, with legal-aid and lawyer-referral information.
notes: CA: CCP s1161.2, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended AB 2304, eff. 2025-01-01). Answers the eviction-record-sealing canvass row - but the mechanism is MASKING AT FILING, not sealing after the fact, which is a materially different design from the sealing statutes found in ND and elsewhere. The default is CLOSED and access opens only on the s1161.2(a)(1)(E)-(G) conditions; a landlord who loses, or who settles, leaves a permanently non-public file. s1161.2(a)(2) also permits the parties to stipulate to bar access - a settlement lever worth knowing. s1161.2(d): an extra $15 filing fee on the plaintiff's first appearance. s1161.2(c) prescribes the clerk's notice content including a verbatim State Bar referral statement; that is the clerk's duty, not the landlord's, and no lease row is needed.

title: Balcony and exterior elevated element inspections
bodyText: Buildings with three or more multifamily dwelling units must have their exterior elevated elements - balconies, decks, porches, stairways, walkways and entry structures more than six feet above ground that rely on wood for support - inspected by a licensed architect, engineer, qualified contractor or certified building inspector hired by the owner. At least 15 percent of each type must be examined. The inspector delivers a written report within 45 days. Inspections were due by January 1, 2026 and are required every six years after that. Elements needing repair must be corrected by the owner under permit, within 120 days of permit approval, and anything posing an immediate threat requires immediate action including blocking access. An owner who does not comply within 180 days faces a civil penalty of $100 to $500 per day and a recordable building safety lien.
notes: CA: H&S s17973, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended AB 130, eff. 2025-06-30). This is one of the two previously-unread entry grounds in Civ. Code s1954(a)(6) - now closed. Entry to comply with this article is a permitted purpose, so a landlord scheduling these inspections has a s1954 basis, subject to the notice requirements in landlord-entry-ca. THE DEADLINE HAS PASSED: first inspections were due 2026-01-01, so any CA landlord with 3+ units who has not done one is already exposed to the s17973(i)(2) penalty of $100-$500 PER DAY plus a building safety lien with judgment-lien priority. That makes this a live compliance item, not a future one. s17973(d)(1): reports kept for two inspection cycles and DISCLOSED AND DELIVERED TO THE BUYER on sale. s17973(n): does not apply to a common interest development. s17973(o): local governments may impose greater requirements - another municipal-layer deferral. s17973(e): buildings permitted on or after 2019-01-01 are inspected within six years of the certificate of occupancy.

title: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms
bodyText: Landlord has installed smoke alarms approved and listed by the State Fire Marshal, and, if the property has a fossil fuel burning heater or appliance, a fireplace, or an attached garage, a carbon monoxide device. Landlord has ensured that the smoke alarms are operable as of the start of this tenancy. Tenant shall notify Landlord or the manager if Tenant becomes aware that any alarm is inoperable, and Tenant shall not disable, remove or obstruct any alarm. Landlord will correct any reported deficiency. Landlord or Landlord's agent may enter the property to install, repair, test and maintain alarms on reasonable written notice, during normal business hours, except in an emergency.
notes: CA: H&S ss13113.7 and 17926, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. s13113.7(d)(2)(B) is the lease-relevant duty and it is time-specific: AT THE TIME A NEW TENANCY IS CREATED the owner must ensure smoke alarms are OPERABLE - not merely installed. Thereafter the tenant must notify the owner of an inoperable alarm, and the owner IS NOT IN VIOLATION for a deficient alarm of which it has received no notice. That allocation is why this ships as a lease clause rather than education. s13113.7(d)(2) extended the owner's testing and maintenance duty to RENTED SINGLE-FAMILY DWELLINGS from 2014-01-01. s13113.7(a)(4): battery-operated alarms suffice unless a local rule prohibits them. s13113.7(b) excludes manufactured homes, mobilehomes and commercial coaches. Violation is an infraction, max $200 per offence (s13113.7(e)). CO devices are CONDITIONAL, not universal: s17926(a) requires one only in a unit having a FOSSIL FUEL BURNING HEATER OR APPLIANCE, A FIREPLACE, OR AN ATTACHED GARAGE. All compliance deadlines have long passed. s17926(c)(2) gives a 30-DAY NOTICE TO CORRECT before any fine, and s17926(d) caps the civil remedy at ACTUAL DAMAGES NOT EXCEEDING $100 - a remarkably limited remedy next to the rest of CA's landlord penalties, and worth not overstating to landlords. SEPARATE ENTRY AUTHORITY: s13113.7(d)(2)(A) grants its own right of entry to install, repair, test and maintain alarms, with its own reasonable-written-notice and 24-hour presumption, sitting in the Health and Safety Code rather than Civ. Code s1954. Cross-noted at landlord-entry-ca. H&S s17926.1 (referenced at s17926(g)) NOT READ. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Condition' -> 'Landlord Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Electric Vehicle Charging Station
bodyText: If Tenant has an allotted parking space, Landlord will approve Tenant's written request to install an electric vehicle charging station at that space where the request meets the requirements of Civil Code section 1947.6 and complies with Landlord's procedural approval process for modifications to the property. Tenant's request must include Tenant's consent to a written agreement covering Landlord's requirements for installation, use, maintenance and removal, a complete financial analysis and scope of work, a written description of the proposed modifications, Tenant's obligation to pay all costs associated with the installation and its infrastructure before any work is done, and Tenant's obligation to pay as part of rent the cost of electricity used and of any damage, maintenance, repair, removal and replacement. Tenant and any successor must maintain personal liability coverage in an amount not exceeding ten times the annual rent, covering property damage and personal injury caused by the installation or operation of the station, unless the station is certified by an OSHA-approved Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory and the work is performed by a licensed electrician. Landlord is not required to provide an additional parking space, and may charge monthly rent for a space that becomes reserved as a result.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1947.6, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended SB 638, eff. 2020-01-01). Applies to any lease EXECUTED, EXTENDED OR RENEWED on or after 2015-07-01, so it reaches long-standing tenancies at renewal. FOUR EXEMPTIONS the builder must evaluate, s1947.6(b): EV stations already available to lessees at 10 PERCENT OR MORE of designated spaces; parking not provided as part of the lease; FEWER THAN FIVE PARKING SPACES; or the dwelling is subject to a residential rent control ordinance - BUT that last exemption was itself switched off for any lease executed, extended or renewed on or after 2019-01-01, so it is now spent except in the narrow s1947.6(b)(5) case (rent control PLUS a local ordinance adopted on or before 2018-01-01 requiring approval). Do not code (b)(4) as a live exemption. s1947.6(i) is the insurance off-ramp: NO insurance may be required where the station is NRTL-certified AND a licensed electrician did the work. TENSION TO WATCH: s1947.6(h) authorises an insurance requirement, while 2 CCR s12181(f) bars imposing insurance as a condition on a DISABILITY-RELATED modification - different contexts, but a request framed as both would need care. Not resolved. s1947.6(g)(3) points at the OPR 'Zero-Emission Vehicles in California: Community Readiness Guidebook' Permitting Checklist - a non-statutory document the app cannot validate against. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Rules & Regulations' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Criminal history in tenant screening
bodyText: California regulates how criminal history may be used in tenant screening. Blanket bans are unlawful: a policy excluding everyone with a criminal record, or with any prior conviction, misdemeanor or felony, is prohibited outright. A landlord may not seek, consider, use, or take adverse action based on an arrest that did not lead to conviction, on being questioned or detained, on participation in a diversion or deferred entry of judgment program, on an infraction, on a conviction that has been sealed, dismissed, vacated, expunged, pardoned or otherwise rendered inoperative, on a conviction for which a certificate of rehabilitation was granted, or on juvenile adjudications. Only convictions directly related to a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest may be considered, judged by the nature and severity of the offense and how much time has passed. Whether a screening practice is defensible turns partly on whether it gives the applicant written notice of an opportunity to present mitigating information and actually considers it, checks the accuracy of the record, and delays the criminal history inquiry until after financial and other qualifications are verified. Mitigating information includes youth at the time of the offense, time elapsed, good tenant history, rehabilitation, and conduct arising from the applicant's status as a survivor of abuse or from a disability.
notes: CA: 2 CCR ss12264-12271 (Civil Rights Council, Article 24, operative 2020-01-01), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. CLOSES the tenant-screening gap flagged from s1950.1(f) - an area the canvass had no row for in ANY state. s12269(a)(5) bans BLANKET BANS by name and gives four examples, so the most common screening policy in the industry is per se unlawful in CA. s12269(a)(1)-(4) list categories that may not be sought OR considered at all - note 'SEEK' is prohibited, so merely running a report that surfaces them is exposure, not just acting on them. Narrow proviso: if the APPLICANT volunteers such information as mitigating evidence, it may be considered. s12266(d)(4) is the structural one for the product: delaying criminal history inquiry until AFTER financial and other qualifications are verified is a factor in whether a less discriminatory alternative was feasible. That is a workflow-ordering rule, not a lease term, and it interacts with the s1950.6(c)(2) screening-process choice and the s1950.1 reusable-report regime. s12266(e) mitigating information expressly includes conduct arising from SURVIVOR STATUS (DV, sexual assault, dating violence, stalking) and conduct arising from a DISABILITY that could be mitigated by a reasonable accommodation - linking this article to edu-abuse-violence-protections-ca and to ss12176-12181. s12269(b): the seven-year look-back permitted by Civ. Code s1785.13(a)(6) is a ceiling, not a safe harbour - a court may find a SHORTER look-back was the feasible alternative. s12270(a): complying with a federal law that REQUIRES consideration (sex offender public housing ineligibility, meth manufacture) is an affirmative defence. s12271: local ordinances may be more protective and are not displaced. s12268(b): advertising a lawful screening policy is not itself unlawful. ss12005(f), 12005(k), 12062(c)-(d) and Gov. Code s12955.8 NOT READ. | CA: SOP 1.31 retro check 24 (rule 78), 2026-10-03: pointer repointed. Found by the full sweep.

title: Damage, Destruction and Failure to Deliver
bodyText: Tenant may terminate this Lease before the end of the Term if Landlord does not, within a reasonable time after Tenant's request, fulfill Landlord's obligations to place and secure Tenant in quiet possession of the property, to put it into good condition, or to repair it. Tenant may also terminate if the greater part of the property, or the part that was the material inducement to Tenant entering this Lease, is destroyed by any cause other than Tenant's want of ordinary care. If the property is destroyed, this Lease terminates.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1932 and 1933, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. Answers two canvass rows that had been open - the fire/casualty termination right and the failure-to-deliver-possession remedy - and CORRECTS an earlier entry: I recorded failure-to-deliver-possession as 'not located' after reading s1925, which only defines hiring. The remedy is in s1932(1), one chapter over. s1932(1) is broader than casualty: it covers failure within a reasonable time after REQUEST to secure quiet possession, to put the property into good condition, OR to repair - a general termination right for landlord non-performance sitting in Chapter 1, separate from the s1942 repair-and-deduct remedy in Chapter 2 and cumulative with it. s1932(2)'s 'material inducement' limb is unusual and worth preserving verbatim in substance: partial destruction suffices if the destroyed part was what induced the tenant to rent. s1933(4): destruction of the thing hired terminates the hiring by operation of law - no notice needed, which is why the body text states it rather than conditioning it on Tenant's election. Both sections date from 1872/1905 and neither has been tested here against s1946.2 just cause; a landlord asserting s1933(4) on a covered property should still expect the s1946.2 notice machinery to apply to the possession claim. NOT RESOLVED. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-casualty-termination-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: When a landlord may not demand or collect rent at all
bodyText: California bars a landlord from demanding rent, collecting rent, issuing a notice of rent increase, or issuing a three-day notice to pay rent or quit where four conditions all exist. The dwelling substantially lacks one of the standard habitability characteristics, violates Health and Safety Code section 17920.10, or is substandard under section 17920.3 to an extent that endangers life, limb, health, property, safety or welfare. A public officer responsible for enforcing housing law has inspected the premises and notified the landlord in writing of the obligation to abate or repair. The conditions have gone unabated for 35 days beyond service of that notice without good cause. And the conditions were not caused by the tenant. A landlord who violates this is liable for actual damages plus special damages of between $100 and $5,000, and the prevailing party recovers attorney's fees and costs. The court may also order the conditions abated and retain jurisdiction until they are.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1942.4, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. SHOULD HAVE SURFACED EARLIER IN THIS PASS - it is the most consequential habitability remedy in the CA set and it was missed until the canvass forced the question. It bars the landlord's core economic act, not merely the eviction. ALL FOUR CONDITIONS MUST COEXIST, and condition (2) is the practical gate: it requires an INSPECTION AND WRITTEN NOTICE BY A PUBLIC OFFICER, so a tenant's own complaint does not trigger the bar. Condition (3) runs 35 DAYS from service, and s1942.4(a)(3) makes service complete ON DEPOSIT IN THE MAIL, not receipt. s1942.4(d): the tenant need NOT exhaust any other remedy first - so this sits alongside s1942 repair-and-deduct rather than after it, and s1942.4(f) makes it cumulative. s1942.4(e): available in small claims. DIRECT PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE: a three-day notice issued while this bar applies is void ab initio, so the legal tracker's notice generator needs a gate here, not just the CCP s1161(2) content checks - cross-refer edu-three-day-notice-ca. Also note s1942.4(a)(1) cites H&S s17920.10, the OTHER incorporation in s1941.1(a) - READ 2026-09-19, see edu-lead-hazards-ca. A unit with lead hazards at or above the s17920.10(c) thresholds satisfies condition (a)(1) of the bar, and repair work disturbing lead paint without containment can itself create one. s1942.4(f) carve-out: the section does not bind a landlord pursuing Ellis Act rights under Gov. Code s7060 et seq. - NOT READ. FEE EXPOSURE, CCP s1174.21 read 2026-09-19: a landlord who brings a NONPAYMENT unlawful detainer while liable for a s1942.4 violation is liable for the TENANT'S attorney's fees and costs. So filing through the bar costs the landlord the tenant's fees as well as losing the case.

title: Attorney-fee clauses are reciprocal by operation of law
bodyText: In California, if a lease provides that attorney's fees incurred to enforce it will be awarded to one party or to the prevailing party, the party who actually prevails is entitled to reasonable fees whether or not the lease names them. A one-sided fee clause therefore operates in both directions, and any provision waiving that rule is void. The fee provision is read as applying to the whole contract unless both parties were represented by counsel in negotiating and executing it and the lease says so. The court decides who prevailed, may find that nobody did, and there is no prevailing party at all where the action was voluntarily dismissed or dismissed under a settlement.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1717, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. CONFIRMS the reasoning already relied on in three places - the extend manifest's decision that CA uses the full default-by-tenant row rather than the Ohio-style default-by-tenant-ks-ne variant, and the notes on default-by-tenant and s1942.5(i). Until now that reciprocity was asserted from the section number alone; it is now read. s1717(a): reciprocity is automatic and the anti-waiver sentence is unconditional - 'any provision in any such contract which provides for a waiver of attorney's fees is void'. s1717(b)(2) is the limb landlords misjudge: VOLUNTARY DISMISSAL OR SETTLEMENT MEANS NO PREVAILING PARTY, so a landlord who settles an unlawful detainer recovers no fees under the clause however favourable the settlement. Worth surfacing in the legal tracker before a settlement decision. The whole-contract rule in s1717(a) means a narrowly drafted fee clause aimed at one covenant is read across the entire lease unless the dual-counsel condition is met and RECITED - which essentially never happens in residential leases. Interacts with Civ. Code s1953(a)(4) (waiver of procedural rights in litigation void) - that relationship is NOT resolved here.

title: Unconscionable lease clauses
bodyText: A California court that finds a contract or any clause of it was unconscionable when it was made may refuse to enforce the contract, enforce the rest of it without the unconscionable clause, or limit the clause's application to avoid an unconscionable result. Where unconscionability is claimed or appears, the parties must be given a reasonable opportunity to present evidence about the clause's commercial setting, purpose and effect.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1670.5, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. NOTE this is s1670.5, NOT s1670.50 (buyer-broker representation agreements) - the two differ by a trailing zero and the wrong one was supplied first. See the cross-body citation-ambiguity topic. s1670.5 is a general contracts doctrine, not a landlord-tenant provision, and it supplies a REMEDIAL FLEXIBILITY the specific voiding statutes do not: where s1953, s1942.1, s1632(l) or 2 CCR s12180(a)(3) make a provision void outright, s1670.5(a) lets a court instead sever the clause or merely LIMIT its application. It is a backstop for clause types CA has not specifically addressed, not a substitute for the specific bars. s1670.5(b) is procedural and matters for drafting evidence: the commercial setting, purpose and effect are expressly in issue, which is where an adhesion-contract argument about a standard-form lease would run. Case law is where the substance of CA unconscionability doctrine lives; none read.

title: Criminal penalty for faking a service dog
bodyText: In California it is a misdemeanor to knowingly and fraudulently represent yourself, verbally or in writing, as the owner or trainer of a dog licensed, qualified or identified as a guide, signal or service dog. The penalty is up to six months in county jail, a fine of up to $1,000, or both.
notes: CA: Pen. Code s365.7, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. Answers the canvass row, but the SCOPE IS NARROW and a landlord should not be told otherwise: it reaches only CANINES, and only guide, signal or SERVICE dogs as defined in Pen. Code s365.5(d)-(f) and Civ. Code s54.1(b)(6). It does NOT reach misrepresentation about a SUPPORT animal, which is the category landlords most often suspect - and support animals are precisely where 2 CCR s12185(c)(2)'s online-certification presumption operates instead. The two mechanisms cover different animals and should not be conflated. It is also a criminal provision, so it is not a landlord remedy: the landlord's route remains the s12178/s12185 documentation process, not a prosecution. Pen. Code s365.5 and Civ. Code s54.1 NOT READ. Pen. Code s365.5 READ 2026-09-19: s365.5(c) makes it a MISDEMEANOR, fine up to $2,500, to prevent or interfere with a disabled person's rights under the section - but those rights, at (b), are admittance to 'accommodations, advantages, facilities... hotels, lodging places, places of public accommodation... and other places to which the GENERAL PUBLIC IS INVITED'. A private residential tenancy is not a place to which the general public is invited, so on its text s365.5 reaches HOTELS AND LODGING but NOT ordinary rental housing. It is also CANINE-ONLY and reaches only guide, signal and service dogs - never support animals. So California has NO criminal penalty for a landlord denying an assistance animal in a residential tenancy; the remedy runs through FEHA and 2 CCR s12176 et seq. Textual conclusion; Civ. Code s54.1, the housing-access provision s365.7 cross-refers to, remains unread. Civ. Code s54.1 READ 2026-09-19 (Disabled Persons Act). s54.1(b)(6)(A): refusing to rent to, or to let a tenant keep, a GUIDE, SIGNAL OR SERVICE DOG is a denial of equal access to housing - even where the landlord bars dogs generally (s54.1(b)(5)). s54.1(b)(6)(B): the lease MAY reasonably regulate the dog's presence outside its duties, and the tenant stays liable for proven damage. Like the Penal Code sections, s54.1 is DOG-ONLY; SUPPORT animals rest on FEHA and 2 CCR s12185 alone. s54.1(b)(3)(A): modifications at the tenant's expense may be conditioned on RESTORATION, and NO ADDITIONAL SECURITY may be required - though an escrow for restoration costs may be negotiated. s54.1(d): any ADA violation is also a s54.1 violation. Remedies are in s54.3, NOT READ.

title: Relocation benefits during habitability repairs
bodyText: Where a California enforcement agency has cited a building and the court finds conditions substantially endangering health and safety, and the owner's repairs or the conditions themselves significantly affect safe and sanitary use so that a tenant cannot safely remain, the owner must provide or pay relocation benefits. These cover actual reasonable moving and storage costs, including transporting, packing and insuring the tenant's property, replacing property lost or damaged in the move, and reconnecting utilities and equipment. On top of that, relocation compensation equals the difference between the contract rent and the HUD fair market rent for a comparable unit in the area, for the period of repair, up to 120 days. A tenant substantially responsible for causing the conditions receives nothing. The owner must also offer each relocated tenant the first right to occupancy in writing by certified mail before renting to anyone else. If a receiver is appointed, the owner is enjoined from collecting rent at all.
notes: CA: H&S s17980.7, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended SB 1465, eff. 2025-01-01). Answers the relocation canvass row. Note the TRIGGER IS ENFORCEMENT-DRIVEN, not tenant-driven: it follows a s17980.6 order or notice and, for the (d) benefits, a court finding - so it is not a self-executing duty the moment a unit becomes uninhabitable. s17980.7(d)(3)(B)(i): compensation is the CONTRACT RENT vs HUD FAIR MARKET RENT DIFFERENTIAL for a comparable unit, capped at 120 DAYS - a formula the app cannot compute without the HUD FMR table, so it is a lookup dependency, not a stored constant. s17980.7(d)(5): the first-right-to-occupancy offer must be in writing by first-class CERTIFIED mail, and the tenant has 10 days to respond - but the duty lapses entirely if the tenant never gave a relocation address. s17980.7(c)(3): on appointment of a receiver the owner AND the owner's agent are ENJOINED FROM COLLECTING RENTS - a second and more drastic rent-collection bar alongside Civ. Code s1942.4. s17980.7(e) IS THE CROSS-LINK WORTH KNOWING: initiating a proceeding or entering judgment under this section is deemed a 'proceeding' or 'judgment' under Civ. Code s1942.5(a)(4)-(5), so it starts a 180-day RETALIATION window - see edu-retaliation-ca. s17980.7(c)(11) prevailing-party fees; (b) loss of state tax deductions for interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization on the cited structure; (h) Ellis Act carve-out. ss17980, 17980.6 and 17995 NOT READ.

title: Tenant-Supplied Refrigerator
bodyText: [Include only if Tenant has asked to supply their own refrigerator.] "Under state law, the landlord is required to provide a refrigerator in good working order in your unit. By checking this box, you acknowledge that you have asked to bring your own refrigerator and that you are responsible for keeping that refrigerator in working order." Tenant may, on 30 days' written notice, tell Landlord that Tenant no longer wishes to keep their own refrigerator, and at the end of that period Landlord will install a refrigerator in good working order. Landlord is not responsible for maintaining a refrigerator Tenant supplies.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1941.1(a)(10)-(11) and (b)-(c), added by AB 628 (Stats. 2025 ch. 342), EFFECTIVE 2026-01-01 and applying only to a lease ENTERED INTO, AMENDED OR EXTENDED on or after that date. Stove and refrigerator are now affirmative habitability characteristics - a genuinely new obligation, not a restatement. s1941.1(a)(11)(B)(i) prescribes the tenant acknowledgment VERBATIM and it is shipped as written. The opt-out is tightly conditioned: s1941.1(a)(11)(B)(ii) requires the lease to give the tenant a 30-DAY WRITTEN NOTICE route back to a landlord-supplied refrigerator; (iii) FORBIDS conditioning the tenancy on the tenant supplying one; (iv) relieves the landlord of maintaining a tenant-supplied unit. There is no equivalent opt-out for the stove. s1941.1(b) exempts permanent supportive housing, single-room occupancy units, residential hotel units, and units in facilities offering shared or communal kitchens including assisted living. s1941.1(c)(1): 30 days to repair or replace a RECALLED appliance; (c)(2) preserves the s1942 remedy. PROVENANCE NOTE, recorded deliberately: on 2026-09-19 a row `refrigerator-tenant-supplied-ca` appeared in the CSV that neither Taylor nor I had written, citing a 'fragment supplied by Taylor' that did not exist in the session, with its citation marked UNKNOWN and inferred to s1941.1. I quarantined and then deleted it on Taylor's instruction. ITS SUBSTANCE WAS CORRECT - verbatim acknowledgment, 30-day revocation, 2026-01-01 commencement all match s1941.1(a)(11) as now read. The quarantine was still the right call on process: an unsourced row asserting live law cannot ship, and the rule that saved us here is the same rule that would have caught a fabrication. This row is rebuilt from primary text, not restored. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Condition' -> 'Landlord Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states). | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the tenant-supplied refrigerator acknowledgment and the 30-day return route the statute requires in the lease; the landlord's stove and refrigerator duty moved to edu-stove-refrigerator-ca.

title: No Immigration or Citizenship Status Inquiry
bodyText: Landlord will not inquire about the immigration or citizenship status of Tenant, any prospective tenant, or any occupant or prospective occupant, will not require any of them to disclose or certify that status, and will not disclose information about that status to any person or entity for the purpose of harassing or intimidating them, retaliating against them for exercising their rights, influencing them to vacate, or recovering possession. Landlord may request information or documentation necessary to determine or verify financial qualifications or identity, and may comply with any obligation under federal law or a subpoena, warrant or court order.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1940.3(b), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (AB 299, eff. 2018-01-01). THIS IS THE ACTUAL INQUIRY PROHIBITION - stronger and earlier in the process than ss1940.2(a)(5) and 1940.35, which the canvass row was answered with previously. s1940.3(b)(1) bars ANY INQUIRY at all; (b)(2) bars requiring disclosure or certification; (b)(3) bars disclosure for improper purposes. s1940.3(c)(2) is the landlord's safe harbour and the line the app must respect: requesting information to verify FINANCIAL QUALIFICATIONS or IDENTITY is permitted - so identity documents may be requested, status may not be asked about. A screening form asking for immigration status is unlawful on its face. s1940.05 separately defines 'immigration or citizenship status' to include a PERCEIVED status and association with someone perceived to have one, so the prohibition reaches assumptions, not just questions. s1940.3(a) also bars a PUBLIC ENTITY from compelling landlords to inquire or report - relevant if a local ordinance ever purports to. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-tenant-harassment-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Double letting of a room suspends all rent in the building
bodyText: California provides that a person who hires part of a room as a dwelling is entitled to the whole room, regardless of any agreement to the contrary. If a landlord lets a room as a dwelling to more than one family, the first person to whom any part of it was let is entitled to possession of the whole room for the agreed term, and every tenant in the building under the same landlord is relieved of all obligation to pay rent for as long as the double letting continues.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1950, read section-open 2026-09-19. Answers the double-letting canvass row, and the remedy is far more severe than the row anticipated: it is not abatement for the affected tenant, it suspends the rent obligation of EVERY TENANT IN THE BUILDING under the same landlord while the double letting continues. Enacted 1872 and never amended. Unusually, it overrides contrary agreement by its own terms ('notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary'), so it does not depend on s1953. No case law read; the practical scope of 'lets a room as a dwelling for more than one family' is untested here.

title: Automatic Renewal Provision
bodyText: [Any provision automatically renewing or extending this Lease if Tenant remains in possession after expiration, or fails to give notice of intent not to renew, must appear here in at least eight-point boldface type, and a recital that such a provision is contained in the body of this Lease must appear in at least eight-point boldface type immediately above the place where Tenant signs.]
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1945.5, read section-open 2026-09-19. A FORMATTING requirement with a substantive consequence: an automatic renewal or extension provision in a residential lease is VOIDABLE BY THE PARTY WHO DID NOT PREPARE THE LEASE unless it appears in at least EIGHT-POINT BOLDFACE TYPE in the body of the lease AND a recital of that fact appears in at least eight-point boldface immediately before the signature line. If voided, the s1945 presumption applies instead (holdover plus acceptance of rent renews on the same terms, not exceeding one month where rent is monthly, nor one year in any case). Waiver void as against public policy. SIXTH TYPE-SIZE FLOOR IN CA, and the first that also dictates WHERE on the page text must sit. The schema cannot express either. This row is written as a bracketed instruction rather than clause text because the requirement is about rendering, not wording - the builder must satisfy it or omit auto-renewal entirely. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Term & Renewal' -> 'Default & Termination' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Reporting Inoperable Locks
bodyText: Tenant will notify Landlord when Tenant becomes aware that any dead bolt lock or window security or locking device in the unit is inoperable.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1941.3, read section-open 2026-09-19. A SEPARATE STATUTORY SECURITY DUTY the library had no row for in any state. s1941.3(a)(1): dead bolt extending at least 13/16 inch beyond the strike edge; horizontal sliding doors excluded; pre-existing half-inch bolts suffice until first repair or replacement after 1998-07-01. (a)(2) window devices, excluding louvered and casement windows and any window more than 12 feet vertically or 6 feet horizontally from ground, roof or platform. (a)(3) does not require installing a door or gate where none existed on 1998-01-01. s1941.3(b) is the allocation that makes this lease text: the TENANT must notify, and the landlord is NOT LIABLE unless it fails to correct within a reasonable time after actual or received notice - the same notice-shifting structure as the smoke alarm duty. s1941.3(c) gives the tenant the ss1942, 1942.4 and 1942.5 remedies, breach of contract, injunctive relief, AND an affirmative defence in an unlawful detainer after rent default with CCP s1174.2 relief - unusually broad. s1941.3(d): does not alter the landlord's general duty of care under s1714. s1941.3(f) exempts historically designated buildings. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Condition' -> 'Landlord Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states). | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the tenant's notice duty; the landlord's installation and repair duty moved to edu-security-devices-ca.

title: Tenant Use Rights Landlord Cannot Prohibit
bodyText: Nothing in this Lease prohibits Tenant from displaying a religious item on the entry door or door frame of the dwelling, subject to the limits in Civil Code section 1940.45; from owning a personal micromobility device, or storing and recharging up to one such device per occupant in the unit where it meets the applicable safety standard or is insured, unless Landlord provides secure long-term storage; from using a clothesline or drying rack in Tenant's private area on the conditions in Civil Code section 1940.20; or, where the property contains no more than two units and Tenant has a ground-level private outdoor area, from personal agriculture in portable containers on the conditions in Civil Code section 1940.10.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1940.45, 1940.41, 1940.20 and 1940.10, read section-open 2026-09-19. Grouped because each is a 'landlord shall not prohibit' rule that a standard lease's general restrictions would otherwise silently breach - the same shape as the political-sign and waterbed findings on common-area-use. s1940.45 religious items: limits are a total display exceeding 36 by 12 square inches, obstruction of the door's operation, threat to health or safety, illegality, or obscenity. Applies to landlords, sublessors and HOAs alike. s1940.41 micromobility: the landlord may NOT ban ownership at all, and may ban in-unit storage and charging only by PROVIDING SECURE LONG-TERM STORAGE - defined at (a)(2) to require resident-only access, on-site location, protection from precipitation, one electrical connection per device, and NO CHARGE to tenants. Battery repair in the unit may be prohibited; changing a tyre or adjusting brakes may not. Disability accommodation overrides (c) and (b)(2)(C). s1940.10 personal agriculture applies only to property of NOT MORE THAN TWO UNITS; the landlord may approve container placement, prohibit synthetic chemicals, and require a written agreement on excess water and waste costs. s1940.10(f) and the clothesline rules both defer to s1954 for any inspection. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Rules & Regulations' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states). || CONFIRMED COMPLETE 2026-09-28, gap-discovery sources 2 and 4. Official leginfo full-text search, all codes: 'personal micromobility device' returns 4 sections - Civ. Code s1940.41 plus three Streets and Highways Code sections with no landlord application - so s1940.41 is the only rental rule and this row is complete on that limb. Worth recording from the lease comparison: the CAA CA-041 12/24 form's 'Personal Micromobility Devices' section permits storage and charging of one device per occupant subject to safety-standard or insurance conditions, but does NOT state the s1940.41(a)(2) condition on banning in-unit storage, which requires the landlord to PROVIDE secure long-term storage meeting five requirements at NO CHARGE. A landlord relying on that form would think it may restrict more than the statute allows. The library's row is the more accurate of the two. FLAG DISPLAY, screened and confirmed absent for rentals: 'flag of the United States' returns 20 sections; the housing ones are Civ. Code s4705 (common interest developments) and s6702 (commercial CIDs), and there is NO landlord-tenant flag display right in California - unlike Ohio's ORC s5321.131. Note that the CAA form cites Civ. Code s1353.6 for governing documents, which is the REPEALED predecessor of s4705: cross-reference rot in a current professional form, the same error shape this project tracks in its own rows. SCOPE: statutes only. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-tenant-display-and-use-rights-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Pest Control Notices Given Before Signing
bodyText: [Include this section if a periodic pest control contract covers the property, or if Landlord routinely applies pesticide in a common area on a set schedule without a licensed pest control operator.] Pest control notices. If a contract for periodic pest control service is in place for the property, Landlord has given Tenant a copy of the notice provided by the registered structural pest control company, and Tenant acknowledges receiving it. If Landlord or Landlord's agent routinely applies pesticide in a common area on a set schedule without a licensed pest control operator, Landlord has given Tenant, before Tenant entered into this Lease, the written notice that identifies the pest to be controlled, the name and brand of the pesticide product, the statutory caution statement and the schedule on which the pesticide will be applied, and Tenant acknowledges receiving it. Landlord will give Tenant a new notice if the pesticide to be used changes.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1940.8 and 1940.8.5, read section-open 2026-09-19 (SB 328, eff. 2016-01-01). s1940.8.5(b)(1)(C) prescribes a CAUTION STATEMENT VERBATIM - 'CAUTION - PESTICIDES ARE TOXIC CHEMICALS...' including the California Poison Control number (1-800-222-1222) and the Department of Pesticide Regulation number (916-324-4100), plus a blank for the County Health Department number. It is not shipped inline here because the county number is property-specific; the builder must assemble it. Also required verbatim: 'The approximate date, time, and frequency of this pesticide application is subject to change.' SCOPE: the notice duty applies only where the landlord applies pesticide WITHOUT a licensed operator - s1940.8.5(e) leaves a registered structural pest control company's own B&P Code s8538 duties intact, and s1940.8 separately requires passing that company's notice to each new tenant. Adjacent-unit notice is triggered only by broadcast application (over two square feet), foggers or aerosol sprays. Four permitted delivery methods including posting at the unit entry. s1940.8.5(b)(3) allows immediate application by written or oral agreement, with the written notice left in the unit no later than the time of application. Common areas: s1940.8.5(c) posting, kept up 24 hours after; (d) a separate regime for routine scheduled applications, with notice to EACH NEW TENANT BEFORE LEASE SIGNING. s1940.8.5(f): nothing authorises entry in violation of s1954. s1940.8.5(g) is a safe harbour - compliant notice is deemed adequate and no further information is required. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-pest-control-notice-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option. | CA: SWITCHED BACK ON AND NARROWED 2026-10-03, SOP 1.31 retro check 26 (rule 78 with rule 46). The 2026-09-29 scrub switched this clause off as restating a duty that applies whatever the lease says. Two of its limbs are not that: they are WRITTEN NOTICES CALIFORNIA REQUIRES BEFORE OR AT THE START OF THE TENANCY, which is the case rule 78 says to keep or restore a lease clause for, and the case Arizona's retro restored move-out-inspection-notice-az for. Both re-read section-open on leginfo 2026-10-03. Civ. Code s1940.8, quoted in full: 'A landlord of a residential dwelling unit shall provide EACH NEW TENANT that occupies the unit with a copy of the notice provided by a registered structural pest control company pursuant to Section 8538 of the Business and Professions Code, if a contract for periodic pest control service has been executed.' Civ. Code s1940.8.5(d)(2)(A)(ii): for a routine scheduled common-area programme the notice goes to 'Each new tenant PRIOR TO ENTERING INTO A LEASE AGREEMENT', and (d)(2)(B)(ii) names personal delivery to the tenant as a permitted method, so delivery with the lease satisfies it; (d)(2)(C) requires a fresh notice if the pesticide changes. NARROWED DELIBERATELY: the in-tenancy 24-hour notice, the adjacent-unit notice, the common-area posting and the safe harbour stay in edu-pest-control-notice-ca, because those duties do apply whatever the lease says. CONDITIONAL, not REQUIRED: both limbs bite only where there is a periodic contract or a routine schedule. The verbatim s1940.8.5(d)(1)(C) CAUTION statement is NOT shipped inline - it carries a property-specific county health department number and the builder must assemble it, as the original note records. Sync 2026-10-03 (Claude Code): lease_clause_basis set to REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE (both statutes require the notice to each new tenant before or at the start of the tenancy; the clause is CONDITIONAL because each applies only where its fact is true); the restored row arrived with the basis blank.

title: Ordnance, Demolition and Shared Utility Disclosures
bodyText: Former ordnance location: [If Landlord has actual knowledge of a former federal or state ordnance location within one mile of the property, disclose it here; otherwise state that Landlord has no such knowledge.] Demolition: [If Landlord has applied for a permit to demolish the unit, state the earliest approximate demolition date and the approximate date Landlord will terminate the tenancy.] Shared utility service: [If gas or electric service through Tenant's meter also serves areas outside the unit, disclose that here; a separate written agreement governs payment for it.]
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1940.7, 1940.6 and 1940.9, read section-open 2026-09-19. Three conditional pre-tenancy disclosures the library had no rows for. s1940.7: ORDNANCE - actual knowledge of a former federal or state military training area that may contain explosive munitions, within ONE MILE ('neighborhood area', s1940.7(c)(2)), disclosed in writing BEFORE execution. Enacted after the 1983 Tierra Santa munition explosion. s1940.6: DEMOLITION - notice to a prospective tenant before entering a rental agreement, before taking an application screening fee or any other fee, and before requiring any writing initiating a tenancy; and to an existing tenant before applying for the permit. Must state the earliest approximate demolition date, and demolition MAY NOT occur before that date. Civil penalty up to $2,500 plus actual damages, moving expenses and prevailing-party fees. s1940.9: SHARED METER - if the tenant's meter serves areas outside the unit and the landlord knows, disclosure before inception or on discovery, PLUS a written agreement on payment or another arrangement. Remedies include ordering the landlord to become customer of record and reimbursement back to the date the duty arose. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): optional (Taylor's pattern 3): these disclosures are owed before signing; the clause records them. Companion: edu-pre-signing-disclosures-ca.

title: Disaster Damage, Evacuation and Rent
bodyText: If a declared disaster damages the property, Landlord will remove debris caused by the disaster and mitigate hazards arising from it, including mold, smoke, smoke residue, smoke odor, ash, asbestos and water damage, within a reasonable time and following any government cleaning protocols. Landlord will notify Tenant in writing that this has been done and that Tenant may view and request copies of any environmental studies, testing or reports. Unless this Lease is lawfully terminated, the tenancy remains in effect and Tenant may return at the same rent as soon as it is safe and practicable. Tenant's obligation to pay rent is discharged for any period Tenant cannot occupy the unit under a mandatory evacuation order, and Landlord will return any rent already paid for that period within 10 calendar days after the order is lifted, or Tenant may deduct it from the next month's rent. If this Lease terminates because the property was destroyed or because Tenant terminated under Civil Code section 1932(2), Landlord will return any advance rent covering a period after termination within 21 days.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1941.8 and 1941.9, added by SB 610 (Stats. 2025 ch. 547), EFFECTIVE 2026-01-01. Brand new and directly relevant to a CA portfolio after the wildfire seasons. s1941.8(b) is the sharp edge: until a local public health agency determines that disaster debris does NOT contain toxic substances, the presence of that debris is PRESUMED TO RENDER THE UNIT UNTENANTABLE under s1941.1 - which routes straight into s1942 repair-and-deduct and s1942.4's rent-demand bar. s1941.8(e): nothing requires the landlord to REBUILD. s1941.8(d): the tenancy survives and the tenant has a right to return AT THE PRE-DISASTER RENT - a significant constraint given s1947.12(b) would otherwise let a new tenancy reset the rate. s1941.8(g) preserves more protective local ordinances. s1941.9(b) discharges rent during a mandatory evacuation with a 10-day refund or deduction. s1941.9(a) ties the 21-day advance-rent return to the s1932(2) and s1933(4) triggers already carried in casualty-termination-ca - cross-referenced there. 'Disaster' is defined at s1941.8(h) by a PRESIDENTIAL OR GUBERNATORIAL declaration, so the duty is not self-executing on local damage alone. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Condition' -> 'Landlord Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states). | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-disaster-duties-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Screening: four things a landlord may not hold against an applicant
bodyText: California bars a landlord from taking adverse action in tenant screening based on any of four things: an alleged breach of a prior lease that stemmed from an act of abuse or violence, where the applicant is not alleged to have committed it; the applicant having previously requested a lock change after abuse or violence, whether or not the request was granted; the applicant, or an immediate family or household member, having been a victim of abuse or violence; or the applicant or a guest having previously summoned law enforcement or emergency assistance for a victim of abuse, a victim of crime, or a person in an emergency. Adverse action includes both denying the application and approving it on terms less favourable than those advertised. A landlord who violates this is liable for actual damages plus statutory damages of $100 to $5,000.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1946.9, added by SB 1051 (Stats. 2024 ch. 75), eff. 2025-01-01. Sits alongside 2 CCR ss12264-12271 as the second distinct screening-restriction regime in CA, and it is not about criminal history at all. s1946.9(d)(2)(B) is the limb most likely to catch a compliant-looking workflow: ADVERSE ACTION INCLUDES APPROVING the application on terms 'different and less favourable' than any written notice, statement or advertisement - so a higher deposit, a co-signer requirement or a shorter term imposed on one of these four grounds is a violation even though the applicant was accepted. s1946.9(a)(1) and (a)(3): where the landlord asks for documentation, it MUST accept any of the forms listed in s1941.5(d), which includes the catch-all 'any other form of documentation that reasonably verifies that the abuse or violence occurred, INCLUDING A SIGNED STATEMENT FROM THE ELIGIBLE TENANT'. A landlord cannot demand a police report or restraining order. Connects to edu-abuse-violence-protections-ca (s1946.7), edu-abuse-violence-protections-ca (ss1161.3, 1941.5, 1941.6) and edu-emergency-assistance-right-ca (s1946.8) - the four together form a single statutory scheme, and s1946.9 is the screening-stage end of it. | CA: SOP 1.31 retro check 24 (rule 78), 2026-10-03: two pointers repointed. Found by the full sweep.

title: Lock Change After Abuse or Violence
bodyText: If a person who has committed or is alleged to have committed abuse or violence against Tenant, or against Tenant's immediate family or household member, is not a tenant of the same unit, Landlord will change the locks of the unit at Landlord's own expense within 24 hours of Tenant's written request accompanied by any one of the forms of documentation listed in Civil Code section 1941.5(d), and will give Tenant a key. If Landlord does not, Tenant may change the locks without Landlord's permission, and Landlord will reimburse Tenant within 21 days, provided Tenant uses locks of similar or better quality, notifies Landlord within 24 hours and provides a key.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1941.5, REPEALED AND RE-ADDED by SB 1051 (Stats. 2024 ch. 75), eff. 2025-01-01. This is the COMPLEMENT to s1941.6, which the library already carries: s1941.6 applies where the restrained person IS a tenant of the same unit and requires a COURT ORDER; s1941.5 applies where the perpetrator is NOT a co-tenant and accepts a much wider evidentiary basis. Both were needed; carrying only s1941.6 left the more common scenario uncovered. s1941.5(d)(4) and (e) are the operative difference: the tenant may choose ANY ONE of four documentation forms, and the catch-all expressly includes 'a signed statement from the eligible tenant' - so no court order, police report or third-party letter can be insisted on. s1941.5(f)(2) defines 'eligible tenant' to include a tenant whose immediate family or household member is the victim, provided that tenant is not the alleged perpetrator. Definitions of household member, immediate family member and victim of violent crime advocate all borrow from s1946.7(h); 'abuse or violence' borrows from CCP s1161.3(a)(1). Self-help lock change limited to leases executed on or after 2011-01-01. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-abuse-violence-protections-ca). title: Bulk-Billed Internet Opt-Out
bodyText: If this tenancy is on a month-to-month or other periodic basis and Landlord offers internet service through a bulk-billing arrangement or other subscription with a third-party internet service provider in connection with the tenancy, Tenant may opt out of paying for that subscription. Landlord will not retaliate against Tenant for doing so. If Landlord does not honour Tenant's opt-out, Tenant may deduct the cost of the subscription from rent.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1942.8, added by AB 1414 (Stats. 2025 ch. 506), EFFECTIVE 2026-01-01. Applies to any residential tenancy COMMENCED, RENEWED OR CONTINUING on a month-to-month or other periodic basis on or after that date - so it reaches existing periodic tenancies without any renewal event, which is unusual. s1942.8(c) gives a SELF-HELP RENT DEDUCTION for non-compliance - a remedy shape otherwise reserved in CA for s1942 repair-and-deduct and s1942.2 utility payments. s1942.8(d) preserves the landlord's right to OFFER bulk billing; only compulsion is barred. s1942.8(b) ties retaliation back to s1942.5. Covers wired internet, cellular and satellite service. 'Internet service provider' defined by reference to Civ. Code s3100, NOT READ. Fixed-term tenancies appear to fall outside the section's own words - flagged, not resolved. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-internet-billing-optout-ca). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Mandatory offer of positive rent reporting
bodyText: California requires most residential landlords to offer each tenant the option of having positive rental payment information reported to a consumer reporting agency. For leases entered into on or after April 1, 2025, the offer must be made at the time of the lease and at least once annually after that. The written election must state that reporting is optional, identify each agency, state any fee, explain how to opt in and out, note that a tenant who opts out cannot resume for six months, and include a signature block. A landlord may charge no more than the actual cost or $10 per month, whichever is less, and nothing if there is no actual cost. Non-payment of that fee cannot be reported, cannot be cause for termination, and cannot be deducted from the security deposit. The duty does not apply to a landlord of a building with 15 or fewer units unless the landlord owns more than one building and is a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1954.07, added by AB 2747 (Stats. 2024 ch. 279), eff. 2025-01-01, offers due from 2025-04-01. A landlord DUTY, not merely a permission - the library has nothing like it in any state. s1954.07(l): only POSITIVE information may be reported - complete, timely payments. Late or missed payments are expressly excluded, so this cannot be used as a collection lever. s1954.07(g)(2): an amount tendered toward rent may NOT be applied or credited to the reporting fee - which cuts directly against the base application-of-payments row's fees-first ordering. Screen that row for CA. s1954.07(k): a tenant who opts in does not forfeit ss1941-1942 rights, and a lawful repair-and-deduct or withholding is NOT a late payment for reporting purposes, provided the tenant notifies before rent is due. s1954.06 is a parallel, earlier and stricter regime for ASSISTED HOUSING developments (from 2021-07-01, reporting ALL payments including late ones where applicable) - read, not separately rowed. Small-landlord exemption at s1954.07(j) mirrors s1954.06(j).

title: Notice of belief of abandonment
bodyText: Where rent has been due and unpaid for at least 14 consecutive days and the landlord reasonably believes the tenant has abandoned the property, the landlord may serve a notice of belief of abandonment. The statute supplies the form. The notice must specify a termination date at least 15 days after personal service or 18 days after mailing, and the lease terminates on that date unless the tenant gives written notice before then stating an intent not to abandon and an address for service by certified mail. The property is not deemed abandoned if the rent was not in fact 14 days overdue, if the landlord's belief was not reasonable, if the tenant gave the required notice, or if the tenant paid all or part of the overdue rent in the relevant window. Knowing that the tenant left personal property behind does not by itself make the belief unreasonable.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1951.3, read section-open 2026-09-19 (amended AB 2847, eff. 2019-01-01). s1951.3(a) limits it to NON-commercial property; s1951.35 is the commercial twin with a different trigger. PRESCRIBED FORM at s1951.3(e), 'in substantially the following form'. s1951.3(h) is the trap: this notice DOES NOT satisfy CCP ss1161 or 1162, and giving it does not preclude or replace a pay-or-quit notice. A landlord who serves only this and then files an unlawful detainer has no predicate notice. Connects two regimes already rowed: s1951.3 terminates the lease for s1951.2 damages purposes, and Civ. Code s1991 permits combining this notice with the s1983 abandoned-property notice in a single document - see edu-abandoned-property-ca and edu-abandonment-damages-ca. s1951.3(f)(2) expressly rejects the inference landlords most often draw: leaving possessions behind does not, of itself, justify a finding that abandonment was not reasonably believed.

title: Unbundled Parking
bodyText: Off-street parking is not included in the rent for this unit and is not part of this Lease. Any parking space is leased under a separate parking agreement or addendum. If a fee under that agreement remains unpaid 45 days after it is owed, Landlord may revoke Tenant's right to lease that space.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1947.1, amended AB 2898 (Stats. 2024 ch. 420), eff. 2025-01-01. A LEASE-STRUCTURE mandate, narrow but absolute where it applies. Applies ONLY to a 'qualifying residential property', which requires ALL THREE of: certificate of occupancy issued ON OR AFTER 2025-01-01; SIXTEEN OR MORE residential units; and location in one of TEN NAMED COUNTIES - Alameda, Fresno, Los Angeles, Riverside, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Joaquin, Santa Clara, Shasta, Ventura. A THIRD INSTANCE OF STATE LAW CONFINED TO NAMED LOCALITIES, after Civ. Code ss3485-3486 - here by county rather than city. s1947.1(b)(1): parking 'shall not be included in any residential rental agreement' - it must sit in an addendum or separate agreement - and (b)(2) makes unbundling permanent 'for the life of the property'. s1947.1(d)(1) is the landlord-facing consequence: an unpaid parking fee CANNOT support an unlawful detainer, only revocation of the space after 45 days. So a combined rent-plus-parking three-day notice on such a property is defective. Exclusions at s1947.1(e)(2)(B): units with an integral individual garage (townhouses, row houses), 100 percent deed-restricted affordable developments, LIHTC developments, CalHFA tax-exempt bond financing, and any unit leased to a Section 8 or HUD-VASH voucher holder. The builder needs the certificate-of-occupancy date, the unit count and the county to evaluate it.
