title: Unconscionable Terms
bodyText: West Virginia's unconscionability statutes are written for other transactions: consumer credit sales, consumer leases of goods and consumer loans; sales and leases of goods; rent-to-own agreements; and contracts governed by the common interest ownership act. Each lets a court refuse to enforce an unconscionable agreement or term. None names an ordinary lease of a home, though a lease with an option to buy, where all or a substantial part of the rent is applied to the price, can be a consumer credit sale. For an ordinary residential lease, whether a court may refuse to enforce an unconscionable term is case law, not checked here. Separately, if the Consumer Credit and Protection Act's debt collection rules reach rent (the statutes do not say), you may not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect it.

title: Consumer Protection Act and Leases
bodyText: West Virginia's Consumer Credit and Protection Act makes unfair or deceptive acts in trade or commerce unlawful and defines a consumer transaction as a sale or lease to a natural person for a personal, family, household or agricultural purpose. Its plain-language rule expressly covers written agreements for the rental of residential space, but its private damages action belongs to a person who purchases or leases goods or services, and the statutes do not say whether renting a home is that (court decisions were not checked). A consumer must give you written notice by certified mail and wait 45 days for a cure offer before suing under the Act. Its debt collection rules (no threats, oppression, unreasonable publicity or misleading statements, and no collecting incidental charges not authorized by both the lease and a statute or regulation) may also reach unpaid rent; treat them as applying. Under this library's reading of the Consumer Credit and Protection Act (not settled; court decisions were not checked), a charge added because of a default or for collection, such as a late fee, returned-check fee, collection costs, attorney's fees, a holdover premium or interest beyond what the statute allows, may be collected only if both the lease and a statute authorize it (statutes authorize a reasonable late charge specified in the lease and a fee of up to $25 for a check, draft or order dishonored for insufficient funds or credit), while charges that are part of what the tenant agreed to pay, such as rent, an actual cost the lease makes the tenant's, or an early-termination fee for an option the tenant chooses, are not affected. The Attorney General may sue for repeated and willful violations, with civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation.

title: Tenant Information and Data Breaches
bodyText: No West Virginia statute specifically limits what a landlord may disclose about tenants or applicants. But if you keep tenants' or applicants' names linked to Social Security numbers, driver's license or state ID numbers, or financial account or card numbers (with any code needed for access) in unencrypted, unredacted computerized form, and an unauthorized person accesses and acquires that data in a way you reasonably believe has caused or will cause identity theft or fraud, you must notify each affected West Virginia resident without unreasonable delay. The notice must describe the kinds of information taken, give a phone number or website for questions, and give the major credit bureaus' contact information and how to place a fraud alert or security freeze; if you must notify more than 1,000 people, you must also notify the nationwide consumer reporting agencies. A vendor holding your tenants' data must tell you of a breach. Only the Attorney General enforces this, and civil penalties (up to $150,000 per breach) apply only to repeated and willful violations.

title: Tenant Screening
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets criminal-history look-back periods, income tests, or rules for using credit or eviction reports in tenant screening, and none protects applicants because of a housing voucher or other source of income. The West Virginia Fair Housing Act bars refusing to rent, setting different terms, or advertising a preference because of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex, familial status, blindness, disability or national origin. It does not bar refusing a person convicted of illegally manufacturing or distributing a controlled substance, and it does not require renting to a person whose tenancy would be a direct threat to others' health or safety or would cause substantial physical damage to others' property (you must prove it). An owner-occupied rooming house with no more than four rented rooms is largely exempt, and some small owners are exempt as to familial status only. No West Virginia statute bars or requires asking an applicant for a Social Security number; if you ask, ask every applicant the same way (national origin is a protected class), and if you keep Social Security numbers electronically, the data-breach notice duties apply (see Tenant Information and Data Breaches). Apply written criteria to every applicant the same way; federal law, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act, was not read.

title: Foreign Owners and Tenants
bodyText: A 2025 West Virginia law, in effect since July 10, 2025, bars a prohibited foreign-party-controlled business from acquiring or owning, directly or indirectly, any interest in West Virginia real estate, and bars anyone from holding such an interest as its agent, trustee or fiduciary; the Attorney General can force a judicial sale. A prohibited foreign party includes a citizen or resident of the People's Republic of China who is not a U.S. citizen or resident alien, that government, entities they significantly control, and any government, entity or person a majority of six named state officials identifies as hostile; a business is covered if such a party owns or operates, even in part, a controlling interest (50 percent or more). The law does not say whether leasing a home to such a business gives it an interest in real estate, and it does not restrict individual foreign tenants. A person not subject to the law need not investigate whether another party is. Otherwise any alien may own land in West Virginia as if a citizen.

title: Refusing a Service or Assistance Animal
bodyText: Apart from the White Cane law described below, which may reach a rooming house, no West Virginia statute makes it a crime to refuse an assistance animal in a tenant's home; refusals are handled under the West Virginia Fair Housing Act. A request for an assistance animal (a service, therapy or support animal under 150 pounds) may not be unreasonably denied or delayed, or conditioned on a fee, deposit or pet terms. You may ask for documentation of the disability-related need, and you may deny the animal itself if there is credible evidence, based on an individualized assessment of the specific animal's actual conduct, that it poses a direct threat to others' health or safety or would cause substantial physical damage to others' property that another reasonable accommodation cannot fix. A tenant can sue for actual and punitive damages and attorney's fees; in an administrative case civil penalties can reach $10,000 for a first violation ($25,000 and $50,000 for repeat violators), and in an Attorney General case up to $50,000 for a first violation and $100,000 after. Separately, the state's White Cane law makes it a misdemeanor (fine up to $50) to deny a person with a disability accompanied by a service animal admittance to hotels, lodging places and other places open to the public, which may reach a rooming house or a leasing office (court decisions were not checked), and falsely representing an animal as a service animal to obtain those rights is also a misdemeanor.

title: Plain Language Leases
bodyText: A written residential lease must be written in a clear and coherent manner using words with common and everyday meanings, printed in type of an easily readable size with ink that contrasts with the paper, and organized and captioned by section so it is easily understood. This applies to agreements entered into after April 1, 1982, for the rental of space to be occupied for residential purposes. A violation does not make the lease void or voidable, but if the tenant asks (at signing or later) for the lease to be rewritten to conform and you refuse, the tenant can sue to have it reformed, and the tenant cannot waive this right. Words a state or federal law requires or permits may be used. No statute sets a minimum point size or requires a statement listing the rights the tenant gives up.

title: Electronic Leases and Records
bodyText: West Virginia's Uniform Electronic Transactions Act lets you sign leases and keep records electronically, but only with a tenant who has agreed to do business electronically (agreement can be shown by the circumstances and conduct), and a party who agreed may still refuse to do a later transaction electronically; that right cannot be waived. An electronic record satisfies a law requiring a writing, and an electronic signature satisfies a law requiring a signature. Where a law requires you to give the tenant information in writing, an electronic version counts only if the tenant can keep it when it arrives, and a record the tenant cannot print or store is not enforceable against the tenant; consumer-consent rules may also apply, including telling the tenant beforehand about the right to paper copies and to withdraw consent. Notices of default, eviction or the right to cure under a rental agreement for an individual's primary residence are excluded from the Act, so give those on paper.

title: Delivering Notices
bodyText: West Virginia has no general rule for delivering landlord-tenant notices; each statute sets its own method, and this library's Notices clause defers to those methods rather than replacing them. A notice ending a year-to-year tenancy must be in writing; for a shorter periodic tenancy the statute calls for "like notice" or notice for one full period, which is best read as written notice too, so give it in writing. Either way, yours may be served on the tenant or on anyone holding the premises under the tenant, and the tenant's on any owner or the owner's agent. To recover possession of abandoned property you post a written notice on the property; to dispose of belongings you also mail notice first-class with a certificate of mailing, in an envelope marked "Please Forward", to the property, any known post office box and any forwarding address. The deposit refund and itemization may be delivered personally or mailed to the tenant's last known or forwarding address. An eviction hearing notice is served under the civil procedure rules or by certified mail, return receipt requested. Default, eviction and right-to-cure notices for a primary residence are outside the electronic transactions act, so deliver them on paper; other notices may go by e-mail only if both sides agreed to deal electronically and no statute requires a particular method, such as posting or mail. If you know an electronic notice did not reach the tenant, try again at another e-mail or the postal address on file.

title: Written Leases and Long Terms
bodyText: A lease of land for more than one year is not enforceable unless it, or a note or memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the party to be charged or that party's agent, and no action may be brought on any agreement that is not to be performed within a year unless it is in a signed writing. A lease for a term of more than five years must be created by deed, and once recorded (or a memorandum of it is recorded) it is valid against the landlord's creditors and buyers. Oral leases are still rental agreements under the deposit law, and without a written lease a landlord can still recover reasonable payment for the use and occupation of the property. Electronic records and signatures satisfy these rules when both sides agreed to deal electronically.

title: Where West Virginia Law Lets Your Lease Decide
bodyText: Several West Virginia rules apply only if, or unless, the lease says so. You may take late charges from the security deposit only if they are reasonable and specified in the rental agreement, and other damages or charges only as the rental agreement provides. A pet fee or application fee is outside the deposit rules only if you and the tenant expressly agree in writing that it is nonrefundable. The deposit law's definitions say you may use submetering, energy allocation equipment or a ratio utility billing system if the rental agreement so provides, so put any such arrangement in the lease. Rent is reasonably reduced after a fire or other casualty unless the lease otherwise provides, and rent ends or is reduced when land is taken by eminent domain unless the lease expressly provides otherwise. The statutory notice periods for ending a periodic tenancy do not apply where a special agreement fixes another notice period or none. A lease that gives you greater repair duties than the habitability statute controls. Terms waiving deposit rights or a deceased tenant's estate's right to end the lease are unenforceable or void (see Lease Terms West Virginia Voids).

title: Landlord Registration
bodyText: West Virginia has no statewide landlord or rental registration or licensing requirement. Cities may by ordinance set up a registration, with fees, for buildings found uninhabitable under the local building code and a registration and maintenance program for vacant buildings. A statute in the Municipal Home Rule Program section also says municipalities may not prohibit or effectively limit the rental of a property, or regulate the duration, frequency or location of rentals, and may regulate activities that arise from rental use only if the regulation applies uniformly to all properties, rented or not. Whether that reaches every city, and whether it rules out a registration or inspection ordinance that applies only to rentals, is unsettled (court decisions were not checked). Local rental registration or licensing ordinances were not checked; ask the city or county where the property is located.

title: Selling the Property or Changing Managers
bodyText: When rented property is sold, inherited or assigned, the new owner can enforce the lease's conditions and covenants as you could, and the tenant has the same benefit of the lease's conditions, covenants and promises against the new owner as against you (except any warranty); the transfer is effective without the tenant's attornment (acknowledgment). A tenant who pays rent to you before notice of the transfer is protected, so give the tenant written notice of the sale and where to pay. Whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends must return any deposit owed, whether or not the deposit was handed over. No statute says when the seller's own liability ends or requires notice of a change of manager, but a managing agent who does not disclose the owner's name is treated as the landlord under the deposit law. Converting a rental building to a condominium or other common interest community gives residential tenants 120 days' notice and a 60-day option to buy, and a buyer at a trustee's sale under a deed of trust has its own notice rules (see Tenants After a Trustee's Sale).

title: Automatic Renewal
bodyText: No West Virginia statute regulates automatic renewal clauses in residential leases. Without one, a lease for a fixed term ends on its end date with no notice needed; a year-to-year tenancy ends on written notice at least three months before the end of a year; and a shorter periodic tenancy ends on like notice or on notice of one full period before the end of a period (give it in writing). A special agreement in the lease can fix another notice period or none. Some rules turn on when a lease is entered into or renewed (for example, a deceased tenant's estate may end a lease entered into or renewed on or after July 1, 2012), so treat each renewal as a new lease date. West Virginia's subscription-cancellation statute covers correspondence courses, occupational courses and magazine subscriptions, not leases.

title: Claims Against the Property
bodyText: If someone other than you claims the property or the rent, a tenant's attornment to that stranger (agreeing to hold the property under them or pay them rent) is void unless you consent or it is under a court's judgment, order or decree. No West Virginia statute requires a tenant to tell you about a lawsuit, foreclosure or other claim against the property; only a lease term can require that. When you transfer the property, the transfer is effective without the tenant's attornment, and a tenant who paid you before notice of the transfer is protected.

title: Mediation and Arbitration
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires mediation, arbitration or a pre-suit meeting before a landlord-tenant case. Under West Virginia's Revised Uniform Arbitration Act, an agreement in a record made on or after July 1, 2015 to arbitrate existing or future disputes is valid, enforceable and irrevocable except on grounds for revoking any contract; a court that orders arbitration must stay a related court case; and some of the Act's protections, such as the right to be represented by a lawyer, cannot be waived before a dispute arises. Whether an arbitration clause can stop a residential eviction case, or is enforceable in a residential lease at all, is case law not checked here (federal arbitration law was not read). This library does not offer an arbitration or mediation clause: it could delay the eviction hearing, which is held 5 to 10 judicial days after filing.

title: Distress for Rent
bodyText: West Virginia still allows distress for rent, but only through the courts: rent may be distrained for within one year after it falls due, whether or not the lease has ended, by the sheriff or a deputy sheriff under a warrant a magistrate issues on your affidavit that the rent is justly due. The levy may reach goods of the tenant, an assignee or a subtenant found on the premises or removed within the past 30 days, subject to liens that already existed when the goods were brought onto the premises and to perfected purchase-money security interests. If the tenant intends to remove, is removing, or has within the past 30 days removed belongings from the premises, and you swear that without an attachment there will not be enough property left on the premises to cover the rent, a magistrate may issue an order of attachment for rent that will become payable within one year, after you post the bond the statute requires. A tenant whose property is distrained for rent not due, or attached without good cause, can sue for damages. A resident tenant may set apart property exempt from execution or other process (for example up to $8,000 in household goods), which likely includes distress, and a waiver of those exemptions is void. Never seize a tenant's belongings yourself.

title: Rental Inspections
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets up a state rental inspection program or requires an inspection before renting. Counties and cities may adopt building and housing codes, and may adopt ordinances to repair, close, vacate or demolish unsafe or unsanitary dwellings. A statute in the Municipal Home Rule Program section also says municipalities may not prohibit or effectively limit the rental of a property, or regulate the duration, frequency or location of rentals, and may regulate activities that arise from rental use only if the regulation applies uniformly to all properties, rented or not. Whether that reaches every city, and whether it rules out a registration or inspection ordinance that applies only to rentals, is unsettled (court decisions were not checked). A city code enforcement official must give the owner reasonable advance notice and ask permission to enter (except in exigent circumstances); if the owner cannot be found or refuses, the official may get an administrative search warrant and must give the owner, and any tenant in possession, a copy five days before entering. You must keep a rental in compliance with applicable health, safety, fire and housing codes unless a violation is the fault of the tenant, the tenant's family or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent.

title: Unfit or Condemned Units
bodyText: No West Virginia statute bars collecting rent for a unit that has been condemned or declared unfit for human habitation, or requires you to relocate the tenant. The tenant's protection comes from your duty to keep the unit fit and habitable and in compliance with health, safety, fire and housing codes, and from the casualty rule: if the building is destroyed in whole or part by fire or otherwise without the tenant's fault or negligence, rent is reasonably reduced for buildings the tenant does not own and cannot remove (unless the lease provides otherwise) and the tenant may surrender possession if you do not rebuild as soon as you reasonably can. Cities and counties may adopt ordinances to vacate and close or demolish unsafe dwellings, and a city may charge the owner its costs and file a lien. The habitability statute does not require repairs while the tenant is behind on rent, but only where the lease promises no more: a greater repair duty in the lease controls, and the Landlord Maintenance clause this library uses for West Virginia promises repairs without an exception for unpaid rent.

title: Association Rules and Rentals
bodyText: If the unit is in a condominium, cooperative or planned community under West Virginia's Uniform Common Interest Ownership Act, the declaration, bylaws and association rules govern leasing, and no provision found sets a fee for leasing a unit or lets the association collect rent from your tenant. An amendment changing the uses to which a unit is restricted needs the unanimous consent of the unit owners unless the Act expressly permits otherwise; whether a new leasing restriction is such a change is not settled by the text. The association may levy reasonable fines for violations of the declaration, bylaws and rules after notice and an opportunity to be heard; the Act does not say whether it may fine a tenant directly. The declaration may give lessees the vote on specified matters. For a community created before the Act took effect, generally only listed parts of the Act apply, and the unanimous-consent rule is not among them; but an older community may amend its declaration under the Act, and an older condominium is also governed by the earlier condominium law (not reviewed here), so check how its declaration may be amended. Read the declaration, bylaws and rules before leasing a unit.

title: Medical Cannabis in Rentals
bodyText: West Virginia allows only medical cannabis, for certified patients and caregivers with a valid identification card, and only in forms such as pills, oils, topicals, tinctures, liquids, dermal patches and forms for vaporization or nebulization. Smoking medical cannabis is unlawful, and so is growing it without a permit; other marijuana possession remains a crime. The Medical Cannabis Act protects patients from arrest, prosecution or penalty, or denial of any right or privilege, solely for lawful use, but says nothing about rental housing. A lease may prohibit smoking and growing; whether you may bar a patient's lawful non-smoked use, or refuse to rent to a patient, is not settled by the text (court decisions were not checked).

title: Renting an Accessory Dwelling Unit
bodyText: Under a West Virginia law in effect since June 4, 2026, a city or town may not adopt a policy, regulation or ordinance that restricts, prohibits or otherwise regulates the use of at least one accessory dwelling unit by right on a lot with a single-family dwelling. An accessory dwelling unit is a self-contained, independently accessed living unit with its own cooking, sleeping and sanitation facilities on the same parcel as a larger single-family dwelling; it may be attached, detached or internal, and an attached or detached unit may be no larger than 75 percent of the main dwelling's floor area or 1,000 square feet, whichever is less, and a manufactured home on a permanent foundation may be one. The municipality may not require a family, marital or employment relationship between the occupants of the main dwelling and of the accessory unit, so you may rent it to an unrelated tenant, and it may not require extra parking, separate water and sewer, or a restrictive covenant. It may charge no more than $250 to review an application (plus its usual building fees) and no more than $250 in development impact fees, and may require will-serve letters from the water and sewer systems. A conflicting local rule in effect on or after January 1, 2027 is invalid to the extent of the conflict. The law does not stop a municipality from regulating short-term rentals of 30 days or less, does not override building, fire and other regulatory requirements, and does not bar private restrictive covenants such as association rules; it speaks only of municipalities, not counties.

title: Penalty for Mishandling a Deposit
bodyText: If you fail to follow West Virginia's security deposit law and the failure is willful or not in good faith, the tenant can get a judgment for any deposit you did not return plus damages for annoyance or inconvenience equal to one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld. If the tenant owes you rent, the court credits that award against the rent due. A lease term in which the tenant gives up any deposit right is unenforceable, and if you sue to enforce one, the tenant can recover actual damages and reasonable attorney's fees. Deposit cases are heard in magistrate court or circuit court in the county where the rental is located, and the tenant's other remedies are not limited.

title: Holding a Deposit and Keeping Records
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a landlord who holds tenants' deposits personally to keep them in a separate or escrow account, at any particular bank, or to pay interest on them. A licensed real estate broker (including a broker acting as your property manager) who holds deposits for you rather than passing them to you at once must keep them in a federally insured trust fund account, not mixed with the broker's own money, that does not earn interest unless a Real Estate Commission rule allows it. You must keep itemized records of every deduction you make from a tenant's deposit because the tenant did not comply with the lease, for one year after the tenancy ends. Within 72 hours after a written request, during normal business hours, you must either let the tenant (or the tenant's authorized agent or attorney) inspect that tenant's record of deductions or, at your option, give them a copy.

bodyText: West Virginia does not limit how much you can charge as a security deposit. title: Deposits When the Property Is Sold
bodyText: Whoever holds the landlord's interest in the property when a tenancy ends is bound by West Virginia's deposit rules and must return any deposit the original landlord received that is owed to the tenant. That is true however the interest was acquired or transferred, whether or not the deposit was handed over, and whatever the seller and buyer agreed between themselves. A buyer should therefore account for tenants' deposits at closing. If a tenant has an assignee or subtenant, you may hold a deposit from only one of them.

title: Last Month's Rent and the Deposit
bodyText: Prepaid rent, such as last month's rent collected at signing, is not a security deposit in West Virginia. title: Tenant Utility Bills and Liens on Your Property
bodyText: Whether a tenant's unpaid water, sewer or stormwater bill can be charged to you or become a lien on your rental depends on which West Virginia statute the utility operates under. For a city waterworks, a city sewer service where another provider supplies the water, a combined city water and sewer system, and a public service district, the statute says an owner may not be held liable for a tenant's delinquent charges, and no lien attaches to the property for them, unless the owner contracted directly with the utility for the service. Other statutes, for city sewerage and stormwater works, other city public works (only if the city's ordinance so provides), and the general section on water shutoffs for unpaid sewer and stormwater bills, which covers privately owned and homeowners' association utilities among others, make unpaid charges a lien on the premises served with no exception for a tenant's bill; city sewerage charges are payable by the property owner, and city stormwater charges by the owner or any user. Before relying on a tenant's own account, ask the utility which law it bills under and whether a tenant's unpaid bill can become a lien. A city may not have a lien for unpaid garbage collection fees, but may adopt an ordinance allowing liens for unpaid fire, police or street fees after at least 90 days' certified-mail notice to the owner.

title: Squatters and Unauthorized Occupants
bodyText: Since July 10, 2025, West Virginia's Stop Squatters Act lets a property owner or authorized agent ask a law enforcement officer to remove a squatter from a residential dwelling without going to court, by submitting a completed and verified complaint, if: the person is unlawfully occupying the property; the property was not open to the public when the person entered; you told the person to leave; the person is not a current or former owner or lawful tenant, or an immediate family member of the owner or tenants; and no litigation about the property is pending between you and the person. After preliminary fact-finding, the agency serves a notice to vacate immediately, puts you in possession, and on request removes a person who does not leave; it may charge a fee for serving the notice. The Act defines a squatter as someone unlawfully occupying who is not entitled under a rental or lease agreement or is not authorized by the tenant or owner to be there, and police removal is only for an unauthorized person who is not a current or former lawful tenant, so it does not reach a guest the tenant let in or a current or former tenant, including one holding over; for them, use the court eviction process. A bad-faith complaint can be prosecuted as false swearing, and a person wrongly removed can sue for possession, costs, damages and attorney fees. Separately, knowingly listing or advertising residential property for rent without legal title or authority is a felony, so check the authority of anyone who offers to rent property to you or to manage it for you, and watch for copies of your own listings posted by someone else.

title: Guests' Rights
bodyText: No West Virginia statute gives tenants or their guests rights that limit a lease's guest terms, apart from fair housing law. Under the Stop Squatters Act, police removal is only for an unauthorized person unlawfully occupying the property, and not for a member of the tenant's immediate family, so a guest the tenant has authorized, or a member of the tenant's immediate family, cannot be removed under that process; whether a former guest whose permission has ended can be is not settled. A guest problem is handled under the lease and, if necessary, the court eviction process against the tenant.

title: Children and Familial Status
bodyText: West Virginia's Fair Housing Act bars refusing to rent to, or setting different terms for, a household because of familial status: a child under 18 living with a parent, a legal custodian or their designee with written permission, or a person who is pregnant or securing legal custody of a child. You also may not advertise a preference against children. Reasonable local, state or federal limits on the maximum number of occupants still apply, and qualifying housing for older persons is exempt from the familial-status rules. A rooming house occupied by the owner, with no more than four rooms rented or for rent, is exempt from most of the Act's rental prohibitions, familial status included. For familial status only, the Act also exempts a single-family house rented by a private owner of no more than three such houses, without a broker or a discriminatory advertisement, and rooms or units in a building for up to four families where the owner lives in one of them. Federal fair housing law was not reviewed.

title: Registered Sex Offenders as Tenants
bodyText: West Virginia's residence limits for sex offenders apply only to certain people on court-ordered extended supervised release of 10 years to life: they may not establish a residence within 1,000 feet of a school, a child care facility or a victim's residence, and one convicted of a sexually violent offense against a child may not live in a household where a child under 16 lives unless the person is the child's parent, grandparent or a qualifying stepparent; a court may also impose other residency conditions. These limits bind the supervised person, not the landlord. No West Virginia statute requires a landlord to screen applicants against the registry, disclose a registrant to other tenants, or refuse to rent to one; registrants must report the address of their residence and of any home they lease and regularly visit. Federal housing program rules were not reviewed.

title: Building Rules and Regulations
bodyText: No West Virginia statute governs rules and regulations for ordinary residential rentals, so a rule binds a tenant as a term of the lease: attach the rules to the lease or have the tenant sign for them. Whether you can add or change rules during the term depends on what the lease says and on contract law. A written residential rental agreement, including rules made part of it, must be clear and coherent, use words with common and everyday meanings, be printed in easily readable type and be organized and captioned so it is easily understood; a violation does not void the agreement, but a tenant whose request to conform it is refused may sue to have it reformed. West Virginia's statutory test for enforceable rules applies only to factory-built (manufactured) home rental communities, which this library does not cover.

title: Firearms
bodyText: West Virginia's Constitution protects the right to keep and bear arms for the defense of self, family, home and state. No West Virginia statute addresses a private landlord's lease rules on firearms inside a rented home. An owner, lessee or other person in charge of real property may prohibit carrying firearms on property under their control, and a person who refuses a request to give up the firearm temporarily or to leave commits a misdemeanor; whether that lets you bar firearms inside a unit leased to and controlled by the tenant is not settled. The same law bars an owner or lessee from prohibiting a customer, employee or invitee from keeping a lawfully possessed firearm out of view and locked in or to a vehicle in a parking lot, or from searching the vehicle for one; whether a residential tenant counts as a customer or invitee is not settled, so the safer course is not to ban guns kept locked and out of view in vehicles. Firing a gun within 500 feet of a dwelling house is generally a misdemeanor, with a narrow exception for residents. Cities may not limit firearm possession in a way that conflicts with state law.

title: Smoking, Vaping and Medical Cannabis
bodyText: No West Virginia statute regulates smoking or vaping in private rental housing or limits a lease's no-smoking terms, so the lease governs; local board of health rules and ordinances, which were not read, may add limits. West Virginia's cannabis law is a medical program: use of medical cannabis is lawful only as that act allows, and the act makes it unlawful to smoke medical cannabis. Medical cannabis may be dispensed as pills, oils, topical forms, tinctures, liquids, dermal patches and forms for vaporization or nebulization, but not in dry leaf or plant form unless the state bureau's rules allow it. The act says a patient or caregiver may not be denied any right or privilege solely for lawful use, but it says nothing about leases or landlords, so whether a lease may bar lawful medical use other than smoking, such as vaping, is unsettled; a ban on smoking cannabis matches state law.

title: Tenant Duties Set by Statute
bodyText: West Virginia has no general statute listing a residential tenant's duties; most come from the lease. A few statutes reach tenants. A tenant who commits waste on the property while in possession, without the owner's special permission, is liable for the damage. In a one- or two-family dwelling the owner does not live in, the tenant must do routine maintenance on the smoke detectors. Your duties to meet housing codes and make repairs do not cover conditions caused by the fault of, or repairs needed primarily because of a lack of reasonable care by, the tenant, a family member or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent. A lease promise to leave the premises in good repair means returning them in good and substantial repair, reasonable wear and tear excepted, and does not oblige the tenant to rebuild after a fire or other destruction that was not the tenant's fault unless other words show that intent. Deliberately or negligently damaging the property, or knowingly letting someone else do so, is a ground for a summary eviction case.

title: Landlord Entry
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets a notice period, hours or permitted purposes for a landlord's entry into a residential rental, so the lease's access terms govern, subject to the tenant's right to possession under case law not reviewed here; state in the lease how much notice you will give and when you may enter without notice. title: Cable and Broadband Access
bodyText: If you own or manage premises with dwelling units for three or more households, including a mobile home park, West Virginia bars you from interfering with the installation, maintenance, operation or removal of cable television facilities, from taking any payment from a tenant for permitting cable service, from taking payment from a cable operator beyond just compensation set under the law, and from charging different rent to tenants who do and do not receive cable. You may require that installation meet reasonable conditions to protect the safety, functioning and appearance of the premises and other tenants' convenience, that the cable operator or tenant bear the full cost of installation or removal, and that the operator indemnify you for damage. The operator must give you written notice at least 15 days before installing; the tenant must get the same written notice, or verbal notice of the date and time of entry at least 24 hours ahead. You are entitled to a single payment of just compensation, set by the Public Service Commission if you cannot agree, but not for a later rebuild, upgrade or rewiring. Separately, an agreement or contract made effective after West Virginia's broadband law took effect may not regulate or prevent exterior installation of antennas and equipment used for broadband; whether that reaches a residential lease is unsettled. The federal rule on satellite dishes and antennas was not reviewed.

bodyText: West Virginia has no statute giving a tenant rights because of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, such as a right to end the lease early, to have the locks changed or to avoid eviction, so there is no statutory list of documents a tenant must give you. title: Home-Based Businesses
bodyText: West Virginia makes using a residential dwelling for a home-based business a permitted use. A home-based business is one owned and operated by the owner or tenant of the dwelling and carried on inside it, limited to the sale of lawful goods and services, that does not generate on-street parking or a substantial increase in traffic and has no signage visible from the street. A city may adopt reasonable regulations and may limit or prohibit some activities, such as selling illegal drugs or products containing alcohol or tobacco, operating a sober living home or operating a vape shop, but may not require rezoning, fire sprinklers in a dwelling of one or two units, or a license not required of similar businesses. The permission does not override any deed restriction, covenant or agreement restricting the use of land, or a common interest community's documents, so a lease limiting the property to residential use still binds the tenant; if you will allow a home business, say so in the lease and set your conditions.

title: Returned Check Fees and Remedies
bodyText: If a tenant's check is dishonored for insufficient funds or credit, West Virginia lets you, as the payee, charge a fee of up to $25. You may not impose or collect the fee after a complaint for a worthless-check warrant has been delivered to magistrate court, and once a complaint has been presented there, payment may be made only through the court. State the fee in the lease and keep it at $25 or less. No statute authorizes a fee for a failed electronic payment, so this library's Returned Payments clause charges none, though it lets you require certified funds to replace any failed payment. If the tenant knowingly fails to pay the check amount in cash within 30 days after your written demand, you may sue for the face amount, damages of $500 or the face amount (whichever is less) and reasonable filing costs, but you may not use both that civil remedy and the criminal worthless-check procedure for the same check. The criminal worthless-check statutes do not apply to a postdated check, or to a check you knew or had reason to believe was not covered when you accepted it.

Code § 61-3-39e ('The payee or holder of any dishonored check may impose a fee of up to $25 a worthless check.'; 'This fee may not be imposed or collected after a complaint for warrant has been delivered to magistrate court.'). Reading the $25 as the most a lease may charge for a dishonored check is Claude's reading: if the debt-collection part of the Consumer Credit and Protection Act reaches rent (Claude's reading of W. Va. Code § 46A-2-122(b)-(d); case law not searched), a fee incidental to the obligation needs express authority in 'the agreement creating or modifying the obligation and by statute or regulation' (W. Va. Code § 46A-2-128(d)). Under the library-wide reading of (d) (Claude's reading, case law not searched), a returned-check fee is a charge added because of a default, so it is incidental and needs statutory authority, and § 61-3-39e is the only statute authorizing a dishonored-check fee (WV battery returned-check (returned or dishonored check fees): 59 hits, control 0; known positives passed (0 real sections, 1 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205) (59 hits read by heading: tax, licensing, government and insurance fees; § 55-16-1 is the civil remedy; none authorizes a larger fee). Scope: the fee sentence speaks of 'any dishonored check', and the rest of § 61-3-39e of 'a check, draft or order' dishonored 'because of insufficient funds or credit'; § 55-16-1(a) defines a check as 'a draft or other written order payable on demand and drawn on a bank or depository'. A failed electronic payment is not a written order, so no statute authorizes a fee for it and, under the library-wide reading of § 46A-2-128(d), a fee for it would be an unauthorized incidental charge (Claude's reading, case law not searched). After a complaint: 'In the event complaint for warrant has been presented to magistrate court, payment may be made only through the court' (W. Va. title: No Statutory Grace Period
bodyText: No West Virginia statute gives residential tenants a grace period before rent is late or before a late fee may be charged, so any grace period is up to the lease. title: Rent Increase Notice
bodyText: Apart from the temporary limit on month-to-month rent during a declared state of emergency or preparedness (see the disaster row), no West Virginia statute sets a notice period, frequency limit or cap for raising rent on a home. During a fixed-term lease, the rent stays as the lease states unless the lease provides for an increase; this library's optional Mid-Term Rent Increase clause requires 30 days' written notice and lets the tenant end the lease without a fee instead. For a periodic tenancy, give written notice of the new rent at least as far ahead as the notice needed to end the tenancy: a full rental period before the end of a period for month-to-month or week-to-week, and three months before the end of a year for year-to-year, unless your lease fixes a different notice period. Avoid raising rent soon after a tenant's complaint; see the retaliation row for how retaliation can be raised.

title: Raising Rent During a Lease Term
bodyText: No West Virginia statute addresses a lease term that lets you raise rent during a fixed term, and none forbids one. Without such a term, the rent stated in a fixed-term lease applies for the whole term. If you want the right to raise rent mid-lease, the lease must say so, including when an increase can take effect, how much notice you will give and how the new rent is set. This library offers an optional Mid-Term Rent Increase clause: you give at least 30 days' written notice of the new rent, and the tenant may instead end the lease without a fee before the increase takes effect.

title: Rent Control and Local Rent Limits
bodyText: Apart from the emergency limit below, no West Virginia statute caps the rent a private landlord may charge or how much it may be raised, and no statute expressly allows or forbids local rent control. A provision of the municipal home rule law says municipalities may not prohibit or effectively limit the rental of a property, or regulate the duration, frequency or location of rentals. A municipality may regulate activities that arise when a property is used as a rental only if the regulation applies uniformly to all properties, rented or not (local hotel occupancy taxes are allowed). Whether these limits would bar a local limit on rent amounts has not been decided in the material searched here. Check your city's ordinances. During a declared state of emergency or state of preparedness a temporary price limit applies to month-to-month rentals (see the disaster row).

title: Algorithmic Rent Pricing
bodyText: No West Virginia statute specifically regulates using software or an algorithm to set rent. West Virginia's antitrust act does apply to renting homes: it makes unlawful any contract, combination or conspiracy in restraint of trade, including an agreement between two or more persons for the purpose or with the effect of fixing, controlling or maintaining a market price, rate or fee. Anyone injured in their business or property may sue for three times their damages plus attorney's fees and costs. Set your rents independently and don't share nonpublic rent data with competitors; federal antitrust law also applies but was not read here.

title: Are Fees Rent?
bodyText: In West Virginia's security deposit law, rent means all money owed or paid to you under the rental agreement other than a security deposit, a nonrefundable fee or a payment for damage the tenant caused. Reasonable late charges specified in the lease are applied with rent when you apply the deposit at move-out. Recurring charges the lease calls rent, such as pet rent, should count as rent too, but the statute does not say so expressly, and in any case you may apply the deposit to other charges the lease provides for. That definition applies only within the deposit law. The eviction statute lets you seek possession when a tenant is in arrears in the payment of rent but does not define rent, and no statute settles whether an unpaid fee alone is unpaid rent. This library's lease does not make an unpaid late fee, by itself, grounds for ending the lease.

title: Collection Fees and Notice Fees
bodyText: Don't charge a tenant a collection-agency fee, or a fee for preparing or serving a notice, unless a statute authorizes it. West Virginia's consumer debt-collection law, which by its words reaches anyone collecting a debt that arose from a transaction for personal, family or household purposes, bars collecting any part of a debt collector's fee for its services, collecting a fee incidental to the debt unless both the agreement and a statute or regulation expressly authorize it, and saying that a debt can be increased by fees that cannot legally be added. A violation can cost actual damages plus a $1,000 penalty for each violation. No West Virginia statute authorizes a residential landlord to charge collection costs or notice fees, so this library's lease includes neither.

title: Fees Must Be in the Lease
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential lease to list every fee or sets a notice period for adding one; the rule that a landlord may not collect a fee not listed in the rental agreement applies only to factory-built home sites. Several West Virginia rules still turn on the lease's words: you may apply the deposit to late charges only if they are specified in the rental agreement, and to other charges only as the rental agreement provides; a pet or application fee is outside the deposit only if the tenant expressly agrees in writing that it is nonrefundable; and, if the consumer debt-collection law applies, a fee added because of a default or for collection, such as a late fee, returned-check fee or collection cost, can be collected only if both the agreement and a statute or regulation expressly authorize it. Rent, reimbursement of an actual cost the lease makes the tenant's, and the price of an option the tenant chooses, such as an early-termination fee, are part of what the tenant agreed to pay. List every fee in the lease and add one mid-term only with the tenant's written agreement. You may not charge any fee or deposit for an assistance animal.

title: No Rent Receipt Requirement
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential landlord to give a receipt for each rent payment, even rent paid in cash. One narrow exception: if a tenant aged 65 or older, with household income of no more than $5,000, claims West Virginia's senior citizens' homestead tax relief and asks, you must sign a statement of the gross rent the tenant paid for the year; willfully failing to do so, or willfully giving a false or fraudulent statement, is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $50. The state's consumer-credit receipt rule covers consumer credit sales, consumer loans and consumer leases of goods, not leases of homes. Giving a written receipt for every cash payment and keeping a rent ledger is still good practice, and helps if the amount owed is disputed in court.

title: Interest on Unpaid Rent and Damages
bodyText: In an action for rent, West Virginia allows interest as on other contracts. The court may award prejudgment interest on special or liquidated damages; if the obligation is based on a written agreement, it bears interest until judgment at the rate the agreement sets, and otherwise at a statutory rate of two percentage points above the Fifth Federal Reserve District secondary discount rate in effect on January 2 of the year the claim arose, but not less than 4% or more than 9% a year. A judgment then bears simple interest at the rate figured the same way for the year it is entered. The general legal rate of interest is 6% a year. This library's lease sets no contract interest rate.
notes: WV: 'In any action for rent, or for such use and occupation, interest shall be allowed as on other contracts.' (W. Va. Code § 37-6-9). Prejudgment: W. Va. Code § 56-6-31(b) ('If an obligation is based upon a written agreement, the obligation bears prejudgment interest at the rate and terms set forth in the written agreement until the date the judgment or decree is entered'), (b)(1) (two points above the Fifth Federal Reserve District secondary discount rate on January 2 of the accrual year; 'may not exceed nine percent per annum or be less than four percent per annum'; the Supreme Court's administrative office publishes the rate). Post-judgment: § 56-6-31(a), (c). Legal rate: W. Va. Code § 47-6-5(a) ($6 upon $100 a year); written contracts 'for the loan or forbearance of money' capped at $8 upon $100 (§ 47-6-5(b)); whether overdue rent is a forbearance is Claude's reading, case law not searched. If the debt-collection rules reach rent, interest is 'incidental' and needs authority in the agreement and a statute (W. Va. Code § 46A-2-128(d)); § 37-6-9 supplies it for interest as on other contracts, while interest beyond that is the incidental charge without statutory authority under the library-wide reading of (d) (Claude's reading, case law not searched; whether § 56-6-31(b) itself authorizes a contract rate is unsettled). title: Unclaimed Security Deposits
bodyText: West Virginia's unclaimed property law lists a security deposit as property a holder must turn over to the State Treasurer when the owner doesn't claim it. If you hold deposits in the course of your rental business, a refund you owe a former tenant is presumed abandoned three years after the tenant became entitled to it if the tenant has not contacted you about it in that time. You must then report it and pay it to the Treasurer: reports are due before November 1 each year, covering the 12 months before July 1, and for $50 or more you must first send the tenant written notice 60 to 120 days before filing if you have an address not known to be wrong and the tenant's claim is not time-barred. The deposit law does not let you keep a refund the tenant does not collect; if personal delivery is not reasonably possible and a mailed refund comes back undeliverable, hold it six months for the tenant to claim, then keep it for the unclaimed property process. Late reports carry 12% interest and daily civil penalties; paying the Treasurer in good faith ends your liability for the money.

Code § 36-8-1: 'Property' includes property referred to as or evidenced by a 'security deposit' and must be held, issued or owed in the course of the holder's business; a holder is a person obligated to hold for the account of, or deliver or pay to, the owner property subject to the article; that a residential landlord owing a deposit refund is a holder is Claude's reading. Period: three years under § 36-8-2(a)(18) (all other property, three years after the owner's right to demand it arises) or (a)(6) (money owed to a customer from a retail business transaction, three years); unclaimed means no communication or indication of interest (§ 36-8-2(c)-(d)). Custody when the last known address is in West Virginia and in the other cases in § 36-8-4. Report and owner notice: § 36-8-7(b), (d), (e) ('not more than one hundred twenty days or less than sixty days before filing the report'; conditions in (e)(1)-(3), including 'The claim of the apparent owner is not barred by a statute of limitations'), (g); payment with the report: § 36-8-8(a); good-faith payment relieves the holder: § 36-8-10(b); interest and penalties: § 36-8-24(a)-(c), waived for good faith without negligence, (e); records kept ten years: § 36-8-21(a); a dormancy charge only under a written contract: § 36-8-5. title: Holding Deposits
bodyText: No West Virginia statute specifically regulates a holding deposit taken before a lease is signed. The deposit law treats money, however labeled, paid to be considered as a tenant as an application fee, and any refundable money given to secure performance of a rental agreement as a security deposit; prepaid rent is neither. Unless you and the applicant expressly agree in writing that a payment is a nonrefundable application fee, treat a holding deposit as a refundable security deposit, applied and returned under the deposit rules. Put in writing what the payment is for, whether it will be credited to the deposit or first month's rent, and when and how it will be refunded if no lease is signed.

title: Fees Instead of a Deposit
bodyText: No West Virginia statute authorizes or regulates a fee or insurance product offered in place of a security deposit. Under the deposit law, any refundable money a tenant gives to secure performance or cover damage is a security deposit, while a nonrefundable fee is neither a deposit nor rent, so a genuinely nonrefundable fee in lieu of a deposit falls outside the deposit rules. If you offer one, say in writing that it is nonrefundable and whether it limits the tenant's liability for damage. Deposit insurance and surety products are governed by insurance law, not read here. This library offers no fee-in-lieu clause.

title: Preset Cleaning and Damage Charges
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets or forbids a lease schedule of preset cleaning, carpet or repair charges. When the tenancy ends you may apply the deposit to damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the lease, less reasonable wear and tear, and to other damages or charges the rental agreement provides for, with a written itemization. A preset charge the tenant pays whatever the unit's condition, such as repainting or carpet cleaning after normal use, risks being treated as a charge for reasonable wear and tear or as a waiver of the tenant's deposit rights; the statute does not settle it. If you use a schedule, tie each charge to actual damage or uncleanliness beyond normal wear and itemize it.

title: What Counts as an Assistance Animal
bodyText: Under West Virginia's Fair Housing Act, an assistance animal is any service, therapy or support animal weighing less than 150 pounds, with or without specific training or certification, that works, provides assistance or performs tasks for a person with a disability, or provides emotional support that alleviates one or more identified symptoms or effects of the disability. A request for one is a request for a reasonable accommodation to your animal rules: it may not be unreasonably denied or delayed, or conditioned on a fee, deposit or other terms that apply to pets. These rules reach small landlords too; the exemptions are narrow (see the fair housing row). An animal of 150 pounds or more is outside the state definition, but the general duty to make reasonable accommodations, and federal law (not read here), may still require you to consider the request.
notes: WV: Definition: 'any service, therapy or support animal, weighing less than 150 pounds, with or without specific training or certification, that works, provides assistance, or performs tasks for the benefit of a person with a disability, or provides emotional support that alleviate one or more identified symptoms or effects of a person's disability' (W. Va. Code § 16B-18-3(p)). Animal rules 'are subject to the reasonable accommodation requirements' (W. Va. Code § 16B-18-5(f)(10)); 'A request for a reasonable accommodation may not be unreasonably denied, conditioned on payment of a fee or deposit or other terms and conditions applied to applicants or residents with pets, and a response may not be unreasonably delayed.' (W. Va. Code § 16B-18-5(f)(10)(D)). Coverage: the familial-status exemptions in § 16B-18-4(a)(1)-(2) apply 'Solely for the purposes of familial status'; an owner-occupied rooming house with no more than four rooms for rent is outside § 16B-18-5 (W. Va. Code § 16B-18-4(a)). That a 150-pound or heavier animal may still need consideration under § 16B-18-5(f)(3)(B) is Claude's reading. title: Misrepresenting a Service Animal
bodyText: In West Virginia it is a misdemeanor to falsely claim that an animal is a service animal, or that you are blind or have a disability, to obtain the rights the state's White Cane law gives in public places, public transportation, hotels, lodging places and other places of public accommodation. The penalty is a fine of up to $200, up to 10 days in jail, or both, rising to $1,000, 30 days, or both for a repeat offense. That law does not by its terms reach a request to keep an assistance animal in a rental home, and no West Virginia statute penalizes a false assistance-animal request in housing. Handle housing requests under the fair housing rules, which let you ask for documentation from a professional treatment provider of the disability-related need.

title: Towing and Abandoned Vehicles
bodyText: West Virginia has no statute setting the signs, notice or fees for a private property owner who has a vehicle towed from a parking lot. A vehicle left on private property without the consent of the owner or person in control for more than five days is an abandoned motor vehicle, and abandoning one there is a misdemeanor. Police and other enforcement agencies may take it, but only after sending you and the vehicle's owner, if known, 30 days' notice by registered or certified mail; the owner and lienholders may then reclaim it within 10 days of notice by paying the towing and storage charges. Tow companies' maximum rates for wrecked or disabled vehicles are set by the Public Service Commission. A tenant's vehicle parked with your permission is not abandoned; enforce parking rules through the lease, and check local ordinances before towing.

title: Storage Units and the Self-Storage Lien Act
bodyText: West Virginia's Self-Service Storage Lien Act gives operators of self-service storage facilities a lien on stored property and a sale procedure, but it works through a storage rental agreement that must contain the statements the Act requires. Unlike the state's storage-insurance statute, the lien Act does not expressly exclude storage rented with a home, so whether it reaches a storage unit you rent to a tenant with an apartment is not settled by statute. This library's storage clause does not invoke the Act. Treat belongings a tenant leaves in a storage space like other property left behind at the end of a tenancy.
notes: WV: Lien Act scope: a self-service storage facility is 'any real property used for renting or leasing individual storage spaces in which the occupants themselves customarily store and remove their own personal property' (W. Va. Code § 38-14-2(8)); 'An occupant may not use a self-service storage facility for residential purposes.' (W. Va. Code § 38-14-7(c)); lien and required statements (W. Va. Code § 38-14-3(a), (c)); late fee (§ 38-14-4); sale after 60 days in default with notice (§ 38-14-5). Insurance statute excludes 'other than storage spaces which are leased or rented as an incident to the lease or rental of residential property or dwelling units' (W. Va. Code § 33-12-38(a)(7)); the lien Act has no such words (WV battery f-storage (storage spaces rented with a dwelling): 6 hits, control 0; known positives passed (2 real sections, 0 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205) (6 hits: § 33-12-38 and art. 38-14). Whether the Act reaches a landlord's tenant storage is Claude's reading, case law not searched. Left-behind property: `edu-abandoned-property-wv`, `edu-post-eviction-property-wv`. Shared `storage-space-ks-oh-ca` tagged. Boundary: the West Virginia Code and Constitution were searched; legislative rules, case law and local ordinances were not. title: Out-of-State Landlords
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires an out-of-state landlord to appoint an agent in West Virginia. But a nonresident who has an interest in, uses or possesses real property in West Virginia is treated as having appointed the Secretary of State to receive process in a circuit court case arising from it; the Secretary of State mails the papers to your out-of-state address by registered or certified mail, and a default judgment may be entered if you don't appear and defend within 30 days. Keep your address current and consider naming a local manager to receive notices. Under the deposit law, a managing agent who does not disclose the owner's name is treated as the landlord.
notes: WV: W. Va. Code § 56-3-33(a)(6) ('Having an interest in, using, or possessing real property in this state'), (a) (Secretary of State as attorney 'in any action or proceeding against him or her, in any circuit court in this state'), (b) (cause of action must arise from the act), (c) (service; 'If any defendant served with summons and complaint fails to appear and defend within 30 days of service, judgment by default may be rendered against him or her at any time thereafter'), (f) (cumulative). By its words the section covers circuit court actions; deposit suits may also be brought in magistrate court (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-5(b)) (Claude's reading). Landlord includes 'a managing agent of the premises who fails to disclose the name of such owner or lessor' (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-1(5)). title: Changing Terms of a Periodic Tenancy
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets a notice period for changing the terms or rules of a periodic tenancy, such as a month-to-month lease. A change the tenant has not agreed to is safest with written notice at least as far ahead as the notice needed to end the tenancy (a full rental period before the end of a period for month-to-month or week-to-week, three months before the end of a year for year-to-year), so the tenant can choose to leave. During a fixed term, change terms only as the lease allows or with the tenant's written agreement.

title: Accepting Rent After a Default
bodyText: No West Virginia statute says whether accepting rent, or part of the rent, after a tenant's default or after a notice to quit waives your right to end a residential tenancy or seek possession. That is a question of case law, which was not searched here. If you accept a payment after giving notice or filing for possession, say in writing that you accept it without waiving the default or your right to possession. Separately, in an ejectment or unlawful detainer case for unpaid rent, a statute ends the case if all the rent and arrears, with interest and costs, are paid or tendered to you or your attorney, or paid into court, before trial (see the redemption row).

title: Taxes on Rent
bodyText: Counties and cities may impose a hotel occupancy tax on hotel rooms, which include boarding houses, condominiums, cabins, lodges and tourist homes where the public can rent sleeping accommodations. The tax does not apply to sleeping accommodations rented month-to-month or for 30 days or longer from the start at a boarding house, condominium, cabin, tourist home, apartment or home. Where it applies, the operator collects it from the guest, states it separately on bills and may not advertise that it will absorb it; if you rent through a booking platform that meets the statute's sales thresholds, the platform must collect and remit it for you. No West Virginia statute expressly taxes ordinary long-term residential rent. If you rent short-term, ask your county or city and the State Tax Department whether occupancy tax or consumers sales tax applies.
notes: WV: W. Va. Code § 7-18-1(a) (county or municipal privilege tax 'upon the occupancy of hotel rooms'), (d) (imposed on the consumer, collected by the operator); § 7-18-3(c) (hotel includes 'boarding houses, hotels, motels, inns, courts, condominiums, lodges, cabins, and tourist homes'), (e)(2) (hotel room excludes 'Sleeping accommodations rented on a month-to-month basis or other rental arrangement for 30 days or longer at the inception at a boarding house, condominium, cabin, tourist home, apartment, or home'); § 7-18-4(a), (d) (separately stated; no absorbing the tax), (b)-(c) (a marketplace facilitator with $100,000 in West Virginia sales or 200 transactions in the current or preceding calendar year collects and remits on the operator's behalf); Class I cities: § 8-13-3. Sales tax reaches the furnishing of services other than professional and personal services (W. Va. Code § 11-15-8; 'Service' in § 11-15-2(b)(18)); whether it reaches lodging or rent is set by Tax Department rules, not searched. No statute taxing long-term residential rent: (WV battery f-rent-tax (sales or occupancy tax on residential rent or lodging): 13 hits, control 0; known positives passed (2 real sections, 0 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205) (WV battery rent-tax (sales or occupancy tax on residential rent): 10 hits, control 0; known positives passed (0 real sections, 1 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205) (13 hits, all hotel occupancy or lodging provisions). title: Late Fees
bodyText: No West Virginia statute caps a late fee on a residential lease or sets a grace period before one may be charged. State the fee and when it applies in the lease and keep it reasonable: you may take late charges out of the security deposit only if they are reasonable charges for late payment of rent specified in the rental agreement. West Virginia's consumer debt-collection law bars collecting a charge incidental to an obligation unless both the agreement and a statute or regulation expressly authorize it, with a penalty of up to $1,000 per violation; it does not say whether it reaches rent, and this library reads the deposit statute's recognition of reasonable, agreed late charges as that authority, but courts have not been checked on either point. A very large fee also risks being treated as an unenforceable penalty. Unpaid rent separately bears interest as on other contracts. This library's lease does not let you end the tenancy for an unpaid late fee alone.
notes: WV: No residential late-fee cap or grace period (WV battery late-fee (late fees or late charges for rent): 13 hits, control 0; known positives passed (1 real section, 1 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205) (WV battery late-fee-nc (late fees or late charges for rent (no context limb)): 51 hits, control 0; known positives passed (1 real section, 1 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205) (WV battery f-grace (grace period before rent is late or a late fee applies): 3 hits, control 0; known positives passed (0 real sections, 2 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205) (WV battery f-grace-nc (grace period before rent is late or a late fee applies (no context limb)): 26 hits, control 0; known positives passed (0 real sections, 2 synthetic); scope CODE 31329, CONST 205): the hits are licensing renewals, tax and municipal fees, consumer credit sales and loans (W. Va. Code §§ 46A-3-112, 46A-3-113, 46A-2-115, which reach only consumer credit sales and consumer loans), self-service storage (W. Va. Code § 38-14-4), unit owners' associations (W. Va. Code § 36B-3-102) and the deposit statute; none governs residential rent. Deposit: 'The payment of rent due, including the reasonable charges for late payment of rent specified in the rental agreement' (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-2(b)(1)); rent includes all money owed under the rental agreement other than a deposit, a nonrefundable fee or payment for tenant damage (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-1(11)). Debt collection: no debt collector may collect 'any interest or other charge, fee or expense incidental to the principal obligation unless such interest or incidental fee, charge or expense is expressly authorized by the agreement creating or modifying the obligation and by statute or regulation' (W. Va. Code § 46A-2-128(d)); a 'claim' is an obligation from a transaction 'primarily for personal, family or household purposes' (W. Va. Code § 46A-2-122(b)); penalty W. Va. Code § 46A-5-101(1). That § 37-6A-2(b)(1) is statutory authority for a reasonable, agreed late charge is Claude's reading; whether the debt-collection sections reach rent, and the penalty doctrine, are case law not searched (`edu-knowing-use-penalty-wv`, `edu-consumer-protection-wv`). Interest: 'In any action for rent, or for such use and occupation, interest shall be allowed as on other contracts' (W. Va. Code § 37-6-9). The shared `late-fee` is tagged (its figures are the landlord's); `default-by-tenant-wv` keeps the late-fee-alone sentence. Grace periods: `edu-no-rent-grace-period-wv`. title: Land Taken by Eminent Domain
bodyText: If all of the leased property is taken by eminent domain (condemnation for public use), the tenant's duty to pay rent ends, unless the lease expressly provides otherwise. If only part of the property, or an easement or other interest in it, is taken, the rent is reduced in proportion to the value of what was taken compared with the whole, again unless the lease expressly provides otherwise. These rules don't affect any right the tenant has to compensation from the condemning authority for the value of the lease or the tenant's property, beyond the rent the tenant no longer owes. This library's lease leaves these rules in place.
notes: WV: 'Whenever the whole of any tract of land which is under lease is taken under the power of eminent domain, the liability of any tenant of such land to pay rent thereon shall terminate unless the lease expressly provide otherwise.' (W. Va. Code § 37-6-29); a partial taking reduces the rent 'in the proportion which the value of the land or interest taken bears, at the time of such taking, to the total value of the land upon which rent was payable' (same section); the tenant's compensation claim is preserved where its value exceeds the rent relieved (same section). Rule 50: the lease may 'expressly provide otherwise'; the library makes no such provision (a drafting choice: no reason to shift a public taking onto the tenant). New topic key `eminent-domain`: no existing key covers a condemnation of leased land (rule 58); `casualty-termination` is fire and other destruction (`casualty-wv`). title: Municipal Service Fees
bodyText: West Virginia cities may charge reasonable fees for services such as police and fire protection, street maintenance and lighting, and garbage collection, imposed by ordinance on the users of the service; in a rental, the tenant may be the user billed. A city may not have a lien on property for these fees, except that it may adopt an ordinance allowing a lien on real property for unpaid fire, police or street fees after at least 90 days' notice to the owner by certified mail. A lease may lawfully require the tenant to reimburse you for a fee billed to you, but this library does not offer such a clause: who is billed varies by city and ordinance, and the tenant is often billed directly as the user. If you want one, add your own clause after taking advice, and state the fee, its amount and how you will bill it in the lease.
notes: WV: A municipality furnishing 'police and fire protection', street services and 'the collection and disposal of garbage' may 'impose by ordinance upon the users of the service reasonable rates, fees, and charges' (W. Va. Code § 8-13-13(a)); 'A municipality may not have a lien on any property as security for payments due under subsection (a) of this section except as provided in subsection (e) of this section' (W. Va. Code § 8-13-13(d)); the lien ordinance for 'unpaid and delinquent fire, police, or street fees' requires certified-mail notice to the property owner with a payment date 'no less than 90 days from the date the notice is mailed' (W. Va. Code § 8-13-13(e)). Water, sewer and other utility charges: `edu-utility-liens-wv`. Rule 54 declined option (canvass proposal F-3): a reimbursement clause like `government-fee-reimbursement-ky` is lawful as a contract term (no statute bars it), but not offered: the fee is often billed to the tenant as the user already, and who pays turns on each city's ordinance, which this library can't know. Under the library's reading of W. Va. Code § 46A-2-128(d), a reimbursement of an actual fee the lease makes the tenant's is part of the tenant's obligation, not an incidental charge (Claude's reading; case law not searched; WV log §6.3). Local ordinances not searched. title: Landlord's Access
bodyText: Landlord, its agents and contractors may enter the property to complete repairs, maintenance, modifications, renovations or improvements; to inspect the property; to show it to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees, tenants or contractors; to ensure the protection and safety of the property and its occupants; to complete work ordered by a government entity; or to respond to a written request from Tenant. Except in an emergency, Landlord will give Tenant written notice at least 24 hours before the entry, stating the date and approximate time of the entry and its specific purpose. The notice will be sent by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing (only if it will be delivered at least 24 hours before the entry), affixed to the door of the property, or, if Tenant has elected electronic delivery, sent by e-mail, text message or Landlord's electronic tenant portal. Landlord will enter only between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday, unless Tenant agrees in writing to another time, and Tenant may agree in writing to an entry on less than 24 hours' notice. Landlord may enter without notice in an emergency to ensure the imminent protection or preservation of the property, the imminent protection and safety of any occupant, or the health, safety and welfare of other tenants and staff. If Tenant reports a housing code violation, Tenant will give Landlord access to the property within 24 hours after notifying Landlord.
notes: MD: Overrides `landlords-access`, whose 'normal business hours' and unspecified 'notice' do not state Maryland's written-notice content, delivery methods or hours. Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-221(a) (purposes, including 'Showing the leased premises to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees, tenants, or contractors'); (b)(1)(ii) ('Enter only between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday, or another time agreed on, in writing, by the tenant'); (b)(2) emergency; (c)(1) ('at least 24 hours in advance'); (c)(2) contents ('The date and approximate time that the landlord intends to enter'); (c)(3) delivery (first-class mail 'with a certificate of mailing', 'Paper notice affixed to the door', electronic delivery 'If elected by the tenant'); (c)(4) proof of transmission; (c)(5) shorter notice by written agreement; (f) ('the tenant shall provide the landlord access to the leased premises within 24 hours'). Enacted by 2025 Md. Laws ch. 564, effective October 1, 2025. Remedies (injunction, quiet-enjoyment damages) in `edu-entry-remedies-md`. The clause does not adopt a standing agreement to other hours, since § 8-221(b)(1)(ii) contemplates the tenant's agreement to another time. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Default by Tenant
bodyText: Tenant will be in default under this Lease if Tenant fails to pay Rent when due and does not cure the failure within the time period specified by applicable law after receiving written notice from Landlord. Tenant will also be in default if Tenant fails to comply with any other obligation under this Lease and does not cure the failure after receiving written notice. Landlord need not give Tenant an opportunity to cure any breach, including a failure to pay Rent, where applicable law permits Landlord to proceed without one. Except as required by applicable law, Tenant's failure to pay an assessed late fee, apart from the underlying Rent itself, will not by itself entitle Landlord to terminate this Lease or pursue eviction. If Tenant breaches this Lease, Landlord may repossess the property before the end of the Term by giving Tenant written notice that Tenant is in violation of this Lease and that Landlord desires to repossess the property, at least 30 days before Landlord files for possession, or at least 14 days before if the breach involves behavior by Tenant or a person on the property with Tenant's consent that demonstrates a clear and imminent danger of doing serious harm to themselves, other tenants, Landlord, Landlord's property or representatives, or any other person on the property.
