If Tenant is in default, Landlord may exercise all rights and remedies available under applicable law, including terminating this Lease, regaining possession of the property, and recovering unpaid Rent, late fees, and reasonable costs and expenses, less amounts obtained from the Security Deposit. Landlord will use reasonable efforts to mitigate damages resulting from Tenant's default to the extent required by applicable law. To the extent permitted under applicable law, the prevailing party may recover from the other party court costs and reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses incurred in connection with any legal proceedings related to this Lease.
notes: MD: Overrides `default-by-tenant` to state the term the breach-of-lease action requires. Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402.1(a)(1)(i) is available only 'where an unexpired lease for a stated term provides that the landlord may repossess the premises prior to the expiration of the stated term if the tenant breaches the lease', after '30 days’ written notice that the tenant is in violation of the lease and the landlord desires to repossess the leased premises' or 14 days' notice for behavior that 'demonstrates a clear and imminent danger of the tenant or person doing serious harm'; the court must find the breach 'substantial and warrants an eviction' (§ 8-402.1(b)(1)). Shared wording kept otherwise. Rent limb: the statutory pre-filing notice gives the tenant 10 days to cure (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-401(c)(1)), and redemption continues to execution (§ 8-401(h)); the clause states no period (rule 43). The no-cure sentence reaches both limbs; § 8-402.1 itself gives no cure right. Attorney's fees: a residential rent-court judgment is for rent, late fees and costs (§ 8-401(e)(2)(iv)); lease fees are named only for nonresidential tenancies (§ 8-401(e)(2)(v)3); 'To the extent permitted' keeps the clause from claiming more (`edu-attorney-fees-rent-court-md`); the fee sentence is reciprocal. Mitigation is non-waivable (§ 8-207(d)). Abuse victims have a rebuttable presumption against eviction for breach (§ 8-5A-04; `edu-abuse-eviction-defense-md`). rule_type REQUIRED because the breach-of-lease repossession remedy is unavailable without this term. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Holding Over
bodyText: If Tenant does not vacate the property when this Lease or the tenancy ends, Landlord may pursue any remedy allowed by law to recover possession, and Tenant will be liable for the actual damages caused by holding over, which will not be less than the Rent apportioned for the holdover period at the rate under this Lease. If Landlord consents to Tenant remaining in the property after this Lease ends, Tenant will become a month-to-month tenant (or a week-to-week tenant if Tenant was a week-to-week tenant before holding over) on the same terms, terminable as Maryland law provides. Landlord's acceptance of any payment after giving Tenant a notice to quit or a notice of breach of this Lease does not waive that notice or any judgment for possession, and does not by itself create a new tenancy.
notes: MD: Overrides `holdover` (and is used instead of `holdover-ca`). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402(a)(1)-(2) (holdover tenant liable for 'the actual damages caused by the holding over', which 'may not be less than the apportioned rent for the period of holdover at the rate under the lease'); (a)(4) other lease remedies not limited; (c)(5)(i) ('Acceptance of any payment after notice but before eviction shall not operate as a waiver of any notice to quit ... unless the parties specifically otherwise agree in writing'); § 8-402.1(d)(1) same for breach notices; § 8-402(d) consented holdover becomes week-to-week if weekly before, 'and a periodic month-to-month tenant in all other cases' unless the written lease says otherwise 'and initialed by the tenant'; the clause follows the statutory default (week-to-week only where the tenancy was week-to-week before the holdover, so a stated-term lease with weekly rent becomes month-to-month), so no initials are needed. Landlord's notice to end the tenancy (60 days for a term of more than a week or month-to-month) is in `edu-termination-notice-periods-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Due at Signing
bodyText: Tenant will pay Landlord the following amounts, at the time specified for each: [specify what is due and when here, e.g. first month's Monthly Rent ({{monthly_rent}}) due at signing; Security Deposit ({{security_deposit}}) due at signing]. Landlord will not require Tenant to pay more than the first month's Monthly Rent and the Security Deposit in order to begin this Lease and move in. Any pet deposit and any prepaid last month's Rent is part of the Security Deposit.
notes: MD: Overrides `due-at-signing`, whose example adds last month's Rent. Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(11) (a lease may not require 'a tenant to pay more than the sum of the security deposit under § 8-203(b) of this subtitle and the first month’s rent in order to commence the lease and occupy the premises'); § 8-203(a)(3) ('Security deposit' means 'any payment of money, including payment of the last month’s rent in advance of the time it is due' given to protect against nonpayment or damage), so a pet deposit or prepaid last month's rent is within the deposit and its cap (§ 8-203(b)(1), `edu-security-deposit-cap-md`). Whether a one-time nonrefundable fee counts toward (d)(11) is not settled by the text (case law not searched); `edu-upfront-pet-fees-md` and `edu-due-at-signing-limit-md` give the cautious reading. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Keys
bodyText: At the start of the Term, Tenant will receive the keys specified by Landlord and will sign a receipt acknowledging the number and type of keys provided. Tenant will return all keys to Landlord at the end of the Term. If Tenant fails to return all keys or requires a replacement, Landlord may re-key the applicable locks and charge the cost to Tenant. Tenant may not duplicate keys without Landlord's consent. This Section does not apply to a lock change requested by a Tenant who is a victim of abuse under Maryland law; for that lock change, Landlord may charge only the reasonable cost of changing the locks, which Tenant may pay within 45 days after the change, and Maryland law governs the rest.
notes: MD: Overrides `keys` (fee screen, kickoff). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-5A-05(c)(1) (landlord 'shall change the locks on the leased premises by the close of the next business day' after a written request with a protective or peace order); (d)(2) (may charge 'a fee to the tenant not exceeding the reasonable cost of changing the locks'); (e)(1) ('the tenant shall pay the fee within 45 days of the date the locks are changed'); (e)(2) unpaid fee may be charged as additional rent or withheld from the deposit; (c)(2) tenant's own certified locksmith if the landlord does not act (preserved by `no-alterations`). Ordinary re-keying cost: no Maryland statute. `edu-abuse-lock-change-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Acceptable Payment Methods
bodyText: Rent and other amounts due under this Lease must be paid by one of the following methods: [list accepted payment methods here, e.g. check or money order, electronic payment service, online payment portal]. Landlord may change the accepted payment methods on reasonable written notice to Tenant. This Section does not limit Tenant's right under Maryland law, after a judgment for possession for nonpayment of Rent, to redeem the property before the eviction is carried out by paying the amount due in cash, by certified check or money order, or by a check issued by or for a government agency.
notes: MD: Overrides `acceptable-payment-methods`. Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-401(h)(1) (tenant may redeem 'by tendering in cash, certified check, or money order' all past due amounts plus costs and fees 'at any time before actual execution of the eviction order'); (h)(2) ('An electronic or written check issued by a political subdivision or on behalf of a governmental entity shall have the same legal effect'); (h)(3) no redemption after three rent judgments of possession in the prior 12 months (`edu-redemption-md`). No Maryland statute otherwise regulates payment methods (Maryland canvass, topic acceptable-payment-methods). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Electronic Signatures
bodyText: [BUILDER: display this Section conspicuously, with its heading in bold and its own initials line.] ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES (SEPARATE CONSENT). All individuals indicated in the Basic Terms as comprising Tenant will sign this Lease and related attached Addenda where indicated. By initialing below, Tenant separately agrees that Landlord and Tenant may sign this Lease and its Addenda electronically, and that a copy of this Lease bearing a party's electronic signature, or delivered by facsimile or as a digital copy, has the same full force and effect as a manually executed original. Landlord gives the same consent. This consent covers signing; it does not by itself allow any notice to be given electronically, which is governed by this Lease's Notices section and Maryland law. Tenant's initials: [______]
notes: MD: Overrides `electronic-signatures`. Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 21-104(b)(3) ('a provision to conduct a transaction electronically may not be contained in a standard form contract unless that provision is conspicuously displayed and separately consented to'); (b)(1) the electronic-transactions title applies only where each party 'has agreed to conduct transactions by electronic means'. § 21-102(b)(4)(ii) excludes from the title laws governing notice of 'Default, acceleration, repossession, foreclosure, eviction, or the right to cure, under ... a rental agreement for a primary residence of an individual', so the consent is limited to signing; electronic notices rest on the specific statutes that allow them 'If elected by the tenant' (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. §§ 8-209(b)(2), 8-221(c)(3), 8-401(c)(2); `electronic-notice-election-md`, `edu-ueta-eviction-notice-exclusion-md`). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Security Deposit and Receipt
bodyText: Tenant shall pay Landlord a security deposit of {{security_deposit}} (Security Deposit). Landlord received the Security Deposit on [date received], and this Section is Tenant's receipt for it. Landlord may withhold all or part of the Security Deposit only for unpaid Rent, for damage due to Tenant's breach of this Lease, and for damage by Tenant or Tenant's family, agents, employees, guests or invitees in excess of ordinary wear and tear to the property, common areas, major appliances and furnishings owned by Landlord. The Security Deposit is not liquidated damages. Tenant has the following rights: (1) to have the property inspected by Landlord in Tenant's presence for the purpose of making a written list of damages that exist at the start of the tenancy, if Tenant requests it by certified mail within 15 days of Tenant's occupancy; (2) to be present when Landlord inspects the property at the end of the tenancy to determine whether any damage was done, if Tenant notifies Landlord by certified mail at least 15 days before Tenant's intended move of Tenant's intention to move, the date of moving, and Tenant's new address; (3) to have that inspection conducted within 5 days before or after Tenant's stated date of intended moving, and to be notified by Landlord in writing of the date of the inspection; (4) to receive, by first-class mail delivered to Tenant's last known address, a written list of the charges against the Security Deposit claimed by Landlord and the actual costs, within 45 days after the tenancy ends; and (5) to have any unused portion of the Security Deposit, with the interest Maryland law requires, returned by first-class mail addressed to Tenant's last known address within 45 days after the tenancy ends. If Landlord fails to comply with the security deposit law, Landlord may be liable to Tenant for a penalty of up to 3 times the security deposit withheld, plus reasonable attorney's fees.
notes: MD: Overrides `security-deposit-use`, whose uses ('to remedy a Tenant default', cleaning 'only if ... substantially less clean') are not Maryland's list, and which carries no receipt. Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-203(c)(1)-(2) (landlord 'shall give the tenant a receipt'; 'The receipt shall be included in a written lease'); § 8-208(c)(3) (a lease shall include 'A receipt for the security deposit as specified in § 8-203.1'); § 8-203.1(a)(1)-(7) receipt contents, followed nearly word for word; § 8-203.1(c) $25 if no receipt; § 8-203(f)(1)(i) withholding list ('for unpaid rent, damage due to breach of lease or for damage by the tenant or the tenant’s family, agents, employees, guests or invitees in excess of ordinary wear and tear'); (f)(1)(vi) tenant 'shall be advised of the tenant’s rights under this subsection in writing at the time of the tenant’s payment'; (f)(2) ('The security deposit is not liquidated damages'); (e)(1) return 'together with simple interest'; (l) 'No provision of this section may be waived in any lease'. Cap, escrow, interest, itemization documents and penalties are in education rows (`edu-security-deposit-cap-md`, `edu-deposit-escrow-md`, `edu-deposit-interest-md`, `edu-deposit-penalties-md`, `edu-move-out-inspection-md`). The court-surcharge deduction is the option `filing-surcharge-deposit-md`. Dormant `security-deposit-cap-md` and `security-deposit-interest-md` stay off: a cap and an interest duty are limits on the landlord, which are education rows unless a statute requires lease text (MD log §5). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. §§ 8-203(c), 8-203.1(a), 8-208(c)(3) | CONSTRAINED_TERM

title: Pet Policy
bodyText: Tenant may keep only pets identified in writing to and approved by Landlord: [list approved pets, or state that no pets are permitted]. Any refundable pet deposit ({{pet_deposit}}, if applicable) is part of the Security Deposit, counts toward the limit on the total Security Deposit, and will be held, receipted, applied and returned with it. Tenant will pay pet rent of {{pet_rent_amount}} per month, if applicable. Tenant is responsible for all damage, waste removal, odor and disturbance caused by a pet, and will reimburse Landlord for claims caused by Tenant's pet, except to the extent a claim arises from Landlord's own omission, fault, negligence or other misconduct. Landlord may revoke approval of a pet that becomes a nuisance or safety concern. Landlord may enter the property in connection with a pet only as this Lease's Access & Entry terms and Maryland law permit, including without notice in an emergency, and will not seize or remove a pet except through a court process; Landlord may report a pet to animal control or law enforcement, which may act under their own authority. This Section does not apply to a service animal or other assistance animal.
notes: MD: Overrides `pet-policy` (found in the independent check, MD log §13). Its pet-removal power is a lease term authorizing the landlord to take the tenant's personal property during the tenancy, which a Maryland lease may not contain (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(6) ('Authorizes the landlord to take possession of the leased premises, or the tenant’s personal property unless the lease has been terminated')), and its entry grounds (incapacity, suspected neglect) are not limited to emergencies under the entry statute (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-221; `landlords-access-md`). Its uncapped indemnity would reach claims caused by the landlord's own negligence (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-105 ('If the effect of any provision of a lease is to indemnify the landlord, hold the landlord harmless')), which § 8-208(d)(7) bars; the reimbursement sentence carves that out. A refundable pet deposit is part of the security deposit and its 1-month cap (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-203(a)(3), (b)(1); `edu-pet-deposit-cap-md`). Pet rent is lawful, and the pet policy must list 'Monthly pet fees' (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-210(c)(2)(ii)3; `edu-pet-policy-disclosure-md`). Self-help removal: `edu-pet-self-help-md`; officers may seize an animal under their own authority (Md. Code Ann., Crim. Law § 10-615(b)(1) ('may seize an animal if necessary to protect the animal from cruelty')), which the clause leaves to them. Montgomery County elderly tenants: revocation must fit the reasonable pet-conduct rules § 8-214(e) allows (`edu-montgomery-elderly-pets-md`). Service dogs: `edu-service-dog-fair-housing-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Condition of the Property
bodyText: Landlord will make the property available to Tenant in a condition permitting habitation, with reasonable safety.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(c)(1) (a lease shall include 'A statement that the premises will be made available in a condition permitting habitation, with reasonable safety, if that is the agreement, or if that is not the agreement, a statement of the agreement concerning the condition of the premises'). The library offers only the habitable statement: every residential landlord 'shall be deemed to warrant that the dwelling unit is fit for human habitation' (§ 8-212(c)), so the alternative statement would not change the landlord's duty (`edu-habitability-warranty-md`). (Claude Code, 2026-10-08, MD sync): topic key changed from `lease-content-requirements` to `habitability-statement` (rule 57, a companion clause keeps its own key; the shared or sibling clause stays on `lease-content-requirements`). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(c)(1)

title: Heat, Utilities and Repairs
bodyText: The parties' specific obligations for heat, gas, electricity, water and repair are: Heat: [state who provides and pays for heat, e.g. Landlord provides heat / Tenant pays the gas or electric account that heats the property]. Gas: [state who pays for gas service, or that the property has none]. Electricity: [state who pays for electricity]. Water and sewer: [state who pays for water and sewer service]. Repair: Landlord will make the repairs described in this Lease's Landlord Maintenance terms and those Maryland law requires of Landlord, and Tenant will perform the maintenance described in this Lease's Tenant Maintenance terms.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(c)(2) (a lease shall include 'The landlord’s and the tenant’s specific obligations as to heat, gas, electricity, water, and repair of the premises'). The shared utility clauses (`utilities-paid-by-landlord`, `utilities-responsibility`) list utilities; this row makes each of the five subjects explicit. The landlord's non-waivable repair duties for serious defects remain (§§ 8-211, 8-212; `edu-rent-escrow-md`). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(c)(2)

title: Maryland Tenants' Bill of Rights
bodyText: [BUILDER: attach the most current version of the Maryland Tenants' Bill of Rights from the website of the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs, Department of Housing and Community Development.] A copy of the most current version of the Maryland Tenants' Bill of Rights, published by the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs in the Department of Housing and Community Development, is attached to and included in this Lease.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(c)(4) (a lease shall include 'A copy of the most current version of the Maryland Tenants’ Bill of Rights published by the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs'); Md. Code Ann., Hous. & Cmty. Dev. § 5-104(c)(1) (the Office publishes it on its website 'On or before June 1 each year'). The attachment controls over conflicting lease terms under `addendum-precedence`. Legal watch: the version changes yearly. Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(c)(4)

title: Maryland Lead Risk Reduction Notices
bodyText: [Use if the property is an affected property under Maryland's lead poisoning prevention law, generally a rental property built before 1978, unless it is certified lead-free.] At the signing of this Lease, Landlord gives Tenant, and Tenant acknowledges receiving: (1) the Maryland Department of the Environment's notice of tenant's rights under Maryland's lead poisoning prevention law; (2) a copy of the current verified inspection certificate for the property [certificate number: ______]; and (3) the lead poisoning information packet prepared or designated by the Maryland Department of the Environment. Tenant's signature or initials acknowledging receipt of these documents: [______]. Tenant will allow Landlord access to the property at reasonable times to perform work required by Maryland's lead poisoning prevention law.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 6-820(b) (owner 'shall give to the tenant of the affected property a notice, prepared by the Department, of the tenant’s rights' 'upon the execution of a lease or the inception of a tenancy'); (d) ('a copy of the current verified inspection certificate'); § 6-823(b) ('a lead poisoning information packet prepared or designated by the Department'); delivery by certified mail or 'A verifiable method approved by the Department' (§§ 6-820(e)(1), 6-823(d)); COMAR 26.16.04.02 ('any method in which written receipt may be acknowledged by the intended recipient'), which the signed acknowledgment satisfies; § 6-820(e)(2) the owner documents the notice to the Department (education). § 6-821(a)(2) ('A tenant shall allow access to an affected property, at reasonable times, to the owner to perform any work required'). Affected property: § 6-801(b)(1) (pre-1950; 'On and after January 1, 2015, a property constructed before 1978 that contains at least one rental unit'); § 6-803(b)(3) lead-free certified property excluded. Turnover, registration and repeat notices every 2 years: `edu-lead-risk-reduction-turnover-md`. Federal disclosure: `lead-based-paint`. (Claude Code, 2026-10-08, MD sync): topic key changed from `lead-based-paint` to `lead-state-notices` (rule 57, a companion clause keeps its own key; the shared or sibling clause stays on `lead-based-paint`). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Envir. §§ 6-820(b), (d), 6-823(b); COMAR 26.16.04.02

title: Mold Information Pamphlet
bodyText: At the signing of this Lease, Landlord has given Tenant the mold information pamphlet developed or used by the Maryland Department of the Environment [identify the pamphlet, e.g. the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's "A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home"], and Landlord will give Tenant another copy on request. Tenant acknowledges receiving the pamphlet: [Tenant's signature or initials ______]
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-220(b)(1) (provide the pamphlet 'At the time the lease or rental agreement is signed' and 'On request by a tenant'); (b)(2) ('Request that a tenant sign a statement acknowledging receipt of the pamphlet'); Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 6-1702(b)(2), (c) (the Department may use the U.S. EPA's 'Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home' pamphlet). 2025 Md. Laws ch. 539, effective July 1, 2025. Assessment and remediation deadlines: `edu-mold-assessment-remediation-md`. The statute requires delivery at signing and a requested signed acknowledgment, not lease text; the lease is the chosen vehicle, and the basis follows the library's treatment of signing-time disclosures (as in `lead-risk-reduction-md`). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-220(b)

title: Pets and Eviction Fact Sheet
bodyText: [Use if Landlord knows that a Tenant has a dog or cat.] Included with this Lease is a link to the Maryland Department of Agriculture's fact sheet on how to care for and protect pets if a person is evicted or loses possession of their home: [insert the current link from the Maryland Department of Agriculture's website].
notes: MD: New topic key `pet-eviction-fact-sheet` (no other state has this duty). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 14-804 ('at the execution of a lease, the landlord shall include with the lease a link to the fact sheet published on the Department of Agriculture’s website under § 14-803 of this subtitle if the landlord knows that a tenant possesses a pet'); § 14-801(d) ('“Pet” means a domesticated dog or cat'); § 14-803 contents. At eviction the sheriff handles pets (§ 14-806; `edu-eviction-pets-md`). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 14-804

title: Positive Rent Reporting Option
bodyText: [Use if Landlord owns six or more residential rental units in Maryland.] Tenant may choose to have Tenant's positive rental payment history (Tenant's complete and timely Rent payments) reported to the following consumer reporting agency or agencies: [name each agency]. Reporting is optional. Fee: [state a monthly fee not exceeding the lesser of Landlord's actual cost or $10 per month, or state 'none']. Tenant may opt in now by signing and dating below, or at any later time by signing, dating and returning the written election form Landlord provides, and may ask Landlord for additional copies of the form. Tenant may stop reporting at any time by written request, but may not resume reporting for at least 6 months after asking to stop. Any reporting fee is not Rent, will not be credited toward Rent or any other obligation, and its payment or nonpayment will not be reported; if Tenant does not pay the fee for 30 days or more, Landlord may stop reporting and Tenant may not elect reporting again for at least 6 months after the fee first became due. Landlord will repeat this offer at least once a year, in the form required by regulations of the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Tenant elects to have Tenant's positive rental payment history reported: [ ] Yes. Tenant's signature: [______] Date: [______]
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208.4(b) (applies 'only to a landlord that owns six or more residential rental units in the State'); (c) ('shall include in a written lease the option to have the tenant’s positive rental payment history reported to at least one consumer reporting agency'); (d)(1) offer at lease signing for leases entered into on or after October 1, 2026 'and at least once annually thereafter'; (d)(2) earlier leases by January 1, 2027 (education); (e)(1)-(8) offer contents; (f) stamped envelope if offered by mail; (g) election any time, extra copies; (h)(1) fee 'not to exceed the lesser of the actual cost to the landlord to provide the service or $10 per month'; (h)(2)-(3) fee not rent, not reported, 30-day nonpayment; (i) stop on written request, 6-month wait. 2026 Md. Laws chs. 772, 773, effective October 1, 2026. The regulations prescribing the form (§ 8-208.4(j)) were not found in COMAR as of 2026-10-08 (COMAR search 'positive rental payment': 0 hits); legal watch. Leases entered into before October 1, 2026: `edu-rent-reporting-existing-leases-md`. (e)(8) signature block carried in the clause (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208.4(e)(8) ('A signature block that the tenant shall date and sign in order to accept the offer of positive rental payment history reporting')). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208.4(c) | CONSTRAINED_TERM

title: Utilities Paid to Landlord
bodyText: [Use if Tenant will pay Landlord for water, sewer, gas or electric service, other than water or sewer billed by a third party through a submeter. In a building with six or more residential units, do not use for a utility allocated by a ratio utility billing system; in a building with five or fewer units, use it together with the ratio utility billing clause.] Tenant is responsible for making payments to Landlord for the following utility services: [list water, sewer, gas and/or electric service]. Landlord will provide Tenant a copy of the utility bill for each of those services. [For a building with six or more residential units, Landlord may instead, before the beginning of this Lease and each later term, notify Tenant in writing of the total utility costs billed to Landlord in the immediately preceding year for each of those services.]
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-205.1(c) (building with 'six or more residential dwelling units': 'Use a written lease that provides notice that the tenant is responsible for making payments for water, sewer, gas, or electric utility services to the landlord' and either a bill copy or, 'Before the beginning of the initial lease and each term thereafter', notice of prior-year totals 'disaggregated by utility type'); (b)(2)(ii) not for a ratio utility billing system; § 8-205.2(c) ('five or fewer residential dwelling units': lease notice and 'Provide a copy of the water, sewer, gas, or electric utility bill'). 2024 Md. Laws chs. 225, 226, effective October 1, 2024. § 8-205.2 has no ratio-billing exclusion, so a building of five or fewer units that uses ratio billing also gives the lease notice and the bill copy. (Claude Code, 2026-10-08, MD sync): topic key changed from `utility-submetering-disclosure` to `utility-landlord-account` (rule 57, a companion clause keeps its own key; the shared or sibling clause stays on `utility-submetering-disclosure`). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. §§ 8-205.1(c), 8-205.2(c)

title: Submetered Water and Sewer
bodyText: [Use if Tenant will pay a third party for water or sewer service measured by an individual submeter.] Tenant is responsible for making payments for water and sewer service measured by an individual submeter to [name of the third-party billing company]. Landlord will provide Tenant a copy of each water or sewer bill at least 20 days before payment of the bill is due. Before this Lease began, Landlord notified Tenant in writing of the total water and sewer costs billed to the occupants of the unit in the immediately preceding 2 years or, if none were billed, to a comparably sized unit in that period.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-205.3(b)(1) ('Use a written lease that provides notice that the tenant is responsible for making payments for the water or sewer services to the third party'); (b)(2) bill copy 'not later than 20 days before payment of the bill is due'; (b)(3) pre-lease notice of 2-year totals; (c) a landlord that does not meet Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 9-1115 'may not require a tenant to make payments to a third party for water or sewer services' (education: `edu-utility-allowance-cap-md`). 2026 Md. Laws chs. 261, 262, effective October 1, 2026. Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-205.3(b)

title: Allocated Utility Billing
bodyText: [Use if Landlord bills Tenant for any utility by a ratio utility billing system, meaning master-metered charges allocated among tenants without measuring each tenant's actual use; not for a condominium or cooperative.] Landlord will bill Tenant for the following allocated utility services: [identify each utility]. Before this Lease was signed, Landlord gave Tenant in writing: a statement that Tenant will be billed by Landlord for allocated utility services identifying each utility; a copy of the last two utility bills issued to Landlord; a description of the method used to allocate the cost of each utility; the average monthly bill for all dwelling units in the property in the previous calendar year, by utility; information about any additional service charges or administrative fees for the billing system; and a citation to Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-212.4. Any dispute about the computation of Tenant's bill is between Tenant and Landlord. Tenant has the right to inspect Landlord's records documenting a utility bill on written request.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-212.4(c)(1)(i)-(viii) disclosures to 'all prospective tenants in writing'; (c)(2) ('A lease provision that requires a tenant to pay the utility charges billed to the tenant under a ratio utility billing system shall be unenforceable if the landlord fails to provide the information'); (d) records on written request; (a)(3) landlord 'offers two or more dwelling units for rent on one parcel'; (b) not condominium or cooperative; (e) local laws may be stricter (flagged, not resolved). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-212.4(c)

title: Submetered Electricity or Gas
bodyText: [Use if the building is submetered for electricity or gas.] The building is submetered for [electricity / gas]. Bills for [electric / gas] consumption will be rendered based on the submeter readings. Electricity or gas for all common areas and common facilities is the responsibility of the owner and not of Tenant. The owner will provide Tenant, at no charge, a copy of the regulations governing submetering in apartment houses.
notes: MD: COMAR 20.25.01.02B ('All rental contracts or leases between the owner and an occupant shall clearly state that' (1) the building 'is submetered'; (2) 'Bills for electric or gas consumption shall be rendered based on the submeter readings'; (3) common-area electricity or gas 'shall be the responsibility of the owner and not of the occupant'; (4) a copy of the regulations 'shall be provided to every occupant by the owner at no charge'); 20.25.01.02A all units must be submetered. Regulation, not statute: flagged for monitoring (rule 21). Energy allocation billing approval and limits: `edu-energy-allocation-approval-md`, `edu-submetering-charge-limits-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Landlord Contact for Notices
bodyText: [Required unless Landlord posts this information on a sign in a conspicuous place on the property.] The name, address and telephone number of [Landlord / the person authorized to accept notice or service of process on behalf of Landlord] are: [name; address; telephone number].
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-210(a)(1) (landlord 'shall include in a written lease or post a sign in a conspicuous place on that property listing the name, address, and telephone number of' the landlord or 'The person, if any, authorized to accept notice or service of process'); (a)(2) otherwise tenant's notice is proper if sent to the rent payee, rent address or tax-bill address. Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-210(a)

title: Columbia Association Property
bodyText: [Use only for property in Howard County subject to Columbia Association covenants.] [If Tenant pays any part of the Columbia Association annual charge as part of the Rent: The Rent includes [amount] of the Columbia Association annual charge, calculated as follows: [describe how the amount is calculated].] As a resident of property subject to Columbia Association covenants and governing documents, Tenant has the rights and privileges described [here: describe them / at: state where Tenant can find a description]. At signing, Landlord has given Tenant a copy (physical, digital or a permanent link) of the Columbia Association covenants and governing documents and of the governing documents of the [village association / Town Center].
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-121(b) (only 'leases for residential and commercial real property in Howard County that are subject to Columbia Association covenants'); (c) charge in rent: lease must include 'Notice of the amount of the annual charge that is included in the rent' and 'A description of how the annual charge is calculated'; (d)(1) rights and privileges description or where to find it; (e) copies at signing, 'physical copy, digital copy, or permanent link'. 2025 Md. Laws ch. 584, effective October 1, 2025. Place-limited state statute (rule 32): scope stated in the body. Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-121(c)-(e)

title: Association Obligations (Montgomery County)
bodyText: [Use only for property in Montgomery County within a condominium or homeowners' development, for a lease with an initial term of 125 days or more.] The owner's obligations under the association's rules, declaration and recorded covenants and restrictions that limit or affect the use and occupancy of the property are enforceable against Tenant. Before Tenant signed this Lease, the owner gave Tenant a copy of those rules, declaration and recorded covenants and restrictions, to the extent applicable.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-210(b)(1) ('This subsection applies only in Montgomery County'); (b)(3)(i) before execution of a lease 'for an initial term of 125 days or more' the owner within a condominium or development provides 'a copy of the rules, declaration, and recorded covenants and restrictions'; (b)(3)(ii) ('The written lease shall include a statement, if applicable, that the obligations of the owner that limit or affect the use and occupancy of the property are enforceable against the owner’s tenant'). Place-limited state statute (rule 32). (Claude Code, 2026-10-08, MD sync): topic key changed from `hoa-compliance` to `association-obligations-disclosure` (rule 57, a companion clause keeps its own key; the shared or sibling clause stays on `hoa-compliance`). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-210(b)(3)

title: No Complete Sprinkler System
bodyText: [Use if the property is in a residential rental high-rise building, meaning four or more stories above grade or over 45 feet tall, that is not protected throughout by a complete automatic sprinkler system, unless the building is less than 75 feet tall, the local fire department has aerial equipment able to reach its roof, and the building is accessible on two sides by a public way kept open to the fire department at all times and close enough for that equipment to reach 75 feet. BUILDER: display this notice conspicuously, in bold capitals and boxed.] NOTICE: THIS BUILDING IS NOT CURRENTLY PROTECTED BY A COMPLETE AUTOMATIC SPRINKLER SYSTEM. Tenant's initials: [______]
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Pub. Safety § 9-403(d)(1) ('Beginning January 1, 2025, and continuing until a residential rental high-rise building is protected by a complete automatic sprinkler system, the owner ... shall include in any lease agreement conspicuous notice'); (d)(2) ('Notice required under paragraph (1) of this subsection shall be initialed by the tenant'); § 9-401(b)(1) ('four or more stories above grade level' or 'over 45 feet in height'); § 9-403(c) entrance warning sign from July 1, 2024 (`edu-high-rise-sprinkler-sign-md`). Layout rule recorded in MD log §4. Exemption stated in the bracket: Md. Code Ann., Pub. Safety § 9-403(b)(1) ('This section does not apply to a building that is less than 75 feet in height above grade level if'). Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Pub. Safety § 9-403(d)

title: Private Well Water Testing
bodyText: [Use if the property is served by a private well.] The property's water is supplied by a private well. The most recent water quality test of the well was completed on [date] with the following results: [summarize the results or attach the test report]. Landlord will provide for water quality testing at least every 3 years, will notify Tenant after each test is complete, and will disclose the results to Tenant.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 9-4A-04(a) (owner of residential rental property 'served by a private well shall' (1) 'Provide for water quality testing every 3 years'; (2) 'Disclose to a tenant the results'; (3) notify a tenant after each test and 'Of the most recent water quality test when they sign a lease'); (b) contamination duties within 60 days, including 'Providing the tenant with the option to terminate the lease' (`edu-private-well-testing-md`); (c) civil penalty up to $1,000; (d) MDE testing criteria by regulation. Enactment date not checked; in force in the 2026-10-01 compilation. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Condominium or Cooperative Conversion Notice
bodyText: [Use only if the notice of conversion of this residential rental facility to a condominium or to a cooperative housing corporation has already been given to the building's tenants.] Landlord informs Tenant that the notice of conversion of this residential rental facility to a [condominium / cooperative housing corporation] required by Maryland law was given to the tenants on [date].
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 11-102.1(a)(2) (owner and landlord 'shall inform in writing each tenant who first leases any portion of the premises as his residence after the giving of the notice required by this subsection that the notice has been given', 'at or before the signing of lease or the taking of possession, whichever occurs first'); Md. Code Ann., Corps. & Ass'ns § 5-6B-05(a)(3) same for cooperative conversions ('on or before signing the lease or taking possession'). Conversion rights of existing tenants: `edu-condo-coop-conversion-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 11-102.1(a)(2); Md. Code Ann., Corps. & Ass'ns § 5-6B-05(a)(3)

title: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms
bodyText: Tenant is responsible for testing the smoke alarms in the property. Tenant will not remove or tamper with a smoke alarm or carbon monoxide alarm or otherwise make it inoperative. Tenant will notify Landlord in writing of any failure or malfunction of a smoke alarm, by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by hand delivery to Landlord or Landlord's agent at the address used for paying Rent. Landlord will give Tenant a written receipt for a hand-delivered notice, will acknowledge the notice in writing, and will repair or replace the smoke alarm within 5 calendar days after the notice.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Pub. Safety § 9-106(d) ('Occupants of a residential occupancy may not remove or tamper with a required smoke alarm or otherwise render the smoke alarm inoperative'); (e)(1) ('Testing of smoke alarms is the responsibility of the occupant of the residential unit'); (e)(2)(i)-(iv) written notice 'by certified mail, return receipt requested to the landlord, or by hand delivery to the landlord or the landlord’s agent, at the address used for the payment of rent', written receipt, written acknowledgment, repair or replace 'within 5 calendar days'; Md. Code Ann., Pub. Safety § 12-1105 ('Except as part of routine maintenance, a person may not render a carbon monoxide alarm inoperable'). Restates tenant duties (serves landlord) with the paired statutory procedure. Landlord installation duties: `edu-smoke-co-alarm-landlord-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Automatic Renewal (Optional)
bodyText: [Optional. BUILDER: set this Section apart from every other provision of the Lease, with its own initials line. Not needed where the renewal period is one month or less.] AUTOMATIC RENEWAL. Unless Landlord or Tenant gives the other written notice of termination at least [number, not less than 60] days before the end of the Term or of any renewal term, this Lease will automatically renew for a further term of [length of renewal term] on the same terms, except for any change Maryland law allows on notice. Tenant's initials agreeing to this automatic renewal provision: [______]
notes: MD: Option (rule 54: a term the statute lets the lease add on conditions). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(e)(1) (an automatic-renewal provision, except for renewal periods 'of 1 month or less', 'shall have the provision distinctly set apart from any other provision of the lease and provide a space for the written acknowledgment of the tenant’s agreement'); (e)(2) unenforceable by the landlord without the tenant's 'initials, signature, or witnessed mark'. One notice period for both parties: a lease may not require a longer tenant notice than the landlord's (§ 8-501); the landlord's notice for a written lease of more than a week is at least 60 days (§ 8-402(c)(2)(i)), and a longer agreed period is allowed (§ 8-208(d)(5)). Rent increases still need § 8-209 notice (90 days for terms over a month; `edu-rent-increase-notice-md`). Layout recorded in MD log §4. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Holdover Charge (Optional)
bodyText: [Optional.] If Tenant remains in possession after this Lease ends without Landlord's written consent, Tenant will pay Landlord, as agreed damages for each day Tenant remains, [state a daily amount that reasonably estimates Landlord's likely loss, e.g. 150% of the daily Rent] instead of the Rent apportioned for that day. This charge does not apply to any day after Landlord ends this Lease or Tenant's possession for nonpayment of Rent, or to any day for which Maryland law lets Tenant keep or redeem possession by paying Rent. Landlord will not recover both this charge and Rent for the same day, and will not recover this charge for any day for which a court awards Landlord holdover damages measured another way.
notes: MD: Option (rule 54: a measure the lease may set). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402(a)(1)-(2) (actual damages, not less than apportioned rent) and (a)(4) ('Nothing in this section is intended to limit any other remedies which a landlord may have against a holdover tenant under the lease'). Exclusions per rule 53: after a nonpayment termination the 5% late-fee cap (§ 8-208(d)(3)) and the right of redemption to execution (§ 8-401(h)) would make a daily charge a second late charge or a price on redemption. No double-rent or statutory multiplier exists in Maryland (canvass, topic holdover-rate). Whether a stipulated rate is an unenforceable penalty turns on case law, not searched; the bracket asks for a reasonable estimate. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Court Surcharge from Deposit (Optional)
bodyText: [Optional.] If Landlord files an action for failure to pay Rent and the District Court grants Landlord a judgment for possession, the summary ejectment surcharge assessed against Landlord may be assessed against Tenant as Maryland law allows: the court may allow Landlord to deduct the surcharge from the Security Deposit. The deduction will not exceed the amount of the Security Deposit, and Landlord will not otherwise charge Tenant for the surcharge.
notes: MD: Option (rule 54: a right that exists only if the lease invokes it). Md. Code Ann., Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 7-301(c)(5)(i) (the summary-ejectment surcharge 'shall be assessed against a landlord and may not be awarded or assigned as a fee or cost against a residential tenant'); (c)(5)(ii) the court may allow deduction from the deposit if 'A judgment for possession is granted in the landlord’s favor' and 'The lease agreement provides that a surcharge may be assessed against the tenant in accordance with this paragraph'; (c)(5)(iii) not more than the deposit; Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(13) (lease may not otherwise shift the surcharge 'Except as authorized under § 7-301(c)(5)(ii)'); § 8-203(f)(2) deposit may be applied for the surcharge. Surcharge amount up to $43 (§ 7-301(c)(2)(i)1). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Electronic Notice Election (Optional)
bodyText: [Optional. Present as a separate election; Tenant's choice is voluntary.] Tenant may choose to receive the following notices from Landlord electronically: notices of a rent increase, notices of Landlord's entry, the notice of intent to file a failure-to-pay-rent case, the positive rent reporting offer, and other notices Maryland law allows Landlord to deliver electronically if Tenant elects it. Tenant's choice: [ ] Yes, deliver those notices electronically by [e-mail to ______ / text message to ______ / Landlord's electronic tenant portal]. [ ] No. Landlord's acceptance of Tenant's application and this Lease does not depend on this choice. Tenant may change this choice by written notice to Landlord. For the notices covered, this election controls over this Lease's Notices section.
notes: MD: Option (rule 46: a written election the statutes make a trigger). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-209(b)(2)(i)2 rent-increase notice 'If elected by the tenant, sent by electronic delivery' by e-mail, text or portal; (b)(2)(iii) ('A landlord may not condition the acceptance of a lease application on the tenant’s election'); § 8-208(d)(9) a lease may not 'Require' electronic delivery of rent-increase notices; § 8-221(c)(3)(iii) entry notice; § 8-401(c)(2)(i)3 pre-filing nonpayment notice; § 8-208.4(d)(2)(ii)3 reporting offer 'if the tenant has elected to receive notices from the landlord in this manner' (for leases entered into before October 1, 2026; no delivery method is set for later annual offers); each requires proof of transmission. Revocation: no statute; the clause allows it (drafting judgment). Control sentence per rule 46. The warrant notice (§ 8-407(b)(1)(iii)) goes by e-mail or text whenever the landlord has them, without an election. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Utility Shutoff Notices to Landlord (Optional)
bodyText: [Optional. Use only for a unit in a multifamily dwelling.] Tenant will ensure that the customer responsible for the electric or gas account for the unit gives the utility company consent for [Landlord / Landlord's property manager] to receive any notice that service will be terminated for nonpayment.
notes: MD: Option (rule 54). Md. Code Ann., Pub. Util. § 7-307.3(b) ('As a term of a lease of a multifamily dwelling unit, the property owner or property manager of the multifamily dwelling unit may require a tenant to ensure that a customer of the public service company that is responsible for the account for that multifamily dwelling unit provides consent'); (a) the utility then notifies the owner or manager before terminating; (c) consent by the customer or, if written, by the owner or manager. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Criminal Activity and Danger (Optional)
bodyText: [Optional.] Tenant, members of Tenant's household, and Tenant's guests and other persons on the property with Tenant's consent will not engage in criminal activity on the property, or in behavior on the property that demonstrates a clear and imminent danger of doing serious harm to themselves, other tenants, Landlord, Landlord's property or representatives, or any other person on the property. A violation is a breach of this Lease for which Landlord may give the written notices and pursue the remedies provided in this Lease's Default by Tenant section and Maryland law, including 14 days' notice where the behavior demonstrates such a danger. This Section does not apply to Tenant or a member of Tenant's household who is the victim of the activity, and Landlord will not treat a request for help from law enforcement or emergency services as a violation.
notes: MD: Option (rule 54). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402.1(a)(1)(i)2B (14 days' notice where 'The breach of the lease involves behavior by a tenant or a person who is on the property with the tenant’s consent, which demonstrates a clear and imminent danger'); the court must still find a substantial breach warranting eviction (§ 8-402.1(b)(1)). § 8-208(d)(10) (a lease may not include a provision that 'Limits the ability of a tenant to summon the assistance of law enforcement or emergency services'); § 8-208.1(a)(2)(iv) retaliation; § 8-5A-04 abuse-victim presumption. Drug and prostitution nuisance suits: `edu-drug-nuisance-actions-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Algorithmic Rent-Setting Law
bodyText: Maryland has no statute that specifically addresses setting rents with shared pricing or revenue-management software. Maryland's general antitrust law still bars agreements and combinations that unreasonably restrain trade. Whether using a common rent-pricing algorithm with competitors violates that law is unsettled in Maryland.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 11-204(a)(1) ('By contract, combination, or conspiracy with one or more other persons, unreasonably restrain trade or commerce'). (MD battery A-algo-rent-notenancy-pos: 13 hits; positives passed). No 2024-2026 enacted act in the saved session laws mentions 'algorithm' (grep). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Application Fee Refund Rule
bodyText: This applies if you offer five or more units for rent on one parcel or at one location; it does not apply to seasonal or condominium rentals. Your application form must explain what the applicant is liable for on signing and the refund rule. If you charge fees other than a security deposit that exceed $25, you must return them within 15 days after the applicant moves in or after either side tells the other in writing that no tenancy will occur. You may keep only the part actually spent on a credit check or other application expenses. If you don't refund, you owe twice the fees. Maryland sets no cap on the fee amount and has no rule about minors' fees.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-213(b)(1)(i) ('If a landlord requires from a prospective tenant any fees other than a security deposit'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-213(b)(1)(i) ('then the landlord shall return the fees, subject to the exceptions below, or be liable for twice the amount of the fees in damages'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-213(c) ('does not apply to any landlord who offers four or less dwelling units for rent on one parcel of property or at one location'). (MD battery A-appfee-all2: 8 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-appfee-cpi-ctx: 2 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-appfee-minor2-tenancy-pos: 1 hits; positives passed). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Reusable Tenant Screening Reports
bodyText: You must tell prospective tenants whether you accept reusable tenant screening reports, either in writing or by a conspicuous posting such as a statement on your listing, your website homepage or your online application page. A reusable report is one prepared by a consumer reporting agency within the previous 30 days at the applicant's request and expense. If you accept them and an applicant gives you one, you may not charge an application fee or a fee to access the report. You may require the applicant to certify there has been no material change in name, address, bankruptcy status, criminal history or eviction history.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-218(c)(1) ('A landlord shall notify prospective tenants regarding whether or not the landlord accepts reusable tenant screening reports'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-218(d) ('the landlord may not charge the prospective tenant: (1) A fee for the landlord to access the report; or (2) An application fee.'). Section marked changed 2026 (2026 Md. Laws ch. 752); October 1, 2026 text relied on. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Applying Payments After Notice
bodyText: After you have given a notice to quit at the end of a tenancy, or a notice of breach of lease, any payment you accept before eviction must be applied in a set order. It goes first to rent, or its equivalent, up to the date you actually recover possession. It then goes to court costs, including court-awarded damages and legal fees, and then to rent lost because of the holdover or breach. Any excess bears no interest and must be returned the way a security deposit is returned. Maryland sets no payment order before any notice is given.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402(c)(5)(ii) ('first applied to the rent or the equivalent of rent apportioned to the date that the landlord actually recovers possession of the premises'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402.1(d)(2) ('then to court costs, including court awarded damages and legal fees and then to any loss of rent caused by the breach of lease'). (MD battery A-apply-payments-tenancy: 10 hits; positives passed). Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402 marked changed 2026; October 1, 2026 text relied on. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Residential Collection-Fee Statute
bodyText: No Maryland statute authorizes or caps a collection fee that a residential landlord adds to unpaid rent or damages. When you collect a debt from a tenant you are a collector under the Maryland Consumer Debt Collection Act. You may not claim, attempt or threaten to enforce a right you know does not exist. In a failure-to-pay-rent case the court can award lease attorney's fees only for nonresidential tenancies. Whether a lease collection-fee clause can be enforced in a separate suit is unsettled.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 14-201(b) ('“Collector” means a person collecting or attempting to collect an alleged debt arising out of a consumer transaction.'); Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 14-202(8) ('Claim, attempt, or threaten to enforce a right with knowledge that the right does not exist'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-401(e)(2)(v) ('In the case of a nonresidential tenancy'). (MD battery A-collection-fee-notenancy: 34 hits; positives passed). A-collection-fee-tenancy found only ground-lease and motor-vehicle-lease rules (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-707, 8-804-8-807; Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 14-2002). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: What Counts At Signing
bodyText: A Maryland lease may not require the tenant to pay more than the security deposit plus the first month's rent to start the lease and move in. Last month's rent collected in advance is legally part of the security deposit, so you cannot require first month's rent, last month's rent and a separate deposit. Whether other one-time charges payable before move-in, such as an up-front pet fee or an administrative fee, count toward this limit is unsettled. The statute covers any amount required to commence the lease and occupy, so the cautious reading counts them.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(11) ('Requires a tenant to pay more than the sum of the security deposit under § 8-203(b) of this subtitle and the first month’s rent'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-203(a)(3) ('including payment of the last month’s rent in advance of the time it is due'). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No All-In Fee Disclosure Law
bodyText: Maryland has no all-in pricing or junk-fee law for residential rentals, no rule that rent appear as one figure including mandatory fees, and no first-page fee disclosure rule. Specific statutes require particular fees to be disclosed: pet fees and deposits in your pet policy, ratio utility billing administrative fees before leasing, any positive rent reporting fee, the applicant's liabilities on the application, and, for Columbia Association property in Howard County, the annual charge included in rent. Whether charging a fee not stated in the lease is a deceptive trade practice is unsettled, but the Consumer Protection Act applies to residential leasing.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-210(c)(2)(ii) ('Any required fees, including: 1. Up-front, nonrefundable pet fees; 2. Refundable pet deposits; and 3. Monthly pet fees'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-212.4(c)(1)(vii) ('Information regarding any additional service charges or administrative fees to be paid by the tenant for the operation of the ratio utility billing system'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-121(c)(1) ('Notice of the amount of the annual charge that is included in the rent'); Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 13-303(1) ('The sale, lease, rental, loan, or bailment of any consumer goods, consumer realty, or consumer services'). (MD battery A-feetransp-notenancy2: 37 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-feetransp-first-page-notenancy2: 16 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-feetransp-not-in-lease-pos: 1 hits; positives passed). Case law not searched. Local: Howard County (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-121, Columbia Association property). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Fees For Services Not Provided
bodyText: Maryland has no general statute barring a fee for a service you do not provide. Related rules do apply. If you bill tenants through individual water submeters, you may not charge for leaks or poor maintenance you are responsible for, common-area use or nonresidential use, and your added billing charge may not exceed $1 per unit per month. If the lease makes you responsible for the gas or electric bill for a unit whose service is in your name on a single meter serving only that unit (not a master meter), and the tenant pays that bill or a deposit to open a new account, the tenant may deduct that amount from rent.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 9-1115(d)(3) ('may not impose on a unit in the facility any costs associated with: (i) Poor maintenance or leaks'); Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 9-1115(d)(4) ('may collect an additional service charge not exceeding $1 per unit per month to cover administrative costs and billing'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-212.3(b) ('A tenant may deduct from rent due to a landlord the amount of payments made to a utility service provider for utility service'). (MD battery A-fee-unprovided-notenancy-pos: 17 hits; positives passed). Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 9-1115 rewritten by 2026 Md. Laws ch. 261/262; October 1, 2026 text relied on. Md. Code Ann., Pub. Util. § 7-309(b)(2) ('is delivered through a single meter to a single dwelling unit; and (iii) does not use a master meter'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Fees In A Rent Case
bodyText: Maryland's failure-to-pay-rent case covers rent and late fees due, minus utility payments a tenant made under the Public Utilities law when you failed to pay a utility. Maryland law does not define rent for ordinary residential leases, and no statute says other charges become rent because the lease calls them additional rent; whether that label works in a rent case is unsettled. Two statutes are specific: a positive rent reporting fee is not rent, and an unpaid domestic-violence lock-change fee may be charged as additional rent.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-401(b)(2)(iii) ('Stating the amount of rent and any late fees due and unpaid'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208.4(h)(2)(ii) ('A fee collected under this subsection is not rent'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-5A-05(e)(2)(i) ('Charge the fee as additional rent'). (MD battery A-fees-as-rent: 14 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-rent-definition-pos: 5 hits; positives passed). The 2026 submetering bill's line that unpaid water bills may not be treated as unpaid rent was struck and is not in compiled Md. Code Ann., Envir. § 9-1115. Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Court Surcharge And Notice Costs
bodyText: The District Court surcharge on a summary ejectment case, up to $43, is assessed against you and may not be awarded or assigned against a residential tenant, and a lease may not make the tenant responsible for it. The one exception: after a judgment for possession, the court may let you deduct it from the security deposit if the lease provides for it, never more than the deposit. You may charge the tenant actual costs of the required warrant-of-restitution notice, up to $5. No Maryland statute addresses passing rental-license, lead-registration or similar government fees to tenants.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 7-301(c)(5)(i) ('shall be assessed against a landlord and may not be awarded or assigned as a fee or cost against a residential tenant by the court'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-407(b)(3) ('A landlord may charge the tenant for expenses actually incurred in providing notice'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(13) ('provides that a tenant is responsible for, or requires a tenant to agree to be responsible for, payment of a filing surcharge'). (MD battery A-govfee-fee-tenant-pay: 8 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-govfee-passthrough: 7 hits; positives passed). Lease wording for the deposit deduction is the option filing-surcharge-deposit-md. Local: Baltimore City has an additional court surcharge of up to $10 on landlord-tenant cases (Md. Code Ann., Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 7-301(c)(3)). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Late Fees: No Grace Period
bodyText: For ordinary residential leases, a late fee may not exceed 5% of the unpaid rent due for the rental period; for weekly-rent leases the limit is $3 a week and $12 a month. Since October 1, 2025 the 5% is measured on the amount left unpaid, not on the full rent. Maryland law sets no grace period and no notice before a late fee. The commonly cited rule allowing the higher of 5% or $5 after a 5-day grace period applies only to mobile home parks. Whether a late fee can be collected if the lease does not provide for one is unsettled.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(3)(i) ('in excess of 5% of the amount of unpaid rent due for the rental period for which the payment was delinquent'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8A-404(2) ('The fee does not exceed 5 percent of the rent due or $5, whichever is higher'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8A-404(3) ('The rent is not paid within 5 days after the due date specified in the rental agreement'); 2025 Md. Laws ch. 580. (MD battery A-latefee-grace-pos: 1 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-latefee-notice-before-collect: 0 hits; no real positive exists, pattern synthetic-tested). Lease wording is the clause late-fee-limit-md. Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Lease-Type Parity Rule
bodyText: Maryland does not bar different terms or rents for month-to-month and fixed-term leases. The one parity rule is that a written lease may not require the tenant to give a longer notice to end the tenancy than you must give the tenant. If you let a tenant stay after the lease ends, the tenant becomes month-to-month, or week-to-week if the tenancy was weekly, unless the written lease says otherwise and the tenant initials that provision.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-501 ('a longer notice period to be furnished by the tenant to the landlord in order to terminate the tenancy than that required of the landlord'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402(d) ('Unless stated otherwise in the written lease and initialed by the tenant'). (MD battery A-leasetype-parity: 2 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-leasetype-more-favorable-pos: 5 hits; positives passed). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Notice Costs: $5 Limit
bodyText: The only notice cost Maryland lets you charge a tenant is the actual expense of the notice required before a warrant of restitution is executed, up to $5. No statute authorizes charging for the 10-day notice of intent to file a failure-to-pay-rent case or for termination notices. Demanding a charge you know you have no right to can violate the Maryland Consumer Debt Collection Act.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-407(b)(3) ('in an amount not to exceed $5'); Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 14-202(8) ('Claim, attempt, or threaten to enforce a right with knowledge that the right does not exist'). (MD battery A-notice-fee: 5 hits; positives passed). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Rent Concession Rules
bodyText: Maryland has no statute on rent concessions, free-rent periods or move-in specials, or on taking back a concession if the tenant leaves early. If a tenant breaks the lease by leaving early or never taking possession, you have a duty to mitigate your damages, and rent you receive from a new tenant during the rest of the term reduces lost-rent damages. Whether a concession clawback clause is enforceable is unsettled.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-203(f)(3) ('any amount of rents received by the landlord for the premises during the remainder if any, of the tenant’s term'). (MD battery A-concession-tenancy-pos: 5 hits; positives passed). Case law not searched. Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-207(a) ('The aggrieved party in a breach of a lease has a duty to mitigate damages'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Local Rent Limits May Apply
bodyText: Maryland has no statewide rent control and no statute preempting local rent limits. State law expects some counties and municipalities to limit rent increases for renewing tenants and requires them to report those laws, so check the county and city where the unit is located. When you file an eviction case where the locality requires a rental license, you must plead that the property is licensed, exempt, or unlicensed for a reason the statute allows. Separate state limits apply to extended leases given to certain senior or disabled households after a condominium or cooperative conversion.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-209.1(b)(1) ('a local law to limit the rent increase that a landlord may charge a current tenant for a subsequent term'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-406 ('Licensed in compliance with applicable local rental licensing requirements'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 11-137(f)(2) ('The increase may not exceed an amount determined by multiplying the annual rent for the preceding year by the percentage increase for the rent component'). (MD battery A-rentcontrol: 1 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-preempt-grp-notenancy: 16 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-rental-license-local: 2 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-locality-sue-for-tenants-pos: 1 hits; positives passed). Also Md. Code Ann., Corps. & Ass'ns § 5-6B-07 (cooperative conversion extended leases). Local: Local rent-stabilization laws (Montgomery County, Takoma Park and Prince George's County are reported to have them; not verified, local codes not researched); local rental licensing. Licensing pleading in full: `edu-rental-license-in-eviction-md`. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Rent Increases During The Term
bodyText: Maryland has no statute on rent escalation clauses and no retaliation safe harbor that depends on one. Whether you may raise rent during a fixed term without a lease provision allowing it is a contract question and unsettled. Any rent increase still requires the written notice period for rent increases. You may not arbitrarily increase rent because a tenant made a good-faith complaint, sued or testified, joined a tenants' organization, or summoned police or emergency help, and a later increase within 6 months of that activity can be challenged.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208.1(a)(1)(ii) ('Arbitrarily increase the rent or decrease the services to which a tenant has been entitled'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208.1(e) ('occurs more than 6 months after a tenant’s action that is protected'). (MD battery A-escalation-pos: 1 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-escalation-notenancy: 0 hits; no real positive exists, pattern synthetic-tested) (MD battery A-midterm-increase: 0 hits; no real positive exists, pattern synthetic-tested). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Rent Increase Notice Periods
bodyText: You must notify the tenant in writing before increasing rent: at least 90 days ahead for a tenancy for a term of more than 1 month; at least 60 days for more than 1 week but not more than 1 month, such as month-to-month; and for 1 week or less, 7 days with a written lease or 21 days without one. Send the notice by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing, or by e-mail, text message or tenant portal if the tenant elected electronic delivery and you get proof of transmission. You may not condition a lease application on that election, and a lease may not require electronic delivery of rent-increase notices. The rule does not apply once you have given notice to terminate the tenancy, and local law may require more notice.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-209(b)(3)(i) ('For tenancies for a term of more than 1 month, at least 90 days in advance of the rent increase'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-209(b)(2)(iii) ('A landlord may not condition the acceptance of a lease application on the tenant’s election to receive notice'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(9) ('Requires the tenant to accept notice of rent increases under § 8-209 of this subtitle or § 8-401 of this title by electronic delivery'). Local: Local laws may add notice (Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-209(c)). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Rent Installment Rules
bodyText: Maryland has no statute on splitting rent into installments or on whether a scheduled installment is a partial payment. The statutes only recognize leases with weekly rent installments, which have their own late-fee limit, and require a failure-to-pay-rent complaint to state the rent and due day for each rental period. A late fee is measured on the rent left unpaid for the rental period.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(3)(ii) ('In the case of leases under which the rent is paid in weekly rental installments'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-401(b)(3) ('the amount of rent due for each rental period under the lease, the day that the rent is due for each rental period'). (MD battery A-rent-installments: 24 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-partial-payment-rent: 2 hits; positives passed). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Rent Receipts And Records
bodyText: You must give the tenant a receipt when the tenant pays in cash or asks for a receipt; failing to do so makes you liable to the tenant for $25. You must also keep records showing the dates and amounts of rent paid and that a receipt was given for each cash payment. In Anne Arundel County, unless the tenant pays by check, every payment requires a receipt showing the payment and the period it covers, and a person convicted of violating that rule forfeits the rent for that period.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-205(b) ('the landlord or landlord’s agent shall give the tenant a receipt if the tenant: (1) Makes payment in cash; or (2) Requests a receipt.'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-205(c) ('the landlord shall be liable to the tenant in the sum of $25'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208.3 ('showing also the fact that a receipt of some form was given to each tenant for each cash payment of rent'). Local: Anne Arundel County: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-205(a). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Sales Tax On Short Stays
bodyText: Ordinary residential rent is not subject to Maryland sales and use tax; the tax reaches a right to occupy a room or lodgings as a transient guest. The Comptroller's regulation says the tax does not apply to monthly renters or permanent residents, but rentals in resort areas for 4 months or less are taxable. County and municipal hotel rental taxes generally reach stays of up to 4 consecutive months, with shorter thresholds in some counties. Beginning July 1, 2028, the state tax definition expands to cover short-term rental units.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Tax-Gen. § 11-101(a-1) ('“Accommodation” means a right to occupy a room or lodgings as a transient guest.'); COMAR 03.06.01.23A ('The tax does not apply to charges to persons who rent living accommodations on a monthly basis or who are permanent residents.'); COMAR 03.06.01.23A ('However, all rentals in resort areas for terms of 4 months or less are subject to the tax.'); Md. Code Ann., Local Gov't § 20-401(d)(1)(i) ('“transient charge” means a hotel charge for sleeping accommodations for a period not exceeding 4 consecutive months'). (MD battery A-renttax-transient: 23 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-renttax-passthrough2: 1 hits; positives passed) (MD battery A-renttax-repealed-passthrough: 0 hits; no real positive exists, pattern synthetic-tested). Md. Code Ann., Tax-Gen. § 11-101 and Md. Code Ann., Local Gov't § 20-401 IN EFFECT versions relied on; later versions take effect July 1, 2028 (2026 Md. Laws ch. 6). No statute bars passing a repealed local tax through to tenants. Local: County hotel rental tax thresholds: Carroll 25 days, Frederick 90 days, Garrett and Washington 30 days. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Rule Listing All Fees
bodyText: Maryland has no general rule that every fee, fine or charge be stated in the residential lease, and no notice period for adding one. Some charges do depend on lease wording: you may deduct the court filing surcharge from the deposit only if the lease provides for it, and you may require utility payments to you or to a submeter billing company only through a written lease giving that notice. A late fee is limited to 5% of the rent left unpaid for the period.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 7-301(c)(5)(ii) ('The lease agreement provides that a surcharge may be assessed against the tenant in accordance with this paragraph.'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-205.1(c)(1) ('Use a written lease that provides notice that the tenant is responsible for making payments'). (MD battery A-required-fees-in-lease2: 18 hits; positives passed). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Returned Check Fee Limit
bodyText: Under Maryland's dishonored-check law, if a check is dishonored and not paid within 10 days you may send a notice of dishonor in the statutory form, with a certificate of mailing or an affidavit of mailing. If the check is still unpaid 30 days after the notice, the drawer owes the check amount, a collection fee of up to $35, and up to twice the check amount but not more than $1,000. You lose the double-damages remedy if you demand and receive collection costs above $35, or demand and receive any collection costs within 30 days after mailing the notice of dishonor. The law applies only to bad checks, and a postdated check is not a check under the bad-check law. Whether a lease may set a higher returned-payment fee is unsettled.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 15-802(b)(2) ('A collection fee of up to $35'); Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 15-804(a)(2) ('That is not a bad check as described under § 8-103 of the Criminal Law Article.'); Md. Code Ann., Crim. Law § 8-101(b) ('“Check” means a negotiable instrument that is not postdated at the time it is issued.'). (MD battery A-postdated-pos: 8 hits; positives passed). Shared clause returned-payments carries the lease wording. Case law not searched. Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 15-802(d)(1) ('The holder has demanded of, and received from, the maker or drawer'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Government Shutdown Eviction Stay
bodyText: In a failure-to-pay-rent case for rent due during a government shutdown, the court must stay the case if an occupant shows the home is their primary residence and they are a federal, State or Maryland local government employee involuntarily furloughed without pay, even if required to report to work. The stay lasts as long as the court considers reasonable, but not beyond 30 days after the shutdown ends unless a party shows sufficient cause.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-401(d)(2)(iii) ('Is involuntarily furloughed from work without pay because of a government shutdown'); Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-401(d)(3)(ii) ('may not be granted for a period that ends more than 30 days after the end of the government shutdown'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Subsidy Late-Fee Rule
bodyText: Maryland has no statute on late fees connected to the part of rent paid by a housing subsidy. The state limit is 5% of the unpaid rent due for the rental period. Federal program rules may apply to subsidized tenancies and are not covered here.
notes: MD: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(3)(i) ('in excess of 5% of the amount of unpaid rent due for the rental period').
