Massachusetts has no statute on ending a residential lease after fire or casualty (MA battery R18 casualty fire damage tenancy: 7 hits, none a residential lease rule; synthetic positive passed); the subject is left to the lease and common law (case law not searched). Prorating rent and refunding prepaid rent mirror Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, §§ 8-9 (proportional rent when a tenancy 'is determined before the end of such period by surrender'). Deposit return: § 15B(4). A board of health may order a unit vacated as unfit (105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.650, not separately quoted here). Excludes tenant-caused damage, which `tenant-caused-damage-ma` covers; the persons whose fault counts are identical in both (tenant, occupant, guest or invitee). Same structure as `casualty-termination-il`. Optional clause, never a default. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: E-mail Notices
bodyText: [Optional.] Landlord and Tenant agree that either may send the other routine communications, and any notice that neither this Lease nor applicable law requires to be delivered in a particular way, by e-mail to the address the other provides for that purpose: Tenant: [e-mail address]; Landlord: [e-mail address]. Tenant may also send Landlord any notice under this Lease or applicable law by e-mail to Landlord's address above. The sender will not send an e-mail in a form that keeps the recipient from printing or storing it. This Section does not apply to any notice to Tenant of nonpayment, default, termination, eviction or the right to cure, or to any other written notice to Tenant that applicable law requires to be delivered in a particular way; Landlord will deliver those as applicable law requires and may also send an e-mail copy. Either party may stop using e-mail under this Section at any time by written notice to the other.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 110G, § 5(b) (applies 'only to transactions between parties each of which has agreed to conduct transactions by electronic means'), § 5(c) (a party may refuse further electronic transactions and 'The right granted by this subsection may not be waived by agreement'), § 8(a) and (c) (a record whose storage or printing the sender inhibits 'shall not be enforceable against the recipient'), § 3(b)(3)(iv) (the chapter does not apply to a law governing any notice 'of the default, acceleration, repossession, foreclosure, or eviction, or the right to cure, under ... a rental agreement for, a primary residence of an individual'). Nonpayment and estate-at-will notices under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, §§ 11-12 must be 'in writing'; they are excluded. Massachusetts's own row: `electronic-notice-nm` fits in wording but rests on the New Mexico act (rule 26). Optional clause, never a default. Rule 15: written section-open. | CT: Tagged as written (tag-first screen, rules 26-28, CT log §2.1). Canvass triage (CT log §18): matches Connecticut's electronic transactions act: e-mail only by agreement, with a right to stop (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-270), and the clause's carve-out covers the act's exclusion of eviction, default and cure notices under a rental agreement for a primary residence (§ 1-268(c)(2)(B)) and notices with statutory methods (§§ 47a-23(c), 47a-11b, 47a-11d). Optional (rule 54). Rule 15: written section-open. | RI: Tagged as written (tag-first screen, rules 26-28, RI log §2.1). Matches Rhode Island's electronic transactions act: e-mail only by agreement (§ 42-127.1-5(b)), either party may refuse further electronic dealings and that right 'may not be waived by agreement' (§ 42-127.1-5(c)), statutory delivery methods must be followed (§ 42-127.1-8(b)), and a record the recipient cannot print or store is unenforceable (§ 42-127.1-8(c)). The clause excludes nonpayment, default, termination and eviction notices, which chapter 34-18 ties to mailing (§§ 34-18-35, -36, -37, -56). Optional (rule 54). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: House Rules
bodyText: [Optional.] Tenant will comply with the reasonable rules and regulations for the property that are attached to this Lease and made part of it at the beginning of the Term. Landlord may adopt or change a rule after the Term begins, but a new or changed rule binds Tenant only if it is reasonable and Tenant accepts it in writing, or it is made part of a renewal lease at the beginning of the renewal term. No rule will conflict with this Lease or with Massachusetts law.
notes: MA: No Massachusetts statute governs a landlord's house rules (MA triage battery recorded by the single-state screen, log §2.3). A rule adopted mid-term that substantially alters the terms of the tenancy within six months after protected tenant activity is presumed retaliatory (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 18: 'any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy'), and a term that violates law is unfair (940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(3)(a)1); requiring written acceptance or a renewal keeps a rule from being imposed unilaterally (Claude's drafting choice). Massachusetts's own row: `rules-ny` fits in wording but rests on N.Y. Real Prop. Law § 216 (rule 26). Optional clause, never a default. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Rent Concession
bodyText: [Optional. Use only if Landlord gives Tenant any rent concession.] In connection with this Lease, Landlord gives Tenant the following rent concession, which is part of this Lease: [describe each period of free or reduced Rent, credit or other concession, with its amount or value and the rental periods to which it applies]. When the concession ends, Monthly Rent will be the amount stated in this Lease.
notes: MA: Stating the concession and the full rent that resumes keeps any return to full rent within 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(3)(a)2 (the conditions of 'an automatic increase in rent' must be stated 'clearly and conspicuously'). No Massachusetts statute regulates rent concessions as such (no statute found by the canvass of topic rent-concession). A concession clawback on default is not offered: recovering a granted concession as damages could exceed 'the damages to which he is entitled under the law' (940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(c)) (Claude's drafting choice). Massachusetts's own row: `rent-concession-wi` rests on Wisconsin's ATCP rule (rule 26). Optional clause, never a default. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Criminal Activity
bodyText: [Optional.] Tenant, occupants and guests will not engage in criminal activity on the property that threatens the health, safety or peaceful enjoyment of the property by others, and will not use the property for the illegal keeping, sale or manufacture of controlled substances, illegal gaming, prostitution, or the illegal keeping of a weapon or explosive. A violation is a material breach of this Lease, for which Landlord may pursue the remedies provided in this Lease's Default by Tenant terms and Massachusetts law, including the remedy for illegal use of rented premises. Landlord will regain possession only through a court process. This Section does not apply to criminal activity of which Tenant or a member of Tenant's household is the victim, and Landlord will not treat a request for help from the police or other emergency assistance as a violation.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 139, § 19 (use of premises for 'prostitution, assignation, lewdness, illegal gaming', 'the illegal keeping, sale or manufacture of controlled substances' or 'the illegal keeping of a weapon' shall 'at the election of the lessor or owner, annul and make void the lease'; the lessor may seek an order to vacate or use ch. 239, and any injunction requires notice and a hearing). Self-help is barred (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 14; § 15F). Victim and emergency-call carve-outs: a summary process action taken because a tenant reported domestic violence to police or sought relief under ch. 186, §§ 23-29 is presumed retaliatory (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 2A). Massachusetts's own row: `criminal-activity-ky` rests on a Kentucky absence finding (rule 26). Optional clause, never a default. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Holdover Charge
bodyText: [Optional.] If Tenant remains in possession after this Lease ends without Landlord's written consent, Tenant will pay Landlord, as agreed damages for each day Tenant remains, [state a daily amount that reasonably estimates Landlord's likely loss, e.g. 150% of the daily Rent] instead of the Rent apportioned for that day. This charge does not apply to any day after this Lease or Tenant's possession ends for nonpayment of Rent, or to any day for which Massachusetts law lets Tenant keep possession by paying the Rent due. Landlord will not recover both this charge and Rent or use and occupancy for the same day, and will not recover this charge for any day for which a court awards Landlord damages for that day measured another way.
notes: MA: Rule 54 (a measure the statute doesn't set). Massachusetts sets no statutory holdover multiple: under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 3 tenants at sufferance 'shall be liable to pay rent therefor for such time as they may occupy or detain the same', and under § 13, after a no-fault termination of a tenancy at will, the tenant owes rent 'at the same rate as theretofore payable' during the notice period. Agreed damages are recognized by 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(c) ('an amount which the parties have otherwise agreed as to the amount of the damages'); whether a given figure is an unenforceable penalty is a case-law question (case law not searched). Exclusions (rule 53): under § 11 a written-lease tenant may cure nonpayment by paying 'on or before the day the answer is due', and under § 12 a tenant at will within 10 days; a stay under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, §§ 9-11 runs on court-set use and occupancy, so the non-stacking sentence keeps the charge out of those days. Model `holdover-rate-md`. Optional clause, never a default. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Rental Application Accuracy
bodyText: Tenant represents that the information Tenant gave Landlord in Tenant's rental application and during screening was true, correct and complete when given, and Tenant acknowledges that Landlord relied on that information in entering into this Lease. If any of that information was materially false or misleading, Tenant is in material breach of this Lease, and Landlord may exercise the remedies this Lease and applicable law provide for a material breach. This Section does not apply to information that Landlord was not permitted by law to request or consider. An answer that Massachusetts law allows an applicant to give, such as "no record" about a sealed eviction record or a sealed criminal record, is not false or misleading, and neither is an applicant's failure to disclose, or answer of "no record" about, a criminal record that has been expunged under Massachusetts law.
notes: MA: Overrides `rental-application-accuracy`, which could treat a statutorily permitted "no record" answer as a material misstatement. Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 16(j) ('An applicant for housing or credit with a sealed record on file with the court pursuant to section 16 of chapter 239 of the General Laws may answer 'no record' to an inquiry relative to that sealed court record'; effective 270 days after August 6, 2024 under 2024 Mass. Acts ch. 150, § 144); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 276, § 100A ('An applicant for employment or for housing or an occupational or professional license with a sealed record on file with the commissioner of probation may answer 'no record''), § 100C (same statement for sealed court-appearance records). Expunged records: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 276, § 100N's no-record answer covers applicants for state, county or municipal employment and employer applications; no housing counterpart was found (MA battery R2-check expunged record no-record answer housing (#390): 4 hits, none a housing rule; positive § 100K passed). The expunged-record words are the landlord's contractual commitment, not a statutory right. Otherwise the same text as the shared clause. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Fire Relocation Benefit
bodyText: FIRE RELOCATION BENEFIT. [Use if the property is part of a multi-unit residential building.] Massachusetts law requires every fire insurance policy on multi-unit residential property to provide, by endorsement, additional benefits of up to $750 per rental unit, without deductible, to cover the actual costs of relocating any tenant or lawful occupant displaced by fire or by damage resulting from fire. Those costs include hotel room rental, a security deposit and first month's rent for a new rental unit (if the Security Deposit or last month's rent is not already due back from Landlord to Tenant), clothing and furniture replacement, and other reasonable costs and living expenses resulting from the displacement. The insurer pays these benefits directly to the tenant or lawful occupant, after taking into account benefits available under any other policy. This notice cannot be waived.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 175, § 99, cl. Fifteenth A ('Every policy which insures multi-unit residential property against loss or damage by fire shall provide additional benefits, by endorsement attached to the policy, up to a limit of seven hundred and fifty dollars, without deductible, for each rental unit'; costs 'shall include, but not be limited to, hotel room rental, a security deposit and first month's rent for a new rental unit if the security deposit or last month's rent is not already due and owing from the landlord to the tenant, clothing replacement, furniture replacement'; benefits 'shall be paid by the insurer to the tenant or lawful occupant after taking into account benefits available under any other policy'; 'The landlord or lessor of the property shall notify each tenant or lawful occupant in writing of the benefits payable under this clause at the beginning of the lease or tenancy period'; 'A waiver of this provision in any lease or other rental agreement shall be void and unenforceable'). The lease is a writing given at the beginning of the tenancy, so it can serve as the notice; each lawful occupant who is not a signer should also get a copy (log §6.3). 'Multi-unit residential property' is not defined in the clause (case law not searched); the use note leaves single-family rentals out. The commissioner may exempt public higher-education residence halls (not relevant to the library). Education row: `edu-fire-relocation-benefit-notice-ma`. Rule 15: written section-open.
lease_clause_basis: REQUIRED_DISCLOSURE: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 175, § 99, cl. Fifteenth A

title: Common-Area Lighting on Tenant Meter
bodyText: [Use only in a building with two or three dwelling units, at the start of a new tenancy, if the lights for a common hallway, passageway, foyer or stairway are wired to the electric service for the property and Tenant pays for that service.] Tenant is responsible for paying for the electricity used by the lights in the following common areas, which are wired to the electric service for the property: [identify the common hallway, passageway, foyer and/or stairway].
notes: MA: 105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.300(F) (in residences containing two or three dwelling units, common-area lights 'may be wired to the electric service serving an adjacent dwelling unit, provided that if the occupant of such dwelling unit is responsible for paying for the electric service to such dwelling unit: (1) A written rental agreement shall state the occupant is responsible for paying for light in the common hallway, passageway, foyer, and/or stairway; and (2) Any requirement for an occupant to pay for lights in common areas shall begin only upon commencement of a new tenancy'). Read with 410.200(A), which lets a written rental agreement shift electricity to an occupant only where the meter serves the unit 'except as allowed by 105 CMR 410.300(F)'. Companion to `utilities-responsibility-ma`, whose item (a) cross-refers to this Section. Re-keyed at sync from `utilities-responsibility` to `common-area-lighting`: a companion clause keeps its own topic key (rule 57; Claude Code, 2026-10-09). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Sanitary Code Variance
bodyText: [Use only if a variance from the State Sanitary Code granted by the local board of health is in effect for the property.] The local board of health has granted a variance from the State Sanitary Code for the property. A copy of the variance is attached to this Lease.
notes: MA: 105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.700(D) ('The variance shall be: ... (3) Provided to all affected persons by the owner and attached to the rental agreement for new tenancies created while the variance is in effect'); a variance must be in writing (410.700(C)), and renewals follow the same notification requirements (410.700(I)). The attachment requirement applies to the 'rental agreement', so an oral tenancy at will still needs the variance provided; the clause covers written leases. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Condominium Repair Contacts
bodyText: [Use only if the property is a condominium unit.] The person or entity Landlord has designated to oversee maintenance and repair of the unit is: [name and telephone number]. The person or entity the condominium association has designated to oversee maintenance and repair of the common areas is: [name and telephone number]. Landlord will notify Tenant in writing whenever either designee changes.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 183A, § 10(k) ('In cases where a unit owner rents a unit to a tenant, the owner of said unit shall designate a person or entity who shall oversee the maintenance and repair of said unit'; 'At the commencement of any tenancy, the unit owner shall notify the tenant and the organization of unit owners in writing of the name and phone number of said person or entity, and shall notify the tenant in writing of the name and phone number of the person or entity designated to oversee maintenance and repair of the common areas'; change notices to the tenant). The owner must separately notify the association (§ 10(k)) and give it the names of tenants and occupants (§ 4); those are not lease text (`edu-condo-rental-notices-ma`). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Activity and Use Limitation
bodyText: [Use only if the property, or any part of it, is subject to a recorded Notice of Activity and Use Limitation under the Massachusetts Contingency Plan.] The property is subject to a Notice of Activity and Use Limitation recorded with the [name] Registry of Deeds at [book and page or document number]. That Notice is incorporated in this Lease by reference, and Tenant will comply with the activities and uses it permits and will not engage in the activities and uses it prohibits. A copy is attached.
notes: MA: 310 Mass. Code Regs. 40.1074(5) ('Upon transfer of any interest in and/or a right to use the property or a portion thereof that is subject to a Notice of Activity and Use Limitation, the Notice of Activity and Use Limitation shall be incorporated either in full or by reference into all future deeds, easements, mortgages, leases, licenses, occupancy agreements or any other instrument of transfer'); the owner's Notice itself contains 'an agreement to reference this Notice in all future deeds, easements, mortgages, leases' (40.1074(2)(k)). Attaching a copy is Claude's drafting choice, since incorporation by reference alone would not tell the tenant the restrictions. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Snow and Ice Removal
bodyText: Unless Landlord provides snow removal, Tenant will promptly remove snow and ice from the following areas under Tenant's exclusive use and control: [list each walkway, step, porch, deck, driveway, parking space and other exit used only by Tenant]. Tenant is not responsible for any area shared with other residents. In a building with more than one unit, Landlord remains responsible for keeping shared means of exit, exterior stairways, fire escapes and egress balconies free of snow and ice.
notes: MA: Overrides `snow-removal`, whose general description of areas Tenant uses for walking, parking and access does not name the areas. 105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.260(D)(4) ('The occupant is responsible for maintaining free of snow and ice, the means of egress under their exclusive use and control, provided there is a written rental agreement that clearly identifies the occupant's responsibility'); 410.260(D)(1)-(2) (in a multi-unit residence the owner maintains common-area egress and, 'For all exterior stairways, fire escapes, egress balconies and bridges', ensures 'They are maintained free of snow and ice'); 410.260(C) (single-unit occupant keeps egress free from obstruction). Reading (D)(2) and (D)(4) together, the clause keeps exterior stairways, fire escapes and egress balconies with the owner in any multi-unit building (Claude's cautious reading; log §6.3). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Collection Costs
bodyText: [Optional.] If any Rent or other amount Tenant owes under this Lease remains unpaid more than 30 days after it is due, and Landlord refers it to a collection agency or attorney for collection, Tenant will pay Landlord the reasonable costs of collection Landlord actually incurs, not to exceed [state a cap, e.g. 15 percent of the amount collected]. Any attorney's fees are recoverable only as this Lease's Tenant Default terms and Massachusetts law allow, and Landlord's right to them carries Tenant's reciprocal right under Massachusetts law. Landlord will not charge any collection cost for an amount that is less than 30 days past due.
notes: MA: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(16) (unfair for a creditor to collect 'any amount (including interest, fees, charges or expenses incidental to the principal obligation) unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law'); 'Debt' means money 'more than 30 days past due and owing, unless a different period is agreed to by the debtor' arising from a 'lease' (940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.03). Without an express lease term a landlord collecting rent more than 30 days overdue may not add collection costs. The 30-day floor also keeps the charge clear of Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c) ('No lease or other rental agreement shall impose any interest or penalty for failure to pay rent until thirty days after such rent shall have been due'). A lease attorney-fee right implies a reciprocal tenant right (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 20). The cap is the landlord's figure; whether a percentage cost is 'reasonable' is a case-law question (case law not searched). Third-party collectors are separately regulated (not researched). Optional clause (rule 54: a charge the regulation lets the agreement authorize), never a default. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Credit Card Surcharge Ban
bodyText: Massachusetts law says no seller in any sales transaction may impose a surcharge on a cardholder who elects to use a credit card instead of paying by cash, check or similar means. The statute does not say whether paying rent is a sales transaction, so whether the ban reaches rent is unsettled. The cautious course is not to charge tenants more for paying rent by credit card. The same law contemplates a discount for paying by cash or check instead.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 140D, § 28A(a)(2) ('No seller in any sales transaction may impose a surcharge on a cardholder who elects to use a credit card'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 140D, § 1 ('Surcharge', any means of increasing the regular price to a cardholder which is not imposed upon customers paying by cash, check or similar means). 'Sales transaction' is not defined in § 1; whether rent is covered is unsettled. Case law not searched. MA battery A payment-method surcharge: card surcharge statutes: 3 hits; positives passed (only 140D §§ 1, 28A and the travel-agent rule in ch. 93, § 48B). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Payment Method Rule
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule on how rent must be paid. Nothing we found requires you to accept cash, or bars you from requiring payment by check, money order, electronic transfer or an online portal. We also found no rule on convenience fees for rent payments, apart from the general ban on credit card surcharges in sales transactions, which may reach rent; get advice before adding a card surcharge. You may name the accepted methods in the lease. Check local rules too.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent. MA battery A acceptable-payment-methods: rent payment method / electronic payment: 2 hits; positives passed (hits only ch. 171, § 75 credit unions and 254 Mass. Code Regs. 7.00 broker records; neither governs rent). MA battery A acceptable-payment-methods 2: payment-method words near rent: 3 hits; positives passed (ch. 105A, § 3 self-storage, ch. 235, § 34 exemptions, 803 Mass. Code Regs. 1.000; none governs rent). Searched General Laws, Constitution, full CMR and court rules. See Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 140D, § 28A for card surcharges. Case law not searched. Local: Boston, Cambridge and other city ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Algorithmic Rent Ban
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule that names algorithmic or software-based rent setting. The state antitrust act still makes every contract, combination or conspiracy in restraint of trade unlawful, and it is read in line with federal antitrust law. Whether sharing data with a pricing tool that coordinates competing landlords' rents is unlawful under that general rule is unsettled. Get legal advice before using such a tool.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent (no algorithm-specific rule). MA battery A algorithmic-rent-setting: algorithm/software pricing near rent: 9 hits; positives passed (all hits are tax, UCC, MassHealth rate or data-center rules; none on rent). The word algorithm does not appear in 2023-2026 session laws. General rule: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93, § 4 ('Every contract, combination in the form of trust or otherwise, or conspiracy, in restraint of trade or commerce in the commonwealth shall be unlawful'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93, § 1 ('construed in harmony with judicial interpretations of comparable federal antitrust statutes'). Case law not searched. Local: city ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Application Fees Not Allowed
bodyText: At or before the start of a tenancy, you and your agent may not require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay more than four things: rent for the first full month, rent for the last full month at the same rate, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock. An application, screening or credit-check fee is not on that list, so do not require one. A conflicting lease term or tenant waiver is void.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(b) ('no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following'; agent wording effective August 1, 2025); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(8) ('any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of any provision of this section shall be deemed to be against public policy'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(4)(a) (same list as an unfair or deceptive practice). No application-fee cap, CPI adjustment, refund or pre-application disclosure rule exists because no fee may be required. Case law not searched (e.g. on a pass-through credit report charge). MA battery A application-fees: rental application / screening fee: 12 hits; positives passed (synthetic; only residential-adjacent hit is the manufactured-housing ban in 940 Mass. Code Regs. 10.00). Local: city ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Eviction Record Question Statement
bodyText: If your rental application asks about the applicant's prior eviction cases, it must include this statement: "An applicant for housing or credit with a sealed record on file with the court pursuant to section 16 of chapter 239 of the General Laws may answer 'no record' to an inquiry relative to that sealed court record." A party is liable for leaving it out only after a written warning from the Attorney General goes unaddressed for 90 days.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 16(j) ('An application used to screen applicants for housing or credit that seeks information concerning prior eviction actions of the applicant shall include the following statement'); same subsection ('has first been issued a written warning from the attorney general and has failed to address the violation within 90 days'). Prescribed text quoted verbatim in the body. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Payment Application Order
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule fixing the order in which you must apply a tenant's payment to rent, fees or other charges. The lease may set the order. Applying payments to rent first is the safer choice, because a late charge may not be imposed until rent is 30 days overdue, and a payment applied to fees could leave rent showing as unpaid.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent. MA battery A application-of-payments: order of applying payments near rent/tenant: 0 hits; positives passed (synthetic). The same allocation pattern without the rent/tenant context (battery A application-of-payments: order of applying payments (any context)) hit 86 units, none on tenancies. Related: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c) ('No lease or other rental agreement shall impose any interest or penalty for failure to pay rent until thirty days after such rent shall have been due'). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Collection Fees Need Lease Authority
bodyText: Under the Attorney General's debt collection rules, rent or other money owed under a household lease that is more than 30 days past due is a debt. Collecting any interest, fee, charge or expense added to it is an unfair or deceptive practice unless the lease expressly authorizes that amount or the law permits it. So a collection fee must be written into the lease. Separately, no interest or penalty for late rent may be imposed until rent is 30 days overdue.
notes: MA: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.03 ('Debt means money or its equivalent which is, or is alleged to be, more than 30 days past due and owing'; covers a lease of real property for personal, family or household purposes); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(16) ('The collection of any amount (including interest, fees, charges or expenses incidental to the principal obligation) unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c) ('No lease or other rental agreement shall impose any interest or penalty for failure to pay rent until thirty days after such rent shall have been due'). Whether a flat collection fee is an unlawful penalty or unrecoverable damages (940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(c)) is unsettled; case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: All-In Rent in Ads
bodyText: Since September 2, 2025, the Attorney General's fee rule covers dwelling units for rent. Whenever you present the price of a unit, in an ad, listing or reply, the first time and every later time, you must clearly and conspicuously show the Total Price: the most the tenant must pay, including every mandatory fee. You may state it as a monthly amount if you also clearly disclose the full lease period. Show the Total Price more prominently than other pricing, and show it before asking for personal or billing information, with narrow exceptions.
notes: MA: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.03 ('Product shall include memberships, subscriptions, and dwelling units available for rent or lease'; 'Total Price. The maximum price a consumer must pay for a Product, inclusive of all fees, charges, or other expenses'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.04(1), (4), (6); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.04 ('the seller must also disclose Clearly and Conspicuously the full period covered by the rental or lease'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.09 ('shall apply to acts committed or practices in force as of September 2, 2025'). Government Charges may be excluded from Total Price. Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Fee Disclosure Before Signing
bodyText: When you first present the Total Price, and again in the final price presentation before the tenant signs, you must clearly and conspicuously disclose the nature, purpose and amount of each fee or charge. For any fee that is optional or that you can waive, say so and explain how to avoid it. The final presentation must also show the final transaction amount. Do not suggest a fee is required by law unless it is. Violations are unfair or deceptive practices under the consumer protection act.
notes: MA: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.04(2)(a) ('the nature, purpose, and amount of any fees, charges, or other expenses that would be imposed on the transaction due to the purchase of that Product'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.04(3) ('in the final presentation of the price of any Product prior to the Sale of the Product'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.04(5) ('Misrepresenting that any fees, charges, or other expenses or any portion thereof are required by law'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.03 ('The terms Sale or Sell includes lease, rent, or barter'). Separately, 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(16) bars collecting past-due fees not expressly authorized by the lease (row edu-collection-fees-ma). No first-page or verbatim-sentence fee rule found (MA battery A fee-transparency: first-page fee disclosure: 4 hits; positives passed; hits are 93 § 48, 255D § 9, 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.000 and the statement-of-condition notice in 186 § 15B). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Provide Promised Services
bodyText: If you represent or agree that services or supplies will be provided during the tenancy, failing to provide them is an unfair or deceptive practice. If you say you will reimburse the tenant for repairs, supplies or services the tenant pays for, you must reimburse within a reasonable or agreed time after notice. We found no Massachusetts statute or regulation aimed specifically at fees for services not provided to an ordinary residential tenant, but charging for an amenity you do not deliver risks these rules.
notes: MA: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(1)(f) ('Fail to provide services and/or supplies after the making of any representation or agreement, that such services would be provided during the term'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(1)(g) ('Fail to reimburse the tenant within a reasonable or agreed time after notice'). MA battery A fee-unprovided-service: charge for service not provided: 20 hits; positives passed (hits are care facilities, MassHealth, manufactured housing 940 Mass. Code Regs. 10.00; none for ordinary tenancies). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Fees As Additional Rent
bodyText: We found no Massachusetts statute or regulation that lets a lease turn fees into rent, or that bars it. One statute assumes a lease may make the landlord's legal costs payable as additional rent, but then the tenant gets a matching right to recover attorneys' fees from you. Calling a fee rent does not avoid the 30-day wait before any late interest or penalty. Whether an unpaid fee labeled as rent supports a nonpayment eviction notice turns on case law.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent (no general fees-as-rent rule). MA battery A fees-as-rent: additional rent / definition of rent: 10 hits; positives passed (relevant hits only ch. 186, §§ 15B, 20 and public-housing 760 Mass. Code Regs. 6.00). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 20 ('amounts paid by the landlord therefor shall be paid by the tenant as additional rent'; implied reciprocal covenant; 'Any waiver of this section shall be void as against public policy'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(5) ('shall mean the periodic sum paid by the tenant for the use and occupation of the dwelling unit'; definition limited to that paragraph); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c). Section 8/public housing: not researched beyond 760 Mass. Code Regs. 6.00. Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Passing Through Government Charges
bodyText: You may make a tenant pay part of a real estate tax increase during the lease only through a lease clause, agreed before the tenancy starts, that meets the tax escalation rules. Otherwise, demanding the increase during the tenancy is an unfair or deceptive practice. We found no Massachusetts statute or regulation on passing other government fees, such as rental registration or inspection fees, through to tenants. Any such charge must still be in the lease and in the advertised Total Price.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15C ('No lease relating to residential real estate shall contain a provision which obligates a lessee to make payments to the lessor on account of an increased real estate tax'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(2)(c) ('Demand payment for increased real estate taxes during the term of the tenancy unless, prior to the inception of the tenancy, a valid agreement is made'). Other government fees: MA battery A government-fee-reimbursement 3: pass government fee/tax to tenant: 23 hits; positives passed (no rule on registration or inspection fee pass-through; Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 59, § 12C lets a tenant who is taxed on the real estate retain the tax from rent unless otherwise agreed). Total Price: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.03 (Government Charges cover only charges imposed on the transaction, not ones the seller 'chooses (but is not legally required) to pass on to consumers'). See planned clause tax-escalation-ma. Local: municipal registration/inspection fee ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Late Fee Limits
bodyText: No lease or rental agreement may impose interest or a penalty for late rent until 30 days after the rent was due, and a penalty clause that breaks this rule is itself an unfair or deceptive practice. Beyond that wait, we found no Massachusetts statute or regulation capping the amount of a residential late fee, requiring a late-fee notice, or giving particular tenants a longer grace period. A late fee must be in the lease to be collected. Whether a large fee is an unenforceable penalty turns on case law.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c) ('No lease or other rental agreement shall impose any interest or penalty for failure to pay rent until thirty days after such rent shall have been due'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(3)(a)3 ('Contains a penalty clause not in conformity with the provisions of M.G.L. c. 186'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(a) ('Impose any interest or penalty for late payment or rent unless such payment is 30 days overdue'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(16) (collection of fees not 'expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law'). No cap, notice or senior grace period: MA battery A late-fee: late charge / penalty for late rent: 24 hits (relevant hits only 186 § 15B, 186 § 22, 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.000, self-storage ch. 105A, condo ch. 183A, public housing 760 Mass. Code Regs. 6.00). Acceptance waiver: none (battery A waiver-by-acceptance: acceptance of rent waives notice/default: 2 hits). Shutdown late-fee bar: see edu-shutdown-late-fee-ma. Case law not searched. Local: city ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Lease Type Parity Rule
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule requiring the same terms or rent for a tenancy at will (month-to-month) and a fixed-term lease, or capping the rent difference between them. The two still differ by law. A tenancy at will ends on three months' written notice, or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, on written notice equal to the rental period or thirty days, whichever is longer, while a written lease runs for its term. Both share the same deposit, up-front money and late-fee limits.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent. MA battery A lease-type-parity 2: month-to-month vs fixed-term terms: 0 hits; positives passed (synthetic; the one unit the context filter excluded, ch. 186, § 8 (proportional rent), has no parity rule either). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12 ('the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(4) ('termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement'). Case law not searched. Local: rent-stabilization or just-cause ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Notice Fee Rule
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule on charging a tenant for preparing or serving a notice, such as a notice to quit. General limits still apply. A charge tied to late rent cannot be imposed until the rent is 30 days overdue, and a fee added to a past-due debt can be collected only if the lease expressly authorizes it. Under a written lease, a tenant cures a nonpayment notice by paying all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit, by the answer date.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent. MA battery A notice-service-fee: fee for preparing/serving notice to tenant: 2 hits; positives passed (synthetic; hits only public housing 760 Mass. Code Regs. 6.00 and assisted living 940 Mass. Code Regs. 40.00). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(16) ('unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 11 ('pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit'). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Rent Concession Limits
bodyText: We found no Massachusetts statute or regulation written for rent concessions. Two general rules matter. If a concession is lost or must be repaid when rent is paid late, that may operate as a penalty for late rent, which cannot be imposed until rent is 30 days overdue. And advertised pricing must clearly show the Total Price the tenant must pay; a monthly figure may be used if the full lease period is also clearly disclosed. Whether a concession clawback is a penalty turns on case law.
notes: MA: No concession-specific rule: MA battery A rent-concession: rent concession / free rent / discount: 2 hits; positives passed (synthetic; refugee resettlement and waterways rules only). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c) ('No lease or other rental agreement shall impose any interest or penalty for failure to pay rent until thirty days after such rent shall have been due'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 38.04 ('advertise the Total Price to rent or lease the dwelling unit as a dollar amount to be paid by the consumer on a periodic basis'). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Local Rent Control Prohibited
bodyText: No Massachusetts city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except a narrow voluntary scheme that owners may decline after six months. Rent control means any regulation requiring below-market rents, and related rules on occupancy, services, evictions or condominium conversion within such a scheme. The ban does not cover publicly owned, publicly subsidized or federally assisted housing, or mobile homes. We found no statewide cap on rent increases for private housing.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 40P, § 4 ('No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 40P, § 3 ('any regulation that in any way requires below-market rents for residential properties'; excludes 'publicly owned housing, publicly subsidized housing, federally assisted housing, or mobile homes'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 40P, § 5 ('this chapter shall preempt, supersede or nullify any inconsistent, contrary or conflicting state or local law'). No statewide rent cap: MA battery A rent-control: rent control / stabilization / preemption: 21 hits; positives passed. No 2023-2026 session law amends ch. 40P. Pending ballot measures not researched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Local Rules and Code Actions
bodyText: Apart from the rent control ban, we found no Massachusetts statute that preempts local landlord-tenant rules or limits local rental registration or periodic inspection programs. The state constitution does limit local power to enact civil law governing private relationships, so a local rule that regulates private landlord-tenant relationships, such as just-cause eviction, may need a special act of the Legislature; how far this limit reaches is a case-law question. Check the city or town where the unit is. Sanitary code enforcement is not left to tenants alone. A public agency, as well as affected occupants, may bring a court action over sanitary code violations, and the court may issue injunctions, order rent paid into court, or appoint a receiver.
notes: MA: No limit on local registration/inspection: MA battery A rent-control 3: state limits on local rental registration/inspection: 0 hits; positives passed (synthetic). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 111, § 127I ('any civil action concerning violations of the sanitary code by any affected occupants or a public agency'; 'appoint a receiver'). Source-of-income: no state preemption of local protections found; state law itself protects public-assistance recipients (not researched here). Local: Boston, Cambridge, Somerville and other registration, inspection, lead-safe or certificate ordinances (flagged, not researched). Mass. Const. amend. art. 89, § 7 withholds from cities and towns the power to enact 'private or civil law governing civil relationships except as an incident to an exercise of an independent municipal power' (§ 7(5)). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Escalation Clauses and Retaliation
bodyText: If your lease provides for an automatic rent increase, it must state clearly and conspicuously the conditions on which the increase is determined. A real estate tax escalation clause has its own rules. Massachusetts retaliation law has no safe harbor for increases written into the lease. Notice of a rent increase within six months after a tenant's protected activity, such as a code complaint, is presumed a reprisal. You can rebut that only by clear and convincing evidence that the increase was not a reprisal, that you had sufficient independent justification, and that you would have raised the rent in the same way and at the same time anyway.
notes: MA: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(3)(a)2 ('Fails to state clearly and conspicuously in the rental agreement the conditions upon which an automatic increase in rent shall be determined'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15C (tax escalation); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 18 ('of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months'; 'rebutted only by clear and convincing evidence'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 2A (same presumption as an eviction defense). Neither § 18 nor § 239, § 2A contains an exception for a lease escalation clause. Whether a fixed-term lease may be increased mid-term without a lease clause is contract law; case law not searched. See planned clauses rent-increase-terms-ma and tax-escalation-ma. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Raising Rent
bodyText: Massachusetts has no separate rent-increase notice statute for ordinary housing. For a tenancy at will, you change rent by ending the tenancy with written notice: three months, or if rent is paid more often, the rental interval or thirty days, whichever is longer. The notice may offer a new tenancy on different terms. During a fixed-term lease, rent is set by the lease, and any automatic increase must be stated clearly and conspicuously. An increase within six months after protected tenant activity is presumed retaliatory.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12 ('Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing'; 'Such written notice may include an offer to establish a new tenancy for the same premises on terms different from that of the tenancy being terminated'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(3)(a)2; Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 18. No other notice rule: MA battery A rent-increase-notice: notice of rent increase: 3 hits; positives passed (only the manufactured-housing rules in Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 140, § 32L and 940 Mass. Code Regs. 10.00, and public housing 760 Mass. Code Regs. 6.00). Emergency pricing: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.18(3) reaches goods or services necessary for health, safety or welfare during a declared emergency; whether rent is covered is unsettled. Fixed-term lease mid-term increases without a clause: contract law, case law not searched. Local: city ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Rent Installment Rule
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule on setting rent in installments or on whether scheduled installments count as partial payments. The lease may set the payment schedule. One limit applies: after the tenancy starts, you may not demand rent in advance beyond the current month's rent. So a schedule cannot require paying future months early, apart from last month's rent collected at the start.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent. MA battery A rent-installments: rent payable in installments / partial payment: 2 hits; positives passed (synthetic; hits are UCC leases ch. 106, § 2A-522 and condominium ch. 183A, § 6). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(d) ('No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent'). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Advance Rent After Move-In
bodyText: Once a tenancy has started, you may not demand rent in advance beyond the current month's rent, or a security deposit larger than the law allows. You cannot require a tenant to prepay several months after move-in, even in exchange for a lower rent. Last month's rent may be collected only at or before the start of the tenancy. Any advance payment made under these rules binds later owners of the property.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(d) ('No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent'; 'The payment in advance for occupancy pursuant to this section shall be binding upon all successors in interest'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(4)(a) ('demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent'). Voluntary tenant prepayment not demanded by the landlord: case law not searched. Tenant deductions from rent allowed by law (deposit and last month's rent interest under § 15B(2)(a) and (3)(b); ch. 111, § 127L; ch. 239, § 8A) are why the shared rent-payment clause's applicable-law exception to the no-deduction wording matters. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Monthly Rent Receipt Rule
bodyText: Massachusetts requires written receipts only when you collect last month's rent in advance or a security deposit, each with set contents. We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no general duty to give a receipt for ordinary monthly rent, even when paid in cash, and no rule making a missing cash receipt an eviction defense. Giving a dated receipt for every cash payment is still good practice and helps prove payment.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent (general receipt duty). MA battery A rent-receipts: receipt for rent payment: 17 hits; positives passed (only ch. 186, § 15B receipts; § 12 and § 18 hit only on the receipt of a notice; ch. 140, § 32P manufactured housing; others not tenancy rules). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(2)(a) ('shall give to such tenant or prospective tenant at the time of such advance payment a receipt'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(2)(b) ('Said receipt shall be signed by the person receiving the security deposit'). Case law not searched. Local: city ordinances (flagged, not researched). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Rent Reporting Rule
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule requiring you to offer positive rent reporting, and none barring you from asking tenants to join a rent-reporting program. One exception applies during a federal government shutdown. You may not furnish rental payment data about missed rent to a consumer reporting agency if, within 30 days after the missed payment, the tenant gives you notice and documentation that the tenant is an impacted federal worker and that the shutdown's significant financial impact caused the nonpayment. This applies only during a federal government shutdown and until 30 days after it ends (the governor may extend that by up to 75 days), and only to tenancies that began before the shutdown.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent (general rule). MA battery A rent-reporting: rent payment data to credit bureaus: 1 hits; positives passed (synthetic; the only hit is the shutdown section, which the saved General Laws file under key ch. 221, § 17 although it is ch. 239, § 17). 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 73, § 54 (adding ch. 239, § 17(e): 'A landlord shall not impose a late fee for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit or furnish rental payment data to a consumer reporting agency'; in effect only during a shutdown and 30 days after, extendable up to 75 days by the governor). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Taxes on Rent
bodyText: Massachusetts sales tax covers sales and rentals of tangible personal property and a narrow set of services, not leases of homes, so ordinary residential rent is not subject to sales tax. A separate 5 per cent room occupancy excise applies to rooms in a lodging house, hotel or similar place occupied for not more than 90 consecutive days, and to short-term rentals of not more than 31 consecutive days. So a rooming house or short-term stay may be taxed even though an apartment lease is not.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 64H, § 1 ('Sale' covers lease or rental 'of tangible personal property or the performance of services'; 'the term services shall be limited to telecommunications services'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 64G, § 1 ('for a period of not more than 90 consecutive calendar days'; short-term rental 'for a period of not more than 31 consecutive calendar days'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 64G, § 3 ('at the rate of 5 per cent of the total amount of rent for each such occupancy'). Exemptions in § 3 (e.g. under $15 a day; short-term rental 14 days a year or less) and local option excises not researched; DOR regulations not read. No repealed-local-tax pass-through rule found. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Dishonored Check Remedy
bodyText: If a tenant's check is dishonored for no account or insufficient funds, Massachusetts gives you a civil remedy. Send a written demand in the statute's prescribed form, printed in at least ten point type in both English and Spanish, by regular mail and by certified mail, return receipt requested. If the tenant does not pay within thirty days, the tenant is liable for the check amount plus damages set by the court of not less than one hundred nor more than five hundred dollars.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93, § 40A ('shall be printed in at least ten point type in both the English and Spanish languages'; 'in no event shall the amount of such damages be less than one hundred nor more than five hundred dollars'). The statute does not fix or cap a contractual returned-check service charge; no returned-payment fee cap found (MA battery A returned-payments: dishonored check / returned payment charge: 13 hits; UCC, banking and agency fee rules only). Criminal: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 266, § 37. Whether a lease returned-payment fee is an interest or penalty barred for 30 days by Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c) is unsettled; case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Postdated Checks for Arrears
bodyText: Rent or other money more than 30 days past due is a debt under the Attorney General's debt collection rules. When collecting it, do not request or demand a postdated check, draft or similar instrument from the tenant, and do not deposit one before its date. Both are unfair or deceptive practices. Keep this in mind when setting up a repayment plan for back rent.
notes: MA: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(17) ('Requesting or demanding from a debtor a post dated check, draft, order for withdrawal or other similar instrument or method in payment for the debt or any portion thereof'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.03 ('Debt means money or its equivalent which is, or is alleged to be, more than 30 days past due and owing'). No MA rule that accepting a postdated check forfeits bad-check remedies was found. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Shutdown Late Fee Bar
bodyText: During a federal government shutdown, and until 30 days after it ends unless the governor extends that by up to 75 days, special rules protect tenants who are impacted federal workers. If such a tenant gives you notice and documentation within 30 days after a missed rent payment that the shutdown caused it, you may not impose a late fee for that nonpayment or report it to a consumer reporting agency. The tenant still owes the rent, and you are protected when you rely in good faith on the documentation.
notes: MA: 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 73, § 54 (adds Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 17, effective November 25, 2025; the saved General Laws file it under key ch. 221, § 17). 2026 Mass. Acts ch. 137, § 84 replaces the word all with any in the shutdown definition (emergency act approved July 9, 2026). 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 73, § 54 ('A landlord shall not impose a late fee for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit'; 'not later than 30 days after the missed rent payment'; 'Nothing in this section shall relieve a tenant from the obligation to pay rent'; 'A landlord or owner shall not be liable for actions taken in good faith reliance on documentation'; 'the governor may postpone such expiration by not more than 75 days'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Shutdown Eviction Limits
bodyText: While the federal shutdown law is in effect, you may not terminate a tenancy or send a notice to quit for nonpayment against a tenant who gives you notice and documentation of significant financial impact from the shutdown as an impacted federal worker. A summary process complaint filed during a shutdown must state that you have not received notice that the defendant is an impacted federal worker. Courts must grant such tenants continuances and toll their deadlines.
notes: MA: 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 73, § 54 (adds Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 17, effective November 25, 2025; the saved General Laws file it under key ch. 221, § 17). 2026 Mass. Acts ch. 137, § 84 replaces the word all with any in the shutdown definition (emergency act approved July 9, 2026). 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 73, § 54 ('send any notice, including a notice to quit, requesting or demanding that a tenant of a residential dwelling unit vacate the premises'; 'a statement that the landlord has not received notice that the defendant is an impacted federal worker'; 'shall be tolled if the defendant provides the court documentation'). Applies to tenancies that began before the shutdown ('any resident whose tenancy began before a federal government shutdown'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Shutdown Use of Last Month Rent
bodyText: During a federal shutdown, if a tenant who is an impacted federal worker cannot pay rent because of it, you may use last month's rent you collected in advance to pay expenses such as the mortgage, utilities and repairs. You may not deduct the tenant's unpaid rent from it. You must tell the tenant in writing that you used the funds early and that you remain obligated to apply them as rent for the last month. You still owe the interest due on that rent.
notes: MA: 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 73, § 54 (adds Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 17, effective November 25, 2025; the saved General Laws file it under key ch. 221, § 17). 2026 Mass. Acts ch. 137, § 84 replaces the word all with any in the shutdown definition (emergency act approved July 9, 2026). 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 73, § 54 ('may access and utilize the funds received from said last month's rent in advance if the tenant is an impacted federal worker'; 'a lessor shall not deduct from said last month's rent in advance any amount to account for the tenant's nonpayment of rent'; 'the lessor remains obligated to apply such funds to its intended application as rent for the last month of tenancy'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Late Subsidy Payments
bodyText: We found no Massachusetts statute or regulation barring a late fee on the part of rent a housing subsidy pays; the general 30-day wait before any late interest or penalty applies to all rent. If unpaid rent was caused by a government agency's failure or delay in mailing or delivering a rental payment, check or voucher, the court must continue an eviction hearing at least seven days. If all rent due with interest and costs is then tendered, the tenancy is treated as not terminated.
notes: MA: No subsidy late-fee rule: MA battery A subsidy-late-fee: late fee on subsidy portion of rent: 0 hits; positives passed (synthetic). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, §§ 11, 12 ('in the mailing or delivery of any subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher other than a salary payment'; 'shall continue the hearing not less than seven days'; 'treat the tenancy as not having been terminated'). Applies to written leases (§ 11) and tenancies at will (§ 12). Federal program (HUD) rules not researched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Interest on Unpaid Amounts
bodyText: If there is no agreement on a rate, interest on money owed runs at six dollars per hundred a year, and a higher rate can be recovered in a lawsuit only if agreed in writing. Interest on late rent may not start until 30 days after the rent was due. When you win a contract judgment, such as for unpaid rent or damages, the court clerk adds interest at the contract rate, or twelve per cent a year from breach or demand if none was set.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 107, § 3 ('If there is no agreement or provision of law for a different rate, the interest of money shall be at the rate of six dollars on each hundred for a year'; 'No greater rate than that before mentioned shall be recovered in a suit unless the agreement to pay it is in writing'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(c); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 231, § 6C ('at the contract rate, if established, or at the rate of twelve per cent per annum from the date of the breach or demand'). Collection of interest on a 30-day past-due debt also needs lease authorization or law: 940 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(16). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Veteran Rent Arrears Payments
bodyText: We found no Massachusetts incentive paid to landlords for renting to veterans. But a local veterans' agent may pay an eligible veteran tenant's overdue rent to prevent eviction. The payment is the full arrearage or three months' rent, whichever is less. As a condition, you must agree in writing to end all eviction proceedings on receiving approval, and not to restart them based on past or current tenant violations. Read that agreement carefully before signing.
notes: MA: No landlord incentive: MA battery A veterans-incentive: incentive to landlords renting to veterans: 2 hits; positives passed (synthetic; hits are 108 Mass. Code Regs. 7.00 veterans' benefits and 803 Mass. Code Regs. 5.00 CORI fee waivers for veterans organizations). 108 Mass. Code Regs. 7.07(2) ('Rental Arrearages to Prevent Eviction'; 'The landlord agrees in writing that all eviction proceedings will be terminated before or upon receipt of written approval by the veterans' agent'; 'the arrearage payment shall be either the fullamount ofthe outstanding arrearages or three month's rent, whichever is less' [sic, as saved]). Eligibility conditions not fully researched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Accepting Rent After Notice
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no rule on whether accepting rent, or a partial payment, after a default or a notice to quit waives the default or the notice, or creates a new tenancy. That question is left to case law, which we did not search. Separately, a tenant under a written lease can stop a nonpayment termination by paying all rent due with interest and costs by the answer date. Get advice before accepting money after serving a notice to quit.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent. MA battery A waiver-by-acceptance: acceptance of rent waives notice/default: 2 hits; positives passed (synthetic; hits are a MassHealth waiver rule and public housing 760 Mass. Code Regs. 6.00). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 11 ('pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit'); tenancy at will 10-day cure: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12. Case law not searched. Shared clauses with a non-waiver sentence are not contradicted by any MA statute found. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Statement of Condition
bodyText: If you take a security deposit, give the tenant a separate signed written statement of the unit's present condition when you receive the deposit or within ten days after the tenancy starts, whichever is later. It must list all existing damage, including certified or adjudicated sanitary or building code violations, and carry the statutory notice in twelve-point bold type at the top of page one. The tenant has fifteen days to return it with any list of disagreements; you then have fifteen days to return a copy with your signed agreement or a clear statement of disagreement.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(2)(c) ('upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later'; 'contain the following notice in twelve-point bold-face type at the top of the first page thereof'; 'within fifteen days of receiving said separate list'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(b)(iii) (deposit allowed only if 'the tenant is given the statement of condition'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(4)(e). Listed damage may not later be deducted: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(4). Applies to any tenancy with a deposit (at will or fixed term); not to vacation rentals of 100 days or less (§ 15B(9)). See planned clause existing-condition-ma for the verbatim notice. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Move-Out Damage Inspection
bodyText: You may enter to inspect the unit for damage that could be deducted from the security deposit during the last thirty days of the tenancy, or after either side has given notice of intent to end it. We found no Massachusetts rule requiring a joint move-out inspection or a separate notice inviting the tenant to attend. Any damage deduction still requires a sworn, itemized list with written cost evidence within thirty days after the tenancy ends.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(a)(iii) ('to inspect, within the last thirty days of the tenancy or after either party has given notice to the other of intention to terminate the tenancy'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(4) ('sworn to by the lessor or his agent under pains and penalties of perjury'). No joint-inspection or inspection-notice rule: MA battery A condition-inspection: move-in/move-out inspection notice or joint inspection: 11 hits; positives passed (only § 15B and lead, environmental and pool inspection rules). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Preset Deposit Charges
bodyText: Do not put a schedule of fixed cleaning, carpet or repair charges in the lease to take from the security deposit. You may deduct only for unpaid rent or water charges, a lawful tax escalation, and a reasonable amount to repair damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, backed by a sworn itemized list and written cost evidence. A lease term that conflicts with the deposit law is void, and trying to enforce it forfeits your right to keep any of the deposit.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(4) ('a reasonable amount necessary to repair any damage caused to the dwelling unit by the tenant'; 'No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those set forth in this section'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(6)(c) ('uses in any lease signed by the tenant any provision which conflicts with any provision of this section and attempts to enforce such provision'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(8) ('shall be deemed to be against public policy and therefore void and unenforceable'). Whether routine cleaning is damage beyond reasonable wear and tear is case law, not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Unclaimed Deposit Refunds
bodyText: A security deposit refund you owe but cannot deliver is unclaimed property, not yours to keep. If it is not claimed within three years after it became payable, it is presumed abandoned. You must then report it to the State Treasurer by November 1 each year, as of June 30, and pay it over with the report. Do not put a lease term forfeiting an unclaimed deposit to you; terms that conflict with the deposit law are void.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 200A, § 1 ('Property', all intangible property, including 'credit balances, customer overpayments, security deposits, refunds'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 200A, § 5 ('shall be presumed abandoned unless claimed by the beneficiary or person entitled thereto within three years after the date prescribed for payment or delivery'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 200A, § 7(d) ('no later than November first of each year as of June thirtieth'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 200A, § 8A (pay at time of filing); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 200A, § 12(c) (penalty up to five hundred dollars for failing to report). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(8) (conflicting lease terms void). No 90-day or 60-day landlord-keeps rule found. Treasurer regulations and dormancy charges (ch. 200A, § 15C covers bank accounts) not researched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Deposit Installment Right
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no tenant right to pay the security deposit in installments. You may agree to an installment schedule, but the total deposit still may not exceed the first month's rent, and the deposit must be handled under the deposit law from receipt. If state regulations authorize a fee in lieu of a deposit, that fee may be recurring, but the fee plus any deposit may not exceed one month's rent.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent. MA battery A deposit-installments: security deposit paid in installments: 2 hits; positives passed (synthetic; hits are court-ordered use-and-occupancy deposits in ch. 239, §§ 8A, 11). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(b)(iii) ('a security deposit equal to the first month's rent'; fee in lieu may be 'a recurring monthly fee'; 'the sum of fees paid to waive a security deposit and the payment of the security deposit shall not exceed, in total, the amount of 1 month's rent'). Whether implementing regulations exist was not confirmed. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Last Month Rent Receipt
bodyText: If you collect last month's rent in advance, give the tenant a receipt at the time of payment showing the amount, the date received, that it will be applied as rent for the last month, who received it (and for an agent, the landlord's name), and a description of the unit. The receipt must also state that the tenant is entitled to interest on it at five per cent a year or the lesser bank rate, and that the tenant should give you a forwarding address at the end of the tenancy.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(2)(a) ('its intended application as rent for the last month of the tenancy'; 'a statement indicating that the tenant is entitled to interest on said rent payment at the rate of five per cent per year'; 'a statement indicating that the tenant should provide the lessor with a forwarding address'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(4)(b). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Interest on Last Month Rent
bodyText: You owe interest on last month's rent from the first day of the tenancy, at five per cent a year or the lesser rate the bank paid. At the end of each year of the tenancy, give the tenant a statement and either the interest or notice that it may be deducted from the next rent. If you do neither within thirty days, the tenant may deduct it. No interest accrues for the last month. Interest unpaid within thirty days after the tenancy ends exposes you to three times the interest, plus costs and attorney's fees.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(2)(a) ('beginning with the first day of tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year'; 'Interest shall not accrue for the last month for which rent was paid in advance'; 'three times the amount of interest to which the tenant is entitled'). Shutdown use of these funds: see edu-shutdown-last-month-rent-ma. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Conditions on Deposit Refund
bodyText: Massachusetts does not let you make the deposit refund depend on advance notice of move-out, a forwarding address or a tenant demand. You must return the deposit or its balance, with interest, within thirty days after the tenancy ends. A lease condition that conflicts with the deposit law is void, and trying to enforce it forfeits your right to keep any of the deposit. You may ask for a forwarding address, and the last month's rent receipt must tell the tenant to give one.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(4) ('within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(8) ('any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of any provision of this section shall be deemed to be against public policy'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(6)(c); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(2)(a) (forwarding-address statement). No surrender-notice or demand condition: MA battery A deposit-surrender-notice: refund conditioned on surrender notice / forwarding address: 2 hits; positives passed (only § 15B and a prescription program rule). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Deposit After Violence Termination
bodyText: When a tenant or co-tenant ends a tenancy because a household member is a victim of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault or stalking, that tenant must receive a full and specific statement of the basis for keeping any of the security deposit, with any refund due, within 30 days after the tenancy concludes and all occupants have delivered full possession to you. Refund any rent prepaid for the period after the tenant's liability ends, which is 30 days or one full rental period after the quitting date, whichever is later.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 24(c) ('a full and specific statement of the basis for retaining any of the security deposit together with any refund due in compliance with section 15B within 30 days of the conclusion of the tenancy and the delivery of full possession of the leased premises by all occupants'; 'entitled to a refund of any prepaid rent for any period thereafter'; '30 days or 1 full rental period after the quitting date, whichever last occurs'). Other co-tenants are not released (§ 24(d)). How a single deposit is split among remaining co-tenants is not addressed; case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Deposit Processing Fee
bodyText: We searched Massachusetts statutes and regulations and found no expedited deposit procedure. You may return the deposit sooner than thirty days, but you may not deduct an administrative, processing or accounting fee from it. No statute authorizes charging such a fee separately either. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent or water charges, a lawful tax escalation, and documented damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, and no deduction may be made for any other purpose.
notes: MA: Confirmed absent (no expedited procedure). MA battery A expedited-deposit-disposition: early deposit disposition / administrative fee: 0 hits; positives passed (synthetic). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(4) ('No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those set forth in this section'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(8). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Fee in Lieu of Deposit
bodyText: A fee in lieu of a security deposit is allowed only once the state housing office issues regulations authorizing it, and we found none in the state regulations. Until then, do not charge one. Any future program must meet the statute: the fee is optional for both sides; you must offer it to every approved applicant on equal terms; the tenant may choose or switch to a full deposit; any non-refundable part must be disclosed in the lease and acknowledged in writing; and fees plus any deposit may not exceed one month's rent.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(b)(iii) ('may promulgate regulations to authorize a lessor and a tenant or prospective tenant to agree to the payment of a fee in lieu of payment of a security deposit'; 'the lessor shall disclose that the fee is non-refundable in the lease'; 'the sum of fees paid to waive a security deposit and the payment of the security deposit shall not exceed, in total, the amount of 1 month's rent'); added by 2024 Mass. Acts ch. 150, § 50. No implementing regulation: MA battery A fee-in-lieu-of-deposit: fee in lieu of / to waive security deposit: 1 hits; positives passed (only § 15B; full CMR searched). No credit-reporting notice rule for no-deposit leases found. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Money Taken Before the Lease
bodyText: Massachusetts has no holding-deposit statute. Any money you require at or before the start of a tenancy must fit the closed list: first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit up to the first month's rent, and a key and lock cost. A separate holding or reservation fee is not on that list. Money you take early as a security deposit starts the deposit rules right away: give a receipt when you take it, hold it in a separate interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank and give the bank receipt within 30 days, and give the statement of condition when you receive the deposit or within 10 days after the tenancy starts, whichever is later. If an applicant signs a rental application but never signs the lease, you may keep no more than your lawful damages or an agreed damages amount.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(b) ('At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy'); Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(3)(a) ('Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account'); 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(c) ('the failure of a prospective tenant to enter into a written rental agreement after signing a rental application'). No holding-deposit rule: MA battery A holding-deposit: holding deposit / earnest money before lease: 2 hits; positives passed (940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17 and ch. 40T, § 4 only). How 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(c) agreed damages fit with the § 15B(1)(b) list is unsettled; case law not searched. Timing: Mass. Gen.
