Federal satellite-antenna rules not researched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Entry Purposes and Notice
bodyText: Your lease may let you enter only to inspect, make repairs, or show the unit to a prospective tenant, purchaser or mortgagee. You may also enter under a court order, if the unit appears abandoned, or to inspect for deposit damage in the last 30 days of the tenancy or after either side gives notice to end it. For access to bring the unit up to the State Sanitary Code, such as repairs, pest elimination or utility service, give at least 48 hours' notice, except for emergency repairs. No statute sets a notice period for other entries; give reasonable notice.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(a) ('except to inspect the premises, to make repairs thereto or to show the same to a prospective tenant, purchaser, mortgagee or its agents'; 'if the premises appear to have been abandoned by the lessee'; 'within the last thirty days of the tenancy'). 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(e). 105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.003(E) ('An owner shall provide at least 48 hours notice to the occupant, except for emergency repairs for which no notice is required'). title: Refused Access and Wrongful Entry
bodyText: Tenants must give you access, on reasonable notice and by appointment if possible, at reasonable times for code repairs, pest elimination and utility service. A tenant who unreasonably denies access and so prevents necessary repairs cannot use the repair-and-deduct remedy for those conditions. Entering for any purpose the law does not allow is an unfair or deceptive practice. Interfering with a tenant's quiet enjoyment can cost you actual and consequential damages or three months' rent, whichever is greater. No statute treats a repair request as consent to enter.
notes: MA: 105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.003(E) ('upon reasonable notice and if possible by appointment, shall give the owner thereof'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 111, § 127L ('has unreasonably denied the owner access to the dwelling unit and thereby prevented the owner from making necessary repairs'). 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(e) ('Enter a dwelling unit other than'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 14 ('interferes with the quiet enjoyment of any residential premises'; 'actual and consequential damages or three month's rent, whichever is greater'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No No-Notice Service Entry
bodyText: Massachusetts has no rule letting a lease authorize entry without notice for regularly scheduled services. Your lease may reserve entry only to inspect, make repairs or show the unit. Code work, including pest elimination and utility service, needs at least 48 hours' notice to the tenant unless it is an emergency repair. Schedule routine services such as filter changes or pest treatments with notice, and by appointment where you can.

Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(a) ('No lease relating to residential real property shall contain a provision that a lessor may'). 105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.003(E) ('Access shall be at a reasonable time and shall include, but not be limited to, any cooperation required for repairs, alterations, pest elimination, and service of utilities'; 'An owner shall provide at least 48 hours notice to the occupant'). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Abandoned-Property Procedure
bodyText: Massachusetts statutes and regulations give you no procedure for storing or disposing of belongings a tenant leaves after moving out on their own. The only statutory rule covers a tenant who ends a tenancy under the domestic violence law: belongings left behind are deemed abandoned and may be disposed of under applicable law, unless the tenant says in writing who is responsible for them and what to do. You may enter if the unit appears abandoned. Never remove a tenant's belongings to regain possession without a court order.
notes: MA: MA battery MA-C abandoned tenant personal property procedure: 8 hits (self-storage, airport, port, shelter, Devens and unclaimed-property rules, and Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 24); positive passed; control 0. Searched General Laws, Constitution, CMR and court rules. Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 24(d) ('such belongings shall be deemed abandoned and may be disposed of under applicable law, unless the tenant or co-tenant indicates in writing'). Mass. Gen. title: Animal Check After Move-Out
bodyText: Within 3 days after you knew or should have known a unit was vacated, whether by end of the tenancy, abandonment or removal of the tenant, you or your designee must inspect it for abandoned animals. If you find one, immediately notify an animal control officer, a police officer or another authorized agent of the animal's presence and condition. Finding the animal does not make you its owner or keeper. Failing to inspect can bring a civil penalty of up to $500 for a first offense and $1,000 after that.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 30 ('Not more than 3 days after a property owner or a lessor knew or should have known that a property has been vacated through termination of tenancy, abandonment'; 'shall immediately notify an animal control officer'; 'a civil penalty of not more than $500 for a first offense and not more than $1,000 for a second or subsequent offense'). After summary process: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 14 (edu-post-eviction-animals-ma). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Mitigation Statute
bodyText: No Massachusetts statute or regulation sets your duty to re-rent after a tenant leaves early, or says when the lease ends because the tenant abandoned the unit. Whether and how far you must mitigate is a question of case law, which this library has not reviewed. If a lease or tenancy at will ends early by surrender, you may recover rent apportioned to the date it ends. Damages you keep for a tenant's breach may not exceed what the law allows or an amount the parties agreed on.
notes: MA: MA battery MA-C landlord duty to mitigate or relet after abandonment: 8 hits (environmental, energy, assisted-living and comprehensive-permit rules), none on residential leases; synthetic positives passed; control 0. Searched General Laws, Constitution, CMR and court rules. Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 8 ('by surrender, either express or by operation of law'; 'a proportional part of such rent'). 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(c) ('any amount which exceeds the damages to which he is entitled under the law'). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Attorney Fees Run Both Ways
bodyText: If your residential lease lets you recover attorneys' fees and expenses when the tenant breaks the lease, or makes those amounts additional rent, the law reads into the lease your promise to pay the tenant's reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses too. That covers your own breach of the lease and the tenant's successful defense of a case you bring. The tenant may recover them in a suit or as a counterclaim in an eviction. No special wording or cap is prescribed. Any waiver of this rule is void.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 20 ('there shall be implied in such lease a covenant by the landlord to pay to the tenant the reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses'; 'in the successful defense of any action or summary proceeding commenced by the landlord'; 'Any waiver of this section shall be void as against public policy'). MA battery MA-C lease attorney fee provisions any: 5 hits (ch. 93, § 93; ch. 106, § 2A-108; ch. 186, §§ 15C, 15F, 20), no cap or prescribed wording; positive passed; control 0. Collection fees on past-due amounts need express lease authority (edu-collection-fees-ma). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Two Termination Tracks
bodyText: Massachusetts treats unpaid rent differently from other lease violations. For nonpayment, give a written fourteen days' notice to quit. A tenant under a written lease can still keep the tenancy by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, by the answer date; a tenant at will has a 10-day cure if they had no similar notice in the prior 12 months. For other violations, no statute sets a notice or cure period for a written lease, so your lease terms control. A tenancy at will can be ended by the regular notice: three months, or if rent is paid more often, the rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 11 ('fourteen days' notice to quit'; 'on or before the day the answer is due'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12 ('within ten days after the receipt thereof'; 'equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer'). MA battery MA-C notice and cure for non-rent lease breach: 1 hit (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 16, definitions); positive and synthetic passed; control 0. Searched General Laws, Constitution, CMR and court rules. Lodging houses: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 17 (seven days' notice). Forfeiture for non-rent breach: case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Limits on Casualty Clauses
bodyText: Because no Massachusetts statute governs casualty or mitigation, your lease may allocate those risks, within limits. It may not exonerate you from liability for your own negligence or misconduct. It may not waive the tenant's code remedies, such as repair-and-deduct or ending the lease for certified violations, or say that nothing you do counts as a constructive eviction. Service interruptions can be excused only for government restrictions you did not cause, necessary repairs, or natural causes beyond your control.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15 ('arising from any omission, fault, negligence or other misconduct of the lessor or landlord'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 111, § 127L (waiver 'shall be against public policy and void'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15F ('agrees that no action or failure to act by the landlord shall be construed as a constructive eviction'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 14 ('interruptions resulting from natural causes beyond the control of the lessor or landlord'). No casualty or mitigation statute: edu-no-disaster-tenancy-rule-ma, edu-no-mitigation-statute-ma. Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Criminal Use Voids the Lease
bodyText: If a tenant or occupant uses the premises for prostitution, illegal gaming, illegal keeping or sale of alcohol, illegal keeping, sale or manufacture of controlled substances, illegal keeping of a weapon or listed explosives offenses, you may elect to treat the lease as void. You may then bring an eviction or ask the court for an order to vacate, including a preliminary injunction giving you possession with an execution to be levied forthwith. The court must first give the tenant notice and a hearing with the chance to cross-examine witnesses. Public and assisted housing has added rules.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 139, § 19 ('at the election of the lessor or owner, annul and make void the lease'; 'may seek an order requiring the tenant to vacate the premises or may avail himself of the remedy provided in chapter two hundred and thirty-nine'; 'may order issuance of an execution for possession of any such premises to be levied upon forthwith'; 'opportunity for the tenant to confront and cross-examine witnesses'). Sealing of such judgments after 7 years: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 16(e). Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Sober Home Certification
bodyText: Massachusetts has a voluntary training and accreditation program for alcohol and drug free housing, commonly known as sober homes. A home does not need certification to operate or advertise as alcohol and drug free. But state agencies and statewide treatment vendors may refer people only to certified homes. No statute sets special lease terms or eviction rules for these homes, or gives any legal effect to a drug-free lease addendum. Ordinary rules apply, including your right to void a lease when the premises are used to keep or sell illegal drugs.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 17, § 18A ('a voluntary training and accreditation program for operators of alcohol and drug free housing'; 'shall not refer that person to alcohol and drug free housing'; 'Nothing in this section shall prohibit a residence that has not received certification from operating or advertising'). MA battery MA-C drug-free or crime-free lease addendum: 12 hits (sober-home certification, parole, treatment-program and tax rules), none on lease addenda; synthetic positives passed; control 0. Searched General Laws, Constitution, CMR and court rules. Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 139, § 19 ('the illegal keeping, sale or manufacture of controlled substances'). Federal HUD addendum rules not researched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Domestic Violence Proof Documents
bodyText: You may ask for proof of victim status, including the perpetrator's name if known. Any one of three documents is enough: a valid protective order under chapter 209A or 258E; a court or law enforcement record of the act; or a written verification from a qualified third party, such as a police officer, prosecutor, victim-witness advocate, licensed medical or mental health provider, licensed social worker, or sexual assault or domestic violence counselor. A verification names the organization and the date of the act, with the adult victim's statement under penalty of perjury. Keep all proof confidential.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 24(e)-(f) ('shall be satisfied by production of any 1 of the following documents'; 'a copy of a valid protection order under chapter 209A or 258E'; 'a record from a federal, state or local court or law enforcement'; 'a statement, under the penalty of perjury'; 'shall keep such documentation and the information contained in the documentation confidential'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 23 (qualified third party list). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Domestic Violence Lock Change
bodyText: If a tenant, co-tenant or adult household member reasonably believes they face an imminent threat of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault or stalking at the premises, they may ask you to change the unit's locks. Within 2 business days, make a good faith effort to change them or give permission to do so, and give the requester a new key within the same period. You may charge no more than the customary local price. To deny a key to a co-occupant perpetrator you need a protective order or court or police record. Obstructing a lock change can cost three months' rent.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 26(b)-(e), (g) ('within 2 business days, make a good faith effort to change the locks or give the tenant, co-tenant or household member permission to change the locks'; 'The fee shall not exceed the reasonable price customarily charged for changing such locks in that community'; 'may change the locks without the owner's permission'; 'actual and consequential damages or 3 months' rent, whichever is greater'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 27 (comply with a 209A vacate order). Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Domestic Violence Reprisal Protections
bodyText: You may not refuse to rent to an applicant because they ended a tenancy under the domestic violence law or asked for a lock change. In an eviction, it is a defense that you acted in reprisal because a tenant or household member sought a protective order, used the domestic violence lease protections, or reported domestic violence, rape, sexual assault or stalking to police. A notice to quit within six months after that is presumed a reprisal, which you can rebut only by clear and convincing evidence. A good faith action against a remaining tenant is not retaliation.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 25 ('An owner shall not refuse to enter into a rental agreement'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 239, § 2A ('seeking relief under sections 23 to 29, inclusive, of chapter 186'; 'reporting to any police officer or law enforcement professional an incident of domestic violence'; 'may be rebutted only by clear and convincing evidence'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 24(d) ('shall not be subject to a claim of retaliation'). MA battery MA-C housing protections for domestic violence victims v2: 9 hits (ch. 186, §§ 23-24; ch. 239, § 2A; housing-program rules); positives passed; control 0. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Domestic Violence Termination
bodyText: A tenant or co-tenant may end the tenancy by written notice to you that a household member is a victim of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault or stalking. The notice must come within 3 months of the most recent act, or while a household member is reasonably in fear of imminent serious physical harm. They must move out within 3 months of the notice or it is void. Their rent liability ends 30 days or 1 full rental period after the quitting date, whichever is later. Other co-tenants stay bound. No lease can waive this.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 24(a)-(d) ('within 3 months of the most recent act'; 'reasonably in fear of imminent serious physical harm'; 'the notice to terminate the rental agreement or tenancy shall be void'; 'for 30 days or 1 full rental period after the quitting date, whichever last occurs'; 'No other tenant or co-tenant who is a party to the rental agreement shall be released'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 28 ('shall be void and unenforceable'). Domestic violence is limited to acts by family or household members: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 23 ('between family or member of a household'); rape, sexual assault and stalking have no relationship limit. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Early Termination Rights
bodyText: Massachusetts gives a tenant few statutory ways to end a lease early. A tenant may end it on notice when a household member is a victim of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault or stalking. A tenant may treat the lease as ended, pay only fair value, and move out when certified code violations go unrepaired after written notice. Otherwise your lease controls. You may keep an amount the parties agreed as damages for breach, but not more than the law allows, and the security deposit cannot be used for it.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 24(a) ('may terminate a rental agreement or tenancy and quit the premises upon written notification to the owner'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 111, § 127L ('treat the lease or rental agreement as abrogated'). 940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.17(6)(c) ('or an amount which the parties have otherwise agreed as to the amount of the damages'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(4) ('No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those set forth in this section'). Servicemembers: edu-state-scra-extension-ma. Penalty versus liquidated damages: case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: Eminent Domain and Tenants
bodyText: If the property is taken by eminent domain, a tenant using part of it as a home need not leave until four months after written notice of the taking. When a tenant for years and you both suffer damages, the whole award is assessed without splitting and held in trust. The trustee pays you, from the income, the value of the rent the tenant would otherwise have paid, and the balance to the tenant for the rest of the term. No statute says directly whether the tenant's own rent duty ends, so address takings in your lease.
notes: MA: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 79, § 8B ('until four months after notice of such taking has been given him in writing'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 79, § 24 ('entire damages shall be assessed without apportionment thereof'; 'pay to the reversioner or remainderman the value of any annual rent or other payment which would, but for such damages, have been payable by the tenant'). Relocation assistance (ch. 79A) not read. Case law not searched. Rule 15: written section-open.

title: No Environmental-Event Termination
bodyText: Massachusetts gives you no statutory right to end a lease because a sudden environmental or public health event, or a government order, makes occupancy impossible or unlawful. Your lease and general contract law govern. This library offers no clause for it; if you want one, write your own term, and it cannot take away rights a tenant has by law. If the board of health condemns the unit, you must provide a non-owner occupant comparable, suitable housing for the period the code sets. A tenancy at will can still be ended by ordinary written notice.

Code Regs. 10.00, manufactured housing), none giving a residential landlord this right; synthetic positive passed; control 0. Searched General Laws, Constitution, CMR and court rules. 105 Mass. Code Regs. 410.900(E) ('the owner shall provide comparable, suitable housing for the occupant'). Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12. Case law (impossibility, frustration) not searched. title: No Infirmity Termination Right
bodyText: Massachusetts statutes and regulations do not let a tenant end a lease early because they must move to a nursing home, assisted living or other care facility, or because of a tenant's death. Your lease decides. This library offers no early-release clause for these events; if you want one, add your own term. If a tenancy ends early by surrender or by death, rent is apportioned to the date it ends. Disability laws may still require a reasonable accommodation, such as an early release, in some cases; that question is not settled here.

Code Regs. 67.00, emergency assistance eligibility, off point); synthetic positives passed; control 0. Searched General Laws, Constitution, CMR and court rules. Mass. Gen. title: Lease Guaranties
bodyText: Massachusetts has no statute specific to lease guaranties. A guarantor's promise to answer for the tenant's debt must be in writing and signed by the guarantor or someone they authorized. No statute limits a guarantor to the original term, so whether a guaranty covers renewals or a later tenancy at will depends on its wording. State clearly whether the guaranty continues through renewals, extensions and holdover.

Laws ch. 259, § 1 ('upon a special promise to answer for the debt, default or misdoings of another'; 'is in writing and signed by the party to be charged therewith'). Mass. Gen.
